```python
column = _normalize_identifier(match.group("column"))
operator = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", match.group("operator").strip().upper())   # "not like" ⇒ "NOT LIKE"
value = match.group("value").strip()
qualifier = _normalize_identifier(match.group("qualifier") or "")
if not column or not value: continue
if column.lower() == "1" or value == "1": continue        # drops "1 = 1" style tautologies
entity = aliases.get(qualifier.lower(), "") if qualifier else single_table
if qualifier and not entity: entity = qualifier           # unknown alias ⇒ alias used as entity
key = (entity.lower(), column.lower())
if key in seen: continue                                  # first occurrence wins
filters.append(ActiveFilter(entity=entity, attribute=column, operator=operator,
                            value=value, origin_turn=turn_index, source="sql"))
if len(filters) >= MaxActiveFilters: break                # MaxActiveFilters = 12
```

Inputs: `request.existing_code` first; if that yields **no** filters and a previous session context exists,
the extraction is retried on `previous.last_sql` (`session_context.py:278-281`). Output: `List[ActiveFilter]`
with `source="sql"`, `origin_turn=turn_index`, capped at `MaxActiveFilters = 12` (`:55`).

Worked example (from `tests/unit/test_session_filters.py:15-44`) — for

```sql
SELECT p.ProductName, SUM(od.Quantity) AS Qty
FROM dbo.Orders o
JOIN dbo.[Order Details] od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
JOIN dbo.Products p ON od.ProductID = p.ProductID
WHERE p.ProductName LIKE '%chocolate%' AND o.OrderDate >= '1997-01-01'
GROUP BY p.ProductName
```

the extracted set is exactly:

| entity | attribute | operator | value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Products` | `ProductName` | `LIKE` | `'%chocolate%'` |
| `Orders` | `OrderDate` | `>=` | `'1997-01-01'` |

with **no** `OrderID` filter (join predicate) and alias resolution `p → Products`, `o → Orders`.

`ActiveFilter` helpers (`app/models/pipeline.py:33-70`, `:121-129`):

```python
def render(self):        return f"{self.attribute} {self.operator} {self.value}".strip()
def phrase(self):
    raw = self.value.strip()
    is_quoted = raw.startswith("'") or raw[:2].lower() == "n'"
    if not is_quoted or self.operator.upper() not in {"=", "LIKE"}: return ""     # dates/numbers: no phrase
    value = raw.strip("'\"").strip("%").strip()
    entity = (self.entity or self._entity_from_attribute()).strip()
    return f"{value} {_pluralize(entity)}" if (entity and value) else (value or entity)
def value_token(self):   return self.value.strip("'\"").strip("%").strip().lower()

def _pluralize(word):
    if word.lower().endswith(("s", "x", "ch", "sh")): return word
    if word.lower().endswith("y") and len(word) > 1:  return word[:-1] + "ies"
    return word + "s"
```

`_entity_from_attribute()` (used only when `entity` is empty) strips a trailing
`Name` / `ID` / `Id` / `Code` / `Title` / `Date` when something remains before it.
So `ProductName` + `'%chocolate%'` ⇒ `phrase() == "chocolate Products"`, while
`OrderDate >= '1997-01-01'` ⇒ `phrase() == ""` (never folded into a sentence).

### 5.7 Filter lifecycle — inheritance, clear, replacement

`apply_filter_lifecycle(filters, query, turn_index) -> (filters, cleared, replaced, notes)`
(`session_context.py:211-246`).

**Step 1 — clear/negation.** If `detect_filter_clear(query)` is true the whole list is dropped:

```python
if detect_filter_clear(query):
    held = list(filters)
    if held: notes.append("Active filters cleared by explicit user negation")
    return [], bool(held), False, notes
```

`detect_filter_clear` (`scenario.py:174-177`) is `detect_reset(text) or any(FILTER_CLEAR_PATTERNS)`.
Full phrase lists (verbatim regexes):

`RESET_PATTERNS` (`scenario.py:26-37`) — also clears filters via `detect_filter_clear`:

| # | Regex |
|---|---|
| 1 | `\bstart\s+over\b` |
| 2 | `\bstart\s+from\s+scratch\b` |
| 3 | `\bnew\s+query\b` |
| 4 | `\bbrand\s+new\s+query\b` |
| 5 | `\breset\s+(the\s+)?(query|context)\b` |
| 6 | `\bforget\s+(the\s+)?(previous|prior|earlier|last)\b` |
| 7 | `\bignore\s+(the\s+)?(previous|prior|earlier|last)\b` |
| 8 | `\bscratch\s+that\b` |
| 9 | `\bnever\s+mind\b` |
| 10 | `\bcompletely\s+different\b` |

`FILTER_CLEAR_PATTERNS` (`scenario.py:40-48`):

| # | Regex |
|---|---|
| 1 | `\bclear\s+(all\s+)?filters?\b` |
| 2 | `\breset\s+(the\s+)?filters?\b` |
| 3 | `\b(remove\|drop\|delete)\s+(the\s+\|all\s+)?filters?\b` (literal alternation `(remove|drop|delete)`) |
| 4 | `\b(no\|without\s+any\|remove\s+all)\s+filters?\b` |
| 5 | `\bignore\s+(the\s+)?filters?\b` |
| 6 | `\bunfiltered\b` |
| 7 | `\bfor\s+(all\|every)\b` |

**Step 2 — replacement.** `_REPLACEMENT_PATTERNS` (`session_context.py:69-78`), searched in order; the first
pattern with a match whose captured value is non-empty and not a stop-word wins:

| # | Regex |
|---|---|
| 1 | `\b(?:now\s+)?(?:do\|show\|run\|make\|give)\s+(?:this\|it\|that)\s+for\s+(?P<value>[A-Za-z][\w\-]*)` |
| 2 | `\binstead\s+(?:of\s+\w+\s+)?(?:use\|do\|show\|for)\s+(?P<value>[A-Za-z][\w\-]*)` |
| 3 | `\bswitch\s+(?:it\s+)?to\s+(?P<value>[A-Za-z][\w\-]*)` |
| 4 | `\bchange\s+(?:it\s+)?to\s+(?P<value>[A-Za-z][\w\-]*)` |
| 5 | `\bfor\s+(?P<value>[A-Za-z][\w\-]*)\s+instead\b` |

`_REPLACEMENT_STOPWORDS = {"all", "every", "the", "a", "an", "me", "them", "this", "that", "now", "instead"}`
(`:80`) — a match whose value is a stop-word is skipped and the next pattern is tried. Example:
`"now do this for coffee"` ⇒ value `coffee`; `"for all products"` is caught by the clear rule first.

For every filter whose operator (lower-cased) is in `_VALUE_OPERATORS = {"=", "like", "<>", "!="}` the value
is re-quoted and the filter is re-stamped `origin_turn=turn_index, source="session"`; all other filters pass
through untouched:

```python
def _requote(template, value):
    stripped = template.strip()
    if stripped.lower().startswith("n'"):
        return f"N'%{value}%'" if "%" in stripped else f"N'{value}'"
    if stripped.startswith("'") and stripped.endswith("'"):
        return f"'%{value}%'" if "%" in stripped else f"'{value}'"
    return value                      # unquoted → bare token
```

The `%` presence of the **original** template decides wildcards: `'%chocolate%'` + `coffee` ⇒ `'%coffee%'`;
`'chocolate'` + `coffee` ⇒ `'coffee'`. Note `LIKE` is re-quoted like `=`; `NOT LIKE` (operator string
`NOT LIKE`) is **not** in `_VALUE_OPERATORS`, so a negation filter is left alone. If at least one filter was
replaced the function returns `replaced=True` and the note `Filter value replaced with '{replacement}'`;
otherwise the input list is returned unchanged (`cleared=False, replaced=False`).

Lifecycle summary:

| Rule | Trigger | Effect on filter list |
|---|---|---|
| Inheritance | default | every stored filter carries forward (`merge_filters`) |
| Clear | `detect_filter_clear(query)` | `[]` (and `filters_cleared=True` on the result) |
| Replacement | `_replacement_value(query)` matched | value-like (`=`, `LIKE`, `<>`, `!=`) filter values rewritten; structure/attributes kept; `replacement_applied=True` |

### 5.8 Conversational context — one turn end to end

`prepare_conversation_context(request, llm=None, store=None)` (`session_context.py:266-324`):

```python
store = store or _session_store
key = session_key(request)
previous = store.get(key) if key else None
turn_index = (previous.turn_index + 1) if previous else 1

filters = list(previous.active_filters) if previous else []
sql_filters = extract_filters_from_sql(request.existing_code, turn_index)
if not sql_filters and previous and previous.last_sql:
    sql_filters = extract_filters_from_sql(previous.last_sql, turn_index)
filters = merge_filters(filters, sql_filters)                     # editor SQL wins on (entity, attribute)

filters, cleared, replaced, notes = apply_filter_lifecycle(filters, request.query, turn_index)

preflight = classify_scenario(request.query, bool(request.existing_code), allow_llm=False)
skip_coreference = bool(request.existing_code) and preflight.scenario == GenerationMode.OPTIMIZATION

if skip_coreference:
    coref = ConversationContextResult(original_query=request.query, rewritten_query=request.query,
                                      active_filters=list(filters), notes=notes, source="skipped_optimization")
else:
    coref = resolve_coreference(request.query, conversation_history=request.conversation_history,
                                active_filters=filters, llm=llm, turn_index=turn_index)
    coref.active_filters = merge_filters(filters, coref.carried_filters)   # LLM-carried filters win
    coref.notes = notes + coref.notes
coref.filters_cleared = cleared
coref.replacement_applied = replaced
coref.session_id = key

if key:
    store.put(SessionSemanticContext(
        session_id=key, source_id=request.source_id,
        active_filters=coref.active_filters,
        active_domains=list(previous.active_domains) if previous else [],
        target_grain=previous.target_grain if previous else None,
        turn_index=turn_index,
        last_sql=request.existing_code or (previous.last_sql if previous else None),
    ))
return coref
```

Merge precedence (`merge_filters`, `coreference.py:262-278`): iterate `inherited + discovered`; the key is
`(entity.lower(), attribute.lower())`; a later entry with the same key **replaces** the earlier one in place,
otherwise it is appended. Keys include the entity, so an LLM-carried filter with an empty `entity` does
**not** collide with the inherited `Products.ProductName` entry — both survive. Preserve that behaviour.

`apply_conversation_context(context, result)` (`session_context.py:327-336`) is the bridge back onto the
context used by routing and prompts:

```python
context.session_id      = result.session_id
context.rewritten_query = result.rewritten_query
context.coreference_notes = list(result.notes)
context.active_filters  = list(result.active_filters)
context.filter_state_text = result.filter_state_text()          # "- attr op value" lines, or "(none)"
if result.was_rewritten and result.rewritten_query:
    context.combined_query = fold_conversation(result.rewritten_query, context.request.conversation_history)
```

`ConversationContextResult.filter_state_text()` (`app/models/pipeline.py:100-103`):

```python
if not self.active_filters: return "(none)"
return "\n".join(f"- {f.render()}" for f in self.active_filters)
```

`AgentContext.effective_query` (`app/models/pipeline.py:162-164`): `self.rewritten_query or self.request.query`
— after `apply_conversation_context` this is the rewritten query whenever a rewrite happened, and otherwise
the original. `route()` classifies on `effective_query`; `apply_conversation_context` runs **before**
`route()` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:102-109`).

### 5.9 Coreference rewrite — when it fires

`needs_coreference(query, active_filters, has_history)` (`coreference.py:83-101`), evaluated in order:

| # | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | empty/whitespace query | `False` |
| 2 | `_SQL_SHAPED = \b(select\|from\|where\|join\|group\s+by\|order\s+by)\b` (IGNORECASE) matches | `False` |
| 3 | `extract_qualified_object_names(text, 1)` non-empty (a `schema.object` mention) | `False` |
| 4 | `is_vague_followup(text)` | `True` |
| 5 | `len(text.split()) <= 8` **and** `_ANAPHORIC` matches **and** (`active_filters` or `has_history`) | `True`, unless a `value_token()` of some active filter is a substring of the lower-cased text ⇒ `False` |
| 6 | otherwise | `False` |

```python
ANAPHORIC = r"\b(it|its|this|that|these|those|them|they|their|same|again|more|also|too|instead|previous|earlier|above)\b"
VAGUE_QUERY_MAX_WORDS = 8
MAX_TURNS_FOR_REWRITE = 3
MAX_REWRITE_CHARS = 400
```

`is_vague_followup(text)` (`coreference.py:74-80`): `False` when empty or `len(text.split()) > 8`; otherwise
`any(pattern.search(text))` over `VAGUE_FOLLOWUP_PATTERNS` (`coreference.py:31-46`, IGNORECASE) — verbatim:

| # | Pattern |
|---|---|
| 1 | `^\s*(all\|the\|show\|give\|list\|get)\b[^.]{0,30}\bdetails?\b` |
| 2 | `\b(all\|full\|complete\|entire)\s+(the\s+)?(\w+\s+){0,2}details?\b` |
| 3 | `\b(need\|want\|show\|give\|list\|get\|see)\b[^.]{0,30}\bdetails?\b` |
| 4 | `\bmore\s+detail(s)?\b` |
| 5 | `\b(and\|then)\s+(the\s+)?(details?\|rest\|others?\|same)\b` |
| 6 | `\bwhat\s+about\b` |
| 7 | `\bhow\s+about\b` |
| 8 | `\bbreak\s*(this\|it\|that)\s*down\b` |
| 9 | `\bdrill\s*(down\|into)\b` |
| 10 | `\bline\s+items?\b` |
| 11 | `\bexpand\b` |
| 12 | `\bgo\s+deeper\b` |
| 13 | `^\s*(and\|also\|plus\|now)\b` |
| 14 | `^\s*(it\|this\|that\|those\|these\|them)\b` |

`resolve_coreference(raw_query, conversation_history, active_filters, llm, turn_index)`
(`coreference.py:104-129`):

```python
query = raw_query.strip(); history = list(...); filters = list(...)
result = ConversationContextResult(original_query=query, rewritten_query=query,
                                   active_filters=list(filters), carried_filters=[])
if not query or not needs_coreference(query, filters, bool(history)): return result   # no rewrite
if llm is not None:
    llm_result = _llm_rewrite(query, history, filters, llm, turn_index)
    if llm_result is not None: return llm_result          # LLM path succeeds
return _deterministic_rewrite(query, filters, result)     # fallback (or no-op)
```

#### 5.9.1 LLM rewrite contract

Messages (`coreference.py:132-168`). System prompt verbatim:

```
You rewrite a short follow-up message into a standalone database question by resolving pronouns and elided context from the conversation so far and the active filters.
Rules:
1. Keep the user's language and intent. Never invent subjects, metrics or filters that are not present in the conversation or the active filters.
2. Keep every active filter unless the user explicitly removes, replaces or negates it.
3. Return JSON only: {"rewritten_query": string, "carried_filters": [{"entity": string, "attribute": string, "operator": string, "value": string}], "changed": boolean}.
4. If the message is already self-contained, return it unchanged with "changed": false.
```

(The literal source is one Python string with `\n` separators; reproduce the text exactly.)

User message construction:

```python
safe_query = prepare_user_query_for_llm(query)                 # sanitize_for_llm_prompt(max_length=500, allow_newlines=False)
recent = history[-MAX_TURNS_FOR_REWRITE:]                       # last ≤ 3 turns
history_lines = []
for turn in recent:
    question = (turn.question or "").strip()
    answer   = (turn.answer or "").strip().replace("\n", " ")[:200]
    if question: history_lines.append(f"- Q: {question}")
    if answer:   history_lines.append(f"  A: {answer}")
history_text = sanitize_conversation_history(history_lines, max_messages=6) if history_lines else "(none)"
filter_text = "\n".join(f"- {f.entity + '.' if f.entity else ''}{f.attribute} {f.operator} {f.value}" for f in filters) or "(none)"

user = (f"CONVERSATION SO FAR (oldest first):\n{history_text}\n\n"
        f"ACTIVE FILTERS (carry forward unless explicitly removed):\n{filter_text}\n\n"
        f"CURRENT TURN (turn {turn_index}):\n{safe_query}")
```

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Call | `llm.complete_json([system, user], max_tokens=256)` |
| Turn window | last 3 turns |
| Per-answer truncation | 200 chars, newlines → spaces |
| History sanitisation | `sanitize_conversation_history(lines, max_messages=6)` — keeps the last 6 lines, each run through `sanitize_for_llm_prompt(max_length=500, allow_newlines=True)` (escapes `"`→`\"` and `'`→`\'`, strips control chars, rewrites the injection patterns `ignore\s+(previous|all)\s+instructions`, `disregard\s+(previous|all)\s+instructions`, `system\s*:`, `<\s*system\s*>`, `\[INST\]`, `<\|im_start\|>` to `[removed]`), total cap 5000 chars, each line prefixed `- ` (`app/utils/sanitization.py:132-169`) |
| Filter rendering | `- {entity}.{attribute} {operator} {value}`, entity omitted when empty |
| Exceptions | any exception from `complete_json` ⇒ `None` ⇒ deterministic fallback |
| Non-dict response | `None` ⇒ deterministic fallback |

Validation and result construction (`coreference.py:171-188`, `:191-199`, `:202-223`):

```python
rewritten = str(data.get("rewritten_query") or "").strip()
if not _valid_rewrite(query, rewritten): return None

def _valid_rewrite(original, rewritten):
    if not rewritten or rewritten == original:                       return False   # must differ
    if len(rewritten) > MAX_REWRITE_CHARS:                            return False   # ≤ 400 chars
    if len(rewritten) < max(8, int(len(original) * 0.5)):             return False   # ≥ 50 % of original (min 8)
    return True

carried = _parse_carried_filters(data.get("carried_filters"), turn_index)
merged  = merge_filters(filters, carried)
changed = bool(data.get("changed")) or rewritten != query
return ConversationContextResult(original_query=query, rewritten_query=rewritten,
        was_rewritten=changed, carried_filters=carried, active_filters=merged,
        notes=[f'Coreference rewrite: "{query}" -> "{rewritten}"'], source="llm")
```

`_parse_carried_filters` (`:202-223`): non-list ⇒ `[]`; non-dict items skipped; `attribute` **and** `value`
are required (both string-coerced and stripped); `entity` defaults `""`; `operator` defaults `"="` when empty;
`origin_turn = int(item.get("origin_turn") or turn_index)`; `source="llm"`. A malformed `origin_turn` raises
`ValueError` and is **not** caught here — it propagates out of `resolve_coreference`.

#### 5.9.2 Deterministic fallback

`_deterministic_rewrite(query, filters, result)` (`coreference.py:226-259`):

```python
phrases = []; seen = set(); lowered_query = query.lower()
for f in filters:
    phrase = f.phrase(); key = phrase.lower()
    if not phrase or key in seen:                 continue
    if key and key in lowered_query:              continue     # phrase already in the sentence
    token = f.value_token()
    if token and token in lowered_query:          continue     # user restated the value ("for coffee")
    seen.add(key); phrases.append(phrase)
if not phrases: return result                                  # ← no rewrite at all
base = query.rstrip()
if base.endswith((".", "?", "!")): base = base[:-1]
rewritten = f"{base} for {' and '.join(phrases)}"
if len(rewritten) > MAX_REWRITE_CHARS: return result           # > 400 chars ⇒ abandon
result.rewritten_query = rewritten; result.was_rewritten = True
result.notes.append(f'Deterministic filter carry-forward: "{query}" -> "{rewritten}"')
return result
```

`source` stays `"deterministic"` (the `ConversationContextResult` default,
`app/models/pipeline.py:98`). Which filters fold into the sentence:

| Filter shape | `phrase()` | Folded? |
|---|---|---|
| `ProductName LIKE '%chocolate%'` | `chocolate Products` | **yes** |
| `ProductName = 'Chocolate'` | `Chocolate Products` | **yes** (N-prefixed too) |
| `OrderDate >= '1997-01-01'` | `""` (operator not `=`/`LIKE`) | no |
| `Quantity > 10` | `""` (value not quoted) | no |
| `CustomerID = 5` (bare numeric value) | `""` | no — `phrase()` requires the raw value to start with `'` or `N'` |
| `CustomerName = 'Acme'` with `entity=""` | `Acme Customers` | yes — the noun is recovered from the attribute suffix (`…Name` → `Customer` → `Customers`) |

> The rule to be careful with: `phrase()` returns `""` unless the raw value starts with `'` or `N'`; the
> `_entity_from_attribute()` fallback only supplies the **noun** (and only when `entity` is empty), never
> the value.

Worked examples (parity contract, `tests/unit/test_coreference_resolution.py:61-123`):

| Turn (editor SQL filters `ProductName LIKE '%chocolate%'`) | Result |
|---|---|
| `I need all order details` | `I need all order details for chocolate Products`, `source="deterministic"` |
| `now do this for coffee` with a replaced filter `'%coffee%'` | unchanged (the value token `coffee` is already in the sentence); count of `coffee` == 1 |
| `I need all order details` + a `OrderDate >= '1997-01-01'` filter | `… for chocolate Products`; `1997-01-01` absent from the sentence, still present in `active_filters` |
| `SELECT * FROM dbo.Orders` | untouched (SQL-shaped) |
| `show total revenue by country` (9 words, no anaphora) | untouched |
| `I need all order details` with no history **and** no active filters | untouched |

#### 5.9.3 What is **not** rewritten, and the exact phrase lists

* A **directed optimization edit** is never rewritten. The gate is evaluated in
  `prepare_conversation_context` *before* the coreference call (`session_context.py:287-296`):

  ```python
  preflight = classify_scenario(request.query, bool(request.existing_code), allow_llm=False)
  skip_coreference = bool(request.existing_code) and preflight.scenario == GenerationMode.OPTIMIZATION
  ```

  When it fires, the result is built directly with `rewritten_query == request.query`,
  `source == "skipped_optimization"`, and `notes == lifecycle notes` only. Note the preflight passes **no**
  `error_message`, so an error-repair turn is never classified `debugging` here; it only skips rewriting when
  the deterministic optimization patterns match.
* The optimization phrase list that can trigger `skipped_optimization` is
  `OPTIMIZATION_PATTERNS` (`scenario.py:89-121`, IGNORECASE) — a turn that matches one of these while
  `existing_code` is present is treated as directed at the editor SQL, not at the sentence:

| # | Regex |
|---|---|
| 1 | `\bmake\s+(it\|this)\s+(faster\|quicker\|more\s+efficient\|perform)\b` |
| 2 | `\b(optimi[sz]e\|tune\|speed\s+up\|improve)\b.*\b(performance\|query\|it\|this\|sql)\b` |
| 3 | `\bperformance\b` |
| 4 | `\bmore\s+efficient\b` |
| 5 | `\bsargable\b` |
| 6 | `\b(execution\|query)\s+plan\b` |
| 7 | `\badd\s+(an?\s+)?(index\|indexes\|indices\|indexing\|hint\|optimizer\s+hint)\b` |
| 8 | `\b(create\|add)\s+(an?\s+)?nonclustered\s+index\b` |
| 9 | `\bformat(ted\|ting)?\b` |
| 10 | `\bbeautify\b` |
| 11 | `\bpretty\s?print\b` |
| 12 | `\bindent(ation)?\b` |
| 13 | `\bclean\s+up\s+(the\s+)?(sql\|query\|code\|formatting)\b` |
| 14 | `\brefactor\b` |
| 15 | `\brewrite\s+(this\|it)\s+(for\s+)?(readability\|clarity\|style\|performance)\b` |
| 16 | `\bconvert\s+(this\|it\|the\s+query)?\s*to\s+(a\s+)?(cte\|common\s+table\s+expression\|with\s+clause)\b` |
| 17 | `\buse\s+(a\s+)?cte\b` |
| 18 | `\bwrap\s+(this\|it)\s+in\s+(a\s+)?cte\b` |
| 19 | `\b(remove\|drop\|delete)\s+(the\s+)?(unused\|redundant\|extra)\s+(joins?\|columns?\|ctes?\|subquer(y\|ies))\b` |
| 20 | `\b(remove\|drop)\s+(the\s+)?(unused\|redundant)\s+joins?\b` |
| 21 | `\bparameteri[sz]e\b` |
| 22 | `\badd\s+(some\s+)?comments?\b` |
| 23 | `\bcomment\s+(the\s+)?(sql\|query\|code)\b` |
| 24 | `\brenam(e\|ing)\s+(the\s+)?alias(es)?\b` |
| 25 | `\badd\s+(an?\s+)?alias(es)?\b` |
| 26 | `\buppercase\b` |
| 27 | `\blowercase\b` |
| 28 | `\btrailing\s+semicolon\b` |
| 29 | `\bsyntax\b` |
| 30 | `\bdialect\b` |
| 31 | `\bfix\s+(the\s+)?formatting\b` |

* Independently of the skip gate, coreference also declines when the turn is SQL-shaped, mentions a
  `schema.object`, or is not short/vague (§5.9 steps 1-6).

### 5.10 Injection of the resolved context into prompts

`_scenario_section(context)` (`app/core/orchestrator/prompts.py:45-52`) is what every system prompt renders:

```python
rules = scenario_rules(context)
parts = [f"GENERATION MODE\n{context.generation_mode.value}"]
if rules:
    parts.append(rules)
if context.filter_state_text and context.filter_state_text != "(none)":
    parts.append(_filter_block(context))
return "\n\n".join(parts)
```

`_filter_block` (`prompts.py:37-42`):

```python
lines = context.filter_state_text or "(none)"
blocks = [f"ACTIVE SESSION FILTERS (inherited from preceding turns)\n{lines}"]
if context.filter_state_text and context.filter_state_text != "(none)":
    blocks.append(SCOPE_GUARD)
return "\n\n".join(blocks)
```

`SCOPE_GUARD` verbatim (`prompts.py:23-24`):

```
### SCOPE GUARD
Preserve all active filters from preceding turns unless the user explicitly requests their removal.
```

`scenario_rules(context)` (`prompts.py:27-34`):

| `generation_mode` | Injected block |
|---|---|
| `optimization` | `OPTIMIZATION_INSTRUCTIONS` |
| `refinement`, `drill_down` | `REFINEMENT_INSTRUCTIONS` |
| `fresh_start`, `debugging` | `""` (nothing) |

`OPTIMIZATION_INSTRUCTIONS` verbatim (`prompts.py:11-15`):

```
### OPTIMIZATION INSTRUCTIONS
You MUST work exclusively from the SQL shown below. Do NOT consult any catalog, schema, or knowledge base.
Do NOT invent, add, or remove tables or columns that are not already present in the provided SQL.
Preserve every filter, join, entity and the output grain exactly as written.
Change only syntax, structure, formatting or performance characteristics.
```

`REFINEMENT_INSTRUCTIONS` verbatim (`prompts.py:18-21`):

```
### REFINEMENT INSTRUCTIONS
1. Base Context: Build upon the query logic, filters, and entities established in the editor SQL and conversation history.
2. Scope Expansion: If the user requests deeper granularity (e.g., transaction-level line items vs. summary views), you are authorized to query base tables and establish appropriate foreign key joins.
3. Filter Preservation: Ensure established domain filters (e.g., specific products, categories, or date ranges) are maintained in the new query structure.
```

Where the filter block actually appears:

| Prompt builder | Contains `ACTIVE SESSION FILTERS` + `SCOPE GUARD`? |
|---|---|
| `build_system_prompt` (SQL) | **yes**, via `_scenario_section(context)` (`prompts.py:87`) |
| `build_system_prompt(..., semantic=True)` | **yes**, appended after `GENERATION MODE` (`prompts.py:64-67`) |
| `build_python_system_prompt` / `build_r_system_prompt` / `build_sas_system_prompt` | **yes**, via `_scenario_section` (`prompts.py:238, 349, 456`) |
| `build_refinement_system_prompt` | **yes** (it delegates to `build_system_prompt`) |
| `build_optimization_system_prompt` (no-discovery path) | **no** — it renders `scenario_rules(context) or OPTIMIZATION_INSTRUCTIONS` and `EDITOR SQL`, never `_filter_block` (`prompts.py:139-152`) |

`filter_state_text` is set **only** by `apply_conversation_context`; the empty default means
`SCOPE GUARD` appears only when the session actually holds filters. Parity test:
`tests/unit/test_scenario_prompts.py:77-81`.

### 5.11 Write-back — `record_generation_outcome`

`session_context.py:339-358`. Called from the KB-exact path (`builtin_sql_generator.py:197`),
the precomputed-exact path (`:225`), the KB-vector path (`:243`) and after the attempt loop
(`:305`, with `result.sql if result.success else None`).

```python
store = store or _session_store
key = context.session_id                       # namespaced key set by apply_conversation_context
if not key: return                             # no session ⇒ nothing persisted
current = store.get(key) or SessionSemanticContext(session_id=key, source_id=context.request.source_id)
generated = extract_filters_from_sql(sql, current.turn_index) if sql else []
current.active_filters = merge_filters(current.active_filters, generated)   # generated wins per (entity, attribute)
current.last_sql = sql or current.last_sql
if target_grain: current.target_grain = target_grain                        # never passed by the orchestrator
if context.request.source_id: current.source_id = context.request.source_id
store.put(current)
```

Effects: the generated SQL's literal predicates become part of the session (with
`origin_turn = current.turn_index`, i.e. the turn that produced them) and `last_sql` becomes the newly
generated SQL, so the next turn can inherit filters even when the client stops sending `existing_code`.
Parity test: `tests/unit/test_session_filters.py:113-130`.

### 5.12 Scenario classification (Stage A, called from `route` and from the coreference preflight)

`GenerationMode` (`app/core/branch_taxonomy.py:46-57`):
`fresh_start`, `optimization`, `refinement`, `drill_down`, `debugging`.
`REFINEMENT_SCENARIOS = (REFINEMENT, DRILL_DOWN)` and `is_refinement_scenario(mode)` accepts enum or string
(`:57-64`). `ScenarioDecision` (`app/models/pipeline.py:106-118`) carries `scenario`, `confidence`,
`signals[]`, `source` (`deterministic` | `llm` | `default`) and the `is_refinement` property.

`classify_scenario(query, has_existing_code, error_message=None, llm=None, allow_llm=True)`
(`scenario.py:180-268`) — full ordered decision table:

| # | Precondition (evaluated in this order) | `scenario` | `confidence` | `signals` | `source` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `error_message` **and** `has_existing_code` | `debugging` | `1.0` | `["error_message"]` | `deterministic` |
| 2 | `not has_existing_code` | `fresh_start` | `1.0` | `["no_existing_code"]` | `deterministic` |
| 3 | `RESET_PATTERNS` match | `fresh_start` | `0.95` | matched groups (deduped, order of the pattern list) | `deterministic` |
| 4 | `DRILL_DOWN_PATTERNS` match | `drill_down` | `0.9` | matched groups | `deterministic` |
| 5 | (`REFINEMENT_PATTERNS` + `FILTER_CLEAR_PATTERNS` if `detect_filter_clear`) non-empty **and** `_STRUCTURAL_ADDITION` does **not** match | `refinement` | `0.85` if `OPTIMIZATION_PATTERNS` also matched else `0.9` | `refine + optimize` | `deterministic` |
| 6 | `_STRUCTURAL_ADDITION` matches | `optimization` | `0.85` | `[structural match] + optimize` | `deterministic` |
| 7 | `OPTIMIZATION_PATTERNS` match | `optimization` | `0.9` | optimize matches | `deterministic` |
| 8 | `allow_llm` and `llm is not None` and `len(text.split()) <= 12` and the LLM returns a recognizable label | label | `0.7` | `[f"llm:{label}"]` | `llm` |
| 9 | fallback | `optimization` | `0.5` | `[]` | `default` |

Precedence motto from the module docstring (`scenario.py:13`): **explicit reset > drill-down > refinement >
optimization > default**.

Signal matching (`_matches`, `scenario.py:158-166`): each regex is `re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)` and is
searched with `.search()`; the **matched text** (`match.group(0).strip()`) is recorded, de-duplicated
case-insensitively, in pattern order. `_note` in the router truncates display to the first 4 signals.

`DRILL_DOWN_PATTERNS` (`scenario.py:50-63`) — verbatim:

| # | Regex |
|---|---|
| 1 | `\bdrill\s*(down\|into\|through)\b` |
| 2 | `\bbreak\s*(this\|it\|that\|them)?\s*down\b` |
| 3 | `\bbreakdown\s+by\b` |
| 4 | `\bbreak\s+it\s+out\b` |
| 5 | `\bgroup(ed)?\s+by\s+\w+` |
| 6 | `\bsplit\s+(this\|it\|them)?\s*(out\s+)?by\b` |
| 7 | `\bsegment(ed)?\s+by\b` |
| 8 | `\bcategoriz(e\|ed)\s+by\b` |
| 9 | `\bfor\s+each\s+\w+` |
| 10 | `\bper\s+(customer\|product\|category\|region\|country\|employee\|order\|month\|quarter\|year\|day\|week\|supplier\|shipper\|territory\|store)\b` |
| 11 | `\bshow\s+(me\s+)?(the\s+)?\w+\s+by\s+\w+` |
| 12 | `\bsummar(y\|ize\|ise)\s+(this\|it)\s+by\b` |

`REFINEMENT_PATTERNS` (`scenario.py:66-86`) — verbatim:

| # | Regex |
|---|---|
| 1 | `\ball\s+(the\s+)?(order\s+)?details?\b` |
| 2 | `\b(full\|complete\|entire)\s+(order\s+)?details?\b` |
| 3 | `\bline\s+items?\b` |
| 4 | `\btransaction[\s-]level\b` |
| 5 | `\b(detail\|row)[\s-]level\b` |
| 6 | `\bexpand\s+(this\|it\|the\s+query)\b` |
| 7 | `\bgo\s+deeper\b` |
| 8 | `\bmore\s+detail(s)?\b` |
| 9 | `\b(add\|include\|append\|bring\s+in\|pull\s+in\|also\s+show\|show\s+also\|as\s+well\s+as)\b` |
| 10 | `\b(exclude\|drop\|remove)\s+(the\s+)?\w*\s*(date\|name\|amount\|quantity\|column\|field\|attribute\|dimension)\b` |
| 11 | `\bchange\s+the\s+grain\b` |
| 12 | `\bnow\s+(do\|show\|run)\s+(this\|it)\s+for\b` |
| 13 | `\binstead\s+(use\|do\|show\|for)\b` |
| 14 | `\b(show\|give\|do\|run\|use\|switch\|try)\b[^.]{0,25}\binstead\b` |
| 15 | `\b(change\|switch)\s+(it\|this\|that)?\s*(to\|into)\b` |
| 16 | `\b(same\|again)\s+(but\s+)?by\s+\w+` |
| 17 | `\bswitch\s+(it\s+)?to\s+\w+\s+instead\b` |
| 18 | `\bwhat\s+about\s+\w+` |
| 19 | `\bhow\s+about\s+\w+` |

`_STRUCTURAL_ADDITION` (`scenario.py:133-137`) — this is what keeps `add an index` in `optimization`
instead of `refinement` (pattern 9 of the refinement list matches "add …"):

```
\b(add|include)\b[^.]{0,30}\b(index(es|ing)?|indices|hints?|alias(es)?|comments?|cte|formatting|semicolon|parameters?)\b
```

#### 5.12.1 LLM scenario fallback contract

Fires only from row 8 above: no deterministic signal, `allow_llm=True`, `llm is not None`,
`len(text.split()) <= 12` (short-turn rule). (`route` always passes `allow_llm` default `True`;
the coreference preflight passes `allow_llm=False`.)

`SCENARIO_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (`scenario.py:146-155`) verbatim:

```
You classify how a user wants to modify an existing SQL query. Reply with exactly one label.
- optimization: the change preserves semantics, filters, entities and output grain (formatting, indexing, performance, converting to a CTE, removing unused joins, aliases, comments).
- refinement: the change adds or removes output attributes or narrows/replaces an established filter value while keeping the prior domain context (e.g. 'add shipping date', 'now do this for coffee').
- drill_down: the change moves to a deeper output grain or a new grouping dimension (e.g. 'break this down by customer', 'I need all order details', 'per order').
- fresh_start: the user resets and wants a new query unrelated to the current SQL.
```

Call (`scenario.py:271-292`):

```python
prompt = f"{SCENARIO_SYSTEM_PROMPT}\n\nEDITOR SQL: present\nUSER REQUEST: {query}\nLABEL:"
text = llm.complete([{"role": "system", "content": "You are a query-modification scenario classifier."},
                     {"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=16)
label = text.strip().lower().replace(" ", "_").strip("`.\n")
for candidate in ("drill_down", "refinement", "optimization", "fresh_start"):   # check order!
    if candidate in label:
        return ScenarioDecision(GenerationMode(candidate), confidence=0.7,
                                signals=[f"llm:{candidate}"], source="llm")
return None     # ⇒ caller falls through to the 0.5 optimization default
```

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| `max_tokens` | `16` |
| Label normalisation | `strip().lower().replace(" ", "_").strip("`.\n")` |
| Match rule | **substring** containment, tested in the order `drill_down`, `refinement`, `optimization`, `fresh_start` (`LLM_SCENARIO_LABELS` at `scenario.py:139-144` is defined but the loop inlines its own tuple) |
| Prompt inputs | the literal string `EDITOR SQL: present` (the SQL text is **not** sent) and the raw user request — **not** sanitised |
| Exceptions / unknown label | return `None` ⇒ default row 9 |
| Editor SQL is assumed | the LLM branch is only reachable when `has_existing_code` is true, since row 2 short-circuits otherwise |

Short-turn threshold: **12 whitespace-separated words** (`len(text.split()) <= 12`). The parallel
coreference threshold is **8 words** (`VAGUE_QUERY_MAX_WORDS`) — do not conflate them.

### 5.13 Router — complete ordered decision table

`route(context, llm=None) -> RouteDecision` (`app/core/orchestrator/router.py:91-156`).
`RouteDecision` fields (`app/models/pipeline.py:227-232`): `route`, `context`, `immediate_result`,
`skip_discovery=False`, `skip_preanalysis=False`. `RouteKind` values
(`app/core/branch_taxonomy.py:38-43`): `CodeFixing`, `Optimize`, `Refine`, `Generate`, `Conversational`.

Before the table, three side effects happen unconditionally (unless row 1 returns):

```python
raw_query = context.effective_query or req.query          # rewritten query when a rewrite happened
decision = classify_scenario(raw_query, has_existing_code=bool(req.existing_code),
                             error_message=req.error_message, llm=llm)
context.generation_mode = decision.scenario
_note(context, f"Scenario: {decision.scenario.value} ({decision.source})")
if decision.signals:
    _note(context, f"Scenario signals: {', '.join(decision.signals[:4])}")
```

`_note(context, message)` appends to `context.schema_metadata.resolution_notes` only when the exact string is
not already present (`router.py:86-88`). These notes are **not** emitted as SSE events by the built-in
generator; they are internal observability.

| # | Precondition (evaluated top-down) | `route` | `skip_discovery` | `skip_preanalysis` | Immediate result / side effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `req.force_general` | `Conversational` | `True` | `False` | yes → §5.13.1, branch `off_topic`, message `General response requested.` |
| 2 | `req.error_message and req.existing_code` | `CodeFixing` | `False` | `False` | sets `generation_mode=DEBUGGING`, `is_error_recovery=True`, `intent="db_query"` |
| — | *(scenario classification runs here for all remaining rows)* | | | | `context.generation_mode` replaced by the scenario; notes appended |
| 3 | `req.database_objects` **and** `req.existing_code` **and** `not req.error_message` **and** `decision.is_refinement` | `Refine` | `False` | `False` | — |
| 4 | `req.database_objects` **and** `req.existing_code` **and** `not req.error_message` (else) | `Optimize` | `False` | `False` | note: discovery is **not** skipped on this pinned path |
| 5 | `req.database_objects` (no existing code — row 2 already consumed error+code) | `Generate` | `False` | `False` | pins validated in Stage B |
| 6 | `should_use_simple_preanalysis_fast_path(context)` | `Generate` | `False` | `True` | `intent="db_query"` |
| 7 | `word_count(req.query) <= 50` **and** `has_strong_language_agnostic_db_signal(req.query)` | `Generate` | `False` | `False` | `intent="db_query"` |
| 8 | `req.existing_code and not req.error_message` **and** `scenario == fresh_start` | `Generate` | `False` | `False` | note `Explicit reset detected: editor SQL context dropped` |
| 9 | `req.existing_code and not req.error_message` **and** `decision.is_refinement` | `Refine` | `False` | `False` | — |
| 10 | `req.existing_code and not req.error_message` (else: `optimization`, or the `default` fallback) | `Optimize` | `True` | `False` | the only row that enables the provided-code/no-discovery path |
| 11 | `inline is not None` **and** `not req.existing_code` | `Generate` | `True` | `False` | inline fenced SQL dominates the turn |
| 12 | `classify_intent(raw_query, llm)` ∈ {`app_feature`, `off_topic`} | `Conversational` | `True` | `False` | yes → §5.13.1, branch `app_feature` / `off_topic`, message `This request was classified as {intent}.` |
| 13 | intent `refine_query` **and** `req.existing_code` | `Refine` | `False` | `False` | `generation_mode=REFINEMENT` |
| 14 | intent `refine_query` (no existing code) | `Generate` | `False` | `False` | — |
| 15 | intent `optimize_code` **and** `req.existing_code` | `Optimize` | `True` | `False` | `generation_mode=OPTIMIZATION` |
| 16 | default (incl. `db_query`) | `Generate` | `False` | `False` | `context.intent` already set to the label |

Ordering traps a re-implementation must preserve:

* Rows 6/7 short-circuit **before** the `existing_code` block (8-10) — they explicitly require
  `not req.existing_code` / `not req.error_message` (row 6) or can only be reached with no editor code in
  practice (row 7 also runs for editor-SQL requests, where rows 3-5 have not fired and row 8 has not
  returned; a ≤50-word SQL-signal query **without** pins reaches row 7 before the optimize block).
* Row 7 uses `req.query` (raw), while row 6 uses `collapse_whitespace(req.query)`; neither uses
  `raw_query`. Only `classify_scenario` and `classify_intent` see the rewritten query.
* `decision.route == Optimize` with `skip_discovery=False` occurs **only** on row 4 (pins + existing code +
  optimization scenario). Such a turn keeps discovery enabled but still gets
  `OPTIMIZATION_INSTRUCTIONS` in the prompt.

#### 5.13.1 Conversational immediate results

`_conversational(context, branch, message)` (`router.py:71-83`) builds:

```python
BuiltInGenerateResult(success=True, sql="", message=message, explanation=message,
                      query_type="general", discovery_branch=branch, attempts=0,
                      source_id=context.request.source_id, error_category=branch)
RouteDecision(route=RouteKind.CONVERSATIONAL, context=context, immediate_result=result, skip_discovery=True)
```

The generator turns that into `sse_result(finalize(result), result.message or "")` + `sse_done()` and returns
before Stage B (`builtin_sql_generator.py:112-115`). `finalize` applies `apply_language_result`, which for
`target_language != "sql"` rewrites `query_type` to `python_code` / `r_code` / `sas_code`
(`app/core/errors.py:54-72`) — so a Python-endpoint conversational turn reports `query_type="python_code"`.

#### 5.13.2 Fast-path heuristics (`skip_preanalysis`)

`has_strong_language_agnostic_db_signal(text)` (`router.py:41-50`) — order-independent OR of three tests:

| Test | Pattern / function |
|---|---|
| statement start | `SQL_STATEMENT_START = ^\s*(SELECT\|INSERT\|UPDATE\|DELETE\|MERGE\|SET\s+NOCOUNT\|SET\s+TRANSACTION\|SET\s+ANSI\|WITH\s+\w+)` (IGNORECASE, `app/utils/regexes.py:6-9`) |
| fenced SQL | `extract_inline_sql(text)` → `INLINE_SQL_BLOCK = ```(?:sql\|tsql)?\s*([\s\S]*?)``` ` (IGNORECASE, `regexes.py:16`) |
| clause pair | `CLAUSE_PAIR = (select\b[\s\S]{0,400}\bfrom\b)\|(insert\s+into\b)\|(update\b[\s\S]{0,200}\bset\b)\|(delete\s+from\b)\|(merge\s+into\b)` (IGNORECASE, `regexes.py:11-14`) |

`should_use_simple_preanalysis_fast_path(context)` (`router.py:53-68`) — **all** must hold:

| # | Condition |
|---|---|
| 1 | `not req.existing_code` and `not req.error_message` |
| 2 | `len(collapse_whitespace(req.query)) <= SimplePreAnalysisMaxCollapsedChars` (**180**) |
| 3 | `word_count(collapsed) <= SimplePreAnalysisMaxWords` (**40**) |
| 4 | `complexity_tier(collapsed) == "simple"` — i.e. **zero** hits of `COMPLEX_KEYWORDS` (`regexes.py:29-39`): `join`, `group by`, `having`, `union`, `except`, `intersect`, `compare`, `versus`, `" vs "`. Substring test on `" {lowered} "`, so `joined` / `joining` count as hits; ≥2 hits ⇒ `complex`, 1 ⇒ `moderate`, 0 ⇒ `simple` |
| 5 | none of the literal substrings `" join "`, `" group by "`, `" having "`, `" union "`, `" except "`, `" intersect "`, `" compare "`, `" versus "`, `" vs "` occurs in `f" {collapsed.lower()} "` |
| 6 | `has_strong_language_agnostic_db_signal(collapsed)` is true |

`word_count(text)` is `len(collapse_whitespace(text).split())` (`regexes.py:57-65`).

#### 5.13.3 LLM intent classifier contract

`classify_intent(query, llm)` (`router.py:159-180`):

```python
INTENT_LABELS = ("db_query", "optimize_code", "refine_query", "app_feature", "off_topic")
if llm is None: return "db_query"
prompt = ("Classify the user request as one of: db_query, optimize_code, refine_query, app_feature, off_topic. "
          "optimize_code = syntax/performance/formatting edits that preserve semantics, filters and output grain. "
          "refine_query = output grain or attribute changes, drill-downs, or replacing an established filter value. "
          "Reply with only the label.\n"
          f"USER: {query}")
text = llm.complete([{"role": "system", "content": "You are an intent classifier."},
                     {"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=16)
label = text.strip().lower().replace(" ", "_")
for candidate in INTENT_LABELS:
    if candidate in label: return candidate
return "db_query"          # also on any exception
```

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Labels | `db_query`, `optimize_code`, `refine_query`, `app_feature`, `off_topic` (checked in that order, substring match) |
| `max_tokens` | `16` |
| Input | the post-rewrite query (`raw_query`), **not** sanitised |
| Failure modes → default | `llm is None`, exception, unparseable/unknown label ⇒ `"db_query"` |

### 5.14 Stage B — pin validation

`builtin_sql_generator.py:117-166`. Runs **after** routing and **before** `DiscoveryEngine` construction.
If `context.request.database_objects` is empty, the whole stage is skipped (no status event).

```python
pins = list(context.request.database_objects or [])
if pins:
    yield emit(PipelineStage.VALIDATE_PINS, "Validating pinned objects")
    resolver = ObjectNameResolver(stores.catalog)
    resolved = resolver.resolve_many(pins)
    missing = [r for r in resolved if r.status == "missing"]
    notes = []; new_pins = []
    for r in resolved:
        if r.status == "fuzzy" and r.qualified:
            notes.append(f"Substituted {r.original} → {r.qualified} (confidence {r.confidence:.2f})")
        if r.qualified:
            new_pins.append(r.qualified)
    context.request.database_objects = new_pins          # exact + fuzzy survive, missing drop out
    context.schema_metadata.resolution_notes.extend(notes)
    if missing:
        # … build the failure payload (see below) and return immediately
```

* Substitutions: every `fuzzy` resolution whose `qualified` is set appends a note
  `Substituted {original} → {qualified} (confidence {c:.2f})` (two decimals) to
  `schema_metadata.resolution_notes`.
* Survivors: `new_pins` keeps `exact` **and** `fuzzy` names in input order; `missing` names are dropped from
  the pin list — but the request still fails (below), so that mutation is never observed by discovery.
* Resolution is **all-or-nothing preview**: if any pin is `missing`, the failure result is emitted even though
  other pins resolved fine.
* No status event accompanies the failure — only `sse_result(payload, message)` and `sse_done()`.

#### 5.14.1 `ObjectNameResolver` algorithm

`app/services/object_name_resolver.py:21-54`. `ResolvedName` dataclass fields (`:12-18`):
`original`, `qualified: Optional[str]`, `status` ∈ {`exact`, `fuzzy`, `missing`}, `confidence: float`,
`candidates: List[dict]`.

```python
def parse(raw):
    cleaned = (raw or "").strip().replace("[", "").replace("]", "")
    parts = [p for p in cleaned.split(".") if p]
    if len(parts) >= 2: return parts[0], parts[1]     # extra parts ignored
    if parts:           return "dbo", parts[0]
    return "dbo", ""

def resolve(raw):
    schema, name = parse(raw)
    if not name:
        return ResolvedName(raw, None, "missing", 0.0, [])
    if catalog.object_exists(schema, name):
        return ResolvedName(raw, f"{schema}.{name}", "exact", 1.0, [])
    for obj in catalog.list_objects():                      # unqualified fallback
        if (obj.get("object_name") or "").lower() == name.lower():
            return ResolvedName(raw, f"{obj['schema_name']}.{obj['object_name']}", "exact", 1.0, [])
    closest = catalog.find_closest(raw)
    if closest and closest[0]["confidence"] >= FuzzyMatchMinConfidence:     # 0.85
        best = closest[0]
        return ResolvedName(raw, f"{best['schema_name']}.{best['object_name']}",
                            "fuzzy", best["confidence"], closest)
    return ResolvedName(raw, None, "missing",
                        closest[0]["confidence"] if closest else 0.0, closest)
```

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Normalisation | `strip()`, then **all** `[` and `]` removed anywhere (`"dbo].[Order Details]"` → `"dbo.Order Details"`), then split on `.` dropping empty parts |
| Qualified input | `parts[0]` = schema, `parts[1]` = name; parts beyond the second are ignored (`db.dbo.T` ⇒ schema `db`, name `dbo`) |
| Unqualified input | schema forced to `"dbo"` |
| Empty name | `missing` with `confidence 0.0` and **no** candidates (no catalog access at all) |
| Exact (qualified) | `catalog.object_exists(schema, name)` — case-insensitive compare of `f"{schema}.{name}"` |
| Exact (unqualified fallback) | first catalog row whose bare `object_name` matches case-insensitively; the row's own `schema_name` is used as the qualifier; confidence `1.0`; candidates `[]` |
| Fuzzy | `catalog.find_closest(raw)`; **threshold `FuzzyMatchMinConfidence = 0.85`** on the best score; `qualified` from the best row; `confidence` = that score; `candidates` = the whole ranked list (≤ 5 rows) |
| Missing | confidence = best fuzzy score, or `0.0` when the catalog is empty; `candidates` = the ranked list (possibly empty) |
| `resolve_many(names)` | `[self.resolve(n) for n in names]` — order preserved, no dedup |

Note `find_closest` is called with the **raw pin string**, not the parsed `schema.name`.

#### 5.14.2 `DatabaseCatalog` (resolution substrate + cache)

`app/services/database_catalog.py`.

| Member | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `list_objects(force=False)` | module-global `_cache: Dict[source_id, (timestamp, List[dict])]`; returns the cached list while `now - timestamp < CatalogCacheTtlSeconds` (**300 s**, `constants.py:43`); otherwise `_load_live()` and re-cache. The cache has **no size bound** and is process-global across requests. |
| `object_exists(schema_name, object_name)` | case-insensitive compare of `f"{schema}.{object}"` over `list_objects()` |
| `find_closest(name, limit=5)` | `needle = name.lower()` with brackets stripped; for each object `candidate = f"{schema}.{object}".lower()`; `ratio = SequenceMatcher(None, needle, candidate).ratio()`; `bare = SequenceMatcher(None, needle.split(".")[-1], object_name.lower()).ratio()`; **`score = max(ratio, bare)`**; sorted descending; returns `[{"confidence": score, **obj}]` for the top `limit` |
| `_load_live()` | `SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, TABLE_TYPE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_TYPE IN ('BASE TABLE','VIEW')` through `get_database_engine(source_id)`; `object_type = "View" if "VIEW" in typ.upper() else "Table"` |
| `_load_live()` fallback 1 | on any exception, `vector_store.get_all_objects_v2(source_id)` mapped to `{schema_name, object_name, object_type or "Table"}` |
| `_load_live()` fallback 2 | on a second exception, `[]` (every pin then resolves `missing` at confidence `0.0` and **no** candidates) |

Instance lifetime: one `DatabaseCatalog` per `build_source_stores(source_id)` call
(`app/services/stores/bundle.py:47`), i.e. per request; the cache behind it is global.

#### 5.14.3 The exact failure result for an unresolvable pin

```python
candidates = []
for r in missing:
    for c in r.candidates:
        candidates.append(ScoredObject(schema_name=c.get("schema_name") or "dbo",
                                       object_name=c.get("object_name") or "",
                                       score=float(c.get("confidence") or 0)))
report = build_failure_report(
    summary="Pinned objects could not be resolved",
    resolution_plan=["Check object names", "Use schema.object format"],
    attempts=[],
    final_guidance="priority_validation_failed",
    candidates=candidates)
result = build_detailed_failure_result(
    message="Pinned objects could not be resolved",
    error_category=ErrorCategory.PRIORITY_VALIDATION_FAILED,        # "priority_validation_failed"
    discovery_branch=DiscoveryBranch.PRIORITY_VALIDATION_FAILED,    # "priority_validation_failed"
    attempts=0,
    token_usage=llm.token_usage.as_dict(),
    processing_time_ms=int((time.time() - started) * 1000),
    hallucination_count=0, agentic_retry_count=0,
    failure_report=report, source_id=source_id)
payload = finalize(result)
yield sse_result(payload, result.message or "")
yield sse_done()
return
```

Resulting HTTP payload highlights: `success=False`, `sql="/*\nPinned objects could not be resolved\n*/"`
(`wrap_failure_sql_comment`, `app/core/errors.py:40-42`), `message`/`explanation` =
`Pinned objects could not be resolved`, `discovery_branch` = `error_category` =
`priority_validation_failed`, `attempts=0`, `failure_report.summary` =
`Pinned objects could not be resolved`, `failure_report.resolution_plan` =
`["Check object names", "Use schema.object format"]`, `failure_report.final_resolution_guidance` =
`priority_validation_failed`, `failure_report.candidate_objects` = the concatenated candidate lists
(no dedup across missing pins; `ScoredObject.priority`/`required` stay `False`, `object_type` stays
`"Table"`). Parity test: `tests/parity/test_pin_failfast.py`.

### 5.15 Stage C — fast paths

Executed only when the no-discovery path did **not** fire. The single emitted status is
`Running pre-analysis fast paths` (`preanalysis`). The three lookups share one gate:

```python
preserve_filters = context.is_refinement and bool(context.active_filters)
effective_query  = context.effective_query
```

| Condition | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `context.is_refinement` | `generation_mode ∈ {refinement, drill_down}` (`AgentContext.is_refinement`, `models/pipeline.py:156-160`) |
| `context.active_filters` non-empty | filters were inherited from the session **or** parsed from this turn's editor SQL |
| `preserve_filters` | every stored-answer lookup is **skipped** (`None`), because a stored answer authored without the active filter must not satisfy the turn |

`effective_query` is the coreference-rewritten query — all three lookups use it, never `request.query`.

Order (first hit wins, each hit returns immediately):

| Order | Lookup | Call | Threshold / filter | Branch on hit | Message (payload) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `kb_exact` | `stores.fewshots.try_get_exact(effective_query)` | exact normalised-question key | `kb_exact` | `KB exact match` |
| C2 | `precomputed_exact` | `stores.vector_search.try_get_precomputed_exact(effective_query)` | `status ∈ {Approved, Modified}` + exact key | `precomputed_exact` | `Precomputed exact match` |
| C3 | `kb_vector_top1` | `stores.fewshots.search(effective_query, top_k=1, max_distance=KbScoreThreshold)` then `hits[0]` | cosine distance ≤ `KbScoreThreshold` (**0.35**) at search time, then `score <= KbExactMatchThreshold` (**0.05**) | `kb_exact` | `KB vector exact match` |

Common payload shape for all three (`builtin_sql_generator.py:187-245`):
`success=True`, `sql=code_from_match(...)`, `message=<text above>`, `discovery_branch=<branch>`,
`attempts=0`, `processing_time_ms=elapsed`, `token_usage=llm.token_usage.as_dict()`, `source_id=source_id`;
then `record_generation_outcome(context, result.sql)`, `yield sse_result(finalize(result))`,
`yield sse_done()`, `return`. `code_from_match(sql)` materialises Python / R / SAS code for the script
endpoints (`materialize_python_code` / `materialize_r_code` / `materialize_sas_code`) and is the identity for SQL.

#### 5.15.1 C1 — `kb_exact` deterministic key

`FewShotVectorService.try_get_exact` (`app/services/fewshot_vector_service.py:86-112`):

* Vector-free: it probes `sqlite_master` / `fetch_all("few_shots", source_id)` and scans scalar columns.
* First drops the legacy `few_shots_meta` table when present (`_ensure_legacy_meta_dropped`).
* Missing `few_shots` table ⇒ `None`.
* Key: `question_lookup_key(question)` (`app/utils/hashing.py:30-36`) =
  `re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.strip().lower())` — **lowercase + whitespace collapse only**; punctuation,
  articles and word order are significant. (`"  Hello   World "` and `"hello world"` are equal;
  `"count customers?"` ≠ `"count customers"`.)
* Rows are iterated in table order; rows with an **empty/whitespace-only `sql` are skipped**; the first
  matching row wins.
* Returned `FewShotExample(question=row.question, sql=stripped_sql, score=1.0, is_exact_match=True, source="few_shot")`.
* Related but separate: `CanonicalQuestionMaxWords = 25` (`constants.py:70`) governs the **critic's**
  `canonical_question` length, not this key.

#### 5.15.2 C2 — `precomputed_exact` and the semantic SMQ step

Lookup (`VectorSearchService.try_get_precomputed_exact`, `app/services/vector_search_service.py:92-108`):
`fetch_all("vec_data_group_queries", source_id)`, keep only rows whose `status` is exactly `"Approved"` or
`"Modified"`, compare `question_lookup_key(row.question) == question_lookup_key(question)`, first match wins.
Returned `FewShotExample(question=row["question"], sql=row.get("sql_query") or "", score=1.0,
is_exact_match=True, smq_query=row.get("smq_query") or "", source="precomputed")`.
Unlike C1 this lookup does **not** skip rows with an empty `sql_query`.

Semantic compile step (`builtin_sql_generator.py:202-228`):

```python
pre_exact = None if preserve_filters else engine.precomputed_exact(effective_query)
if pre_exact:
    sql = pre_exact.sql
    if semantic_mode and pre_exact.smq_query:
        from app.services.semantic_compiler import SemanticCompiler
        from app.models.pipeline import SmqPayload
        import json
        try:
            payload = SmqPayload.model_validate(json.loads(pre_exact.smq_query))
            sql = SemanticCompiler().compile(payload, stores.semantic.get_active_model(), context.dbms_type)
        except Exception:
            sql = pre_exact.sql          # any failure ⇒ stored physical SQL (fallback)
```

* `semantic_mode` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:170`):
  `False` for `python`/`r`/`sas` targets (`script_mode`), else
  `stores.semantic.is_enabled(context.request.semantic_mode)`.
  `SemanticModelService.is_enabled` (`app/services/semantic_model_service.py:22-33`): an explicit
  `request_override` must be truthy **and** an active model must exist; `enable_flag` comes from
  `settings.semantic_layer_enabled_for(source_id)` (`app/core/config.py:108-115`, `None` when the source is
  absent from `ENABLE_SEMANTIC_LAYER_PER_DATA_SOURCE`); `False` ⇒ disabled; otherwise enabled iff
  `get_active_model()` is not `None`.
* `smq_query` is a JSON string of `{"metrics": [], "dimensions": [], "filters": [], "timeframes": []}`.
* The fallback covers: invalid JSON, `SmqPayload` validation error, no active model, compiler error.
  No status event and no note is emitted either way.

#### 5.15.3 C3 — `kb_vector_top1` threshold semantics

`DiscoveryEngine.kb_vector_top1` (`discovery_engine.py:68-70`) =
`stores.fewshots.search(question, top_k=1, max_distance=KbScoreThreshold)` → `hits[0] if hits else None`.
`search` (`fewshot_vector_service.py:114-133`) passes `min_score=max_distance` to
`provider.search_vector`; the SQLite/Milvus providers drop rows where `cosine_distance > min_score`
(`app/services/stores/sqlite_vec_provider.py:171-177`, `milvus_provider.py:273`). So:

| Stage | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| pre-filter | `KbScoreThreshold = 0.35` | keep only neighbours with cosine **distance ≤ 0.35** (similarity ≥ 0.65) |
| `FewShotExample.score` | the raw `_distance` | a distance, not a similarity |
| `is_exact_match` flag | set when `_distance <= KbExactMatchThreshold (0.05)` | informational; the fast path does its own check |
| fast-path gate | `kb_top and kb_top.score <= KbExactMatchThreshold` (**0.05**) | distance ≤ 0.05 ⇒ similarity ≥ 0.95 ⇒ treat as exact |

The gate calls `Kb_distance_exact()` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:355-358`), a thin wrapper returning
`KbExactMatchThreshold`.

#### 5.15.4 Refinement-with-active-filters bypass

All three lookups are individually gated by `None if preserve_filters else …`. Consequences to reproduce:

* A `refinement`/`drill_down` turn whose session (or editor SQL) carries at least one filter **always**
  continues to query analysis + discovery, even when a stored exact answer exists. This is the intent of
  `tests/parity/test_refinement_scope_expansion.py:125-143`, where `I need all order details` is stored in
  `few_shots` and the request still ends with a discovery branch ≠ `kb_exact`.
* A `fresh_start` turn, or any turn with no active filters, still benefits from the fast paths.
* The bypass is evaluated **once**, before C1, so all three lookups see the same decision.
* `record_generation_outcome` is *not* called on a bypassed lookup (nothing was matched).

### 5.16 The provided-code / no-discovery path

**Trigger** (`builtin_sql_generator.py:172-178`) — all three conditions must hold:

1. `decision.skip_discovery is True`, **and**
2. `decision.route in {RouteKind.OPTIMIZE, RouteKind.GENERATE}`, **and**
3. `context.request.existing_code` is non-empty/truthy.

Which router rows satisfy that: row 10 (`Optimize`, existing code, optimization scenario or default),
row 11 (`Generate` + inline SQL — but row 11 requires `not req.existing_code`, so condition 3 fails and it
never takes this path), row 15 (intent `optimize_code` + existing code), row 12 (`Conversational`, route is
not OPTIMIZE/GENERATE). In practice the path is reached from **row 10 and row 15 only** — and row 4 (pins +
existing code + optimization) deliberately does **not** reach it because its `skip_discovery` is `False`.

On entry: `yield emit(PipelineStage.PREANALYSIS, "No-discovery provided-code path")`, run
`_generate_from_provided_sql(context, stores, llm, emit, started, target_language=...)`, then
`yield sse_result(finalize(result), result.message or "")`, `yield sse_done()`, `return`.
Note this happens **before** `Running pre-analysis fast paths`, so the provided-code path never consults the
KB / precomputed stores.

`_generate_from_provided_sql` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:361-512`) — full behaviour:

```python
existing  = context.request.existing_code or ""
validator = SqlValidator(context.request.source_id, context.dbms_type)
deadline  = started + (NoDiscoveryTimeBudgetMs / 1000.0)          # 90 s

def _validate(code):
    if python_mode:            # r_mode / sas_mode are the mirror image
        ok, err = syntax_check_python(code)
        if not ok: return False, err
        sqls = extract_sql_from_python(code)
        if not sqls: return True, ""                              # no embedded SQL ⇒ nothing more to check
        for sql in sqls:
            db_ok, db_err, _ = validator.validate(sql)
            if not db_ok: return False, db_err
        return True, ""
    return validator.validate(code)[:2]                           # SQL: (ok, err)

code = materialize_python_code(existing) / materialize_r_code / materialize_sas_code / existing
optimization_scenario = context.generation_mode == GenerationMode.OPTIMIZATION

ok, err = _validate(code)
if ok and not optimization_scenario:                             # 1) historical short-circuit
    return BuiltInGenerateResult(success=True, sql=code, discovery_branch=NO_DISCOVERY, attempts=1, …)

if time.time() > deadline:                                        # 2) budget already blown
    return build_detailed_failure_result(message=err or "timeout", error_category=TIMEOUT,
        discovery_branch=NO_DISCOVERY, attempts=1,
        failure_report=build_failure_report(summary=err, resolution_plan=[], attempts=[], final_guidance="timeout"), …)

system_prompt = build_optimization_system_prompt(context, code,
                    error_message=err if not ok else None, target_language=target_language)
user_prompt   = build_optimization_user_prompt(context, code, err if not ok else None)
original_code = code
try:
    raw   = llm.complete([{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
                          {"role": "user",   "content": user_prompt}])      # no max_tokens ⇒ LlmClient default 2048
    fixed = extract_python_body(raw) / extract_r_body / extract_sas_body / extract_sql_body(raw) or code
    ok, err = _validate(fixed)
    if ok: code = fixed
except Exception:
    pass                                                          # ok/err keep their pre-call values

if ok:                                                            # 3) rewrite validated
    return BuiltInGenerateResult(success=True, sql=code,
        message="Optimized in place (editor SQL only)" if optimization_scenario else None,
        discovery_branch=NO_DISCOVERY, attempts=2, …)
if optimization_scenario:                                         # 4) never break the user's query
    return BuiltInGenerateResult(success=True, sql=original_code,
        message="Optimization rewrite did not validate; the original editor SQL was kept.",
        discovery_branch=NO_DISCOVERY, attempts=2, …)
return build_detailed_failure_result(message=err or "validation failed", error_category=VALIDATION,
    discovery_branch=NO_DISCOVERY, attempts=2,
    failure_report=build_failure_report(summary=err or "validation failed", resolution_plan=[], attempts=[],
                                        final_guidance=err or "validation failed"), …)
```

Decision table:

| # | Condition | Outcome | `success` | `attempts` | `message` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_validate(code)` OK **and** scenario ≠ `optimization` | return the editor code unchanged | `True` | `1` | `None` |
| 2 | `time.time() > deadline` | `TIMEOUT` failure result | `False` | `1` | `err or "timeout"` |
| 3 | rewrite validates | return the rewritten code | `True` | `2` | `Optimized in place (editor SQL only)` when the scenario is `optimization`, else `None` |
| 4 | rewrite fails **and** scenario == `optimization` | return the **original** editor code | `True` | `2` | `Optimization rewrite did not validate; the original editor SQL was kept.` |
| 5 | rewrite fails, other scenario | `VALIDATION` failure result | `False` | `2` | `err or "validation failed"` |
| — | LLM raised | falls into rows 3-5 with the pre-call `ok`/`err` — i.e. the original validation verdict decides | | | |

Key subtleties:

* For the `optimization` scenario the LLM is called **even when the editor code already validates**
  (`ok and not optimization_scenario` is the only short-circuit); a modification request must produce a
  modification.
* `discovery_branch` is always `no_discovery` (`DiscoveryBranch.NO_DISCOVERY`).
* The prompt used is `build_optimization_system_prompt` — schema-free, no `AVAILABLE SCHEMAS`, and
  **no** `ACTIVE SESSION FILTERS` block (§5.10).
* `_validate` returns a 2-tuple everywhere, including the script branches.

### 5.17 Per-stage contracts (inputs / outputs / side effects / caches / SSE)

| Stage | Inputs | Outputs | Side effects | Cache usage | SSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-1 `build_agent_request` | `GenerateSQLRequest`, `stores.source_id` | `AgentRequest` | none | none | — (status #1 already emitted) |
| A-2 `parse_query_history` / `fold_conversation` | `request.query`, `request.queryHistory` | `List[ConversationTurn]`, `combined_query: str` | none | none | — |
| A-3 `preprocess` | `AgentRequest` (+ ignored `stores`) | `AgentContext` (`schema_metadata`, `generation_mode`, `is_error_recovery`, `combined_query`) | none observable (`resolved_object_names` / `resolution_notes` are write-only) | none | — |
| A-4 `prepare_conversation_context` | `AgentRequest`, `llm`, store | `ConversationContextResult` | **writes the session store** (`store.put`, LRU touch/evict) | in-process `_session_store` (256 LRU, no TTL) | #2 or #3 |
| A-4b `apply_conversation_context` | `AgentContext`, result | mutated `AgentContext` (`session_id`, `rewritten_query`, `coreference_notes`, `active_filters`, `filter_state_text`, `combined_query`) | none | — | — |
| A-5 `route` | `AgentContext`, `llm` | `RouteDecision` | mutates `context.generation_mode`, `context.intent`, `context.is_error_recovery`, appends `resolution_notes` | none | #1 already sent; conversational rows produce `result`+`done` |
| B pin validation | `request.database_objects`, `stores.catalog`, `llm.token_usage` | `ResolvedName[]` → new pin list + notes | mutates `request.database_objects`, extends `resolution_notes` | `DatabaseCatalog._cache` (global, keyed by `source_id`, TTL 300 s, unbounded); `list_objects` may hit `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` or the vector store | #4, or `result`+`done` on failure |
| C fast paths | `context.effective_query`, `context.is_refinement`, `context.active_filters`, `semantic_mode`, stores | a `BuiltInGenerateResult` or `None` | `record_generation_outcome` on a hit; `DiscoveryEngine.clear_analysis_cache()` runs just before (per-request instance ⇒ no-op) | `few_shots` / `vec_data_group_queries` scanned with `fetch_all` (no row cache); C3 uses the vector search path (provider-side embedding cache) | #6 (only) |
| C′ no-discovery | `existing_code`, `llm`, `SqlValidator`, 90 s budget | `BuiltInGenerateResult` (`no_discovery`) | token usage on `llm`; DB validation calls | none | #5, then `result`+`done` |

`record_generation_outcome` is the only Stage-A/C code that persists anything beyond the request lifetime
(§5.11); the session store and `DatabaseCatalog._cache` are process-local, so a re-implementation with
multiple workers must accept per-process session state (standard for this port).
