### Implementation checklist

- [ ] `build_agent_request`: mask the query with the four PII regexes **in order**; use
      `existing_code or previousSQL`; `top_k or 8`; copy `database_objects` / `table_override` verbatim;
      parse `queryHistory`; carry `is_user_code`, `semantic_mode`, `forceGeneral`, `session_id`, `source_id`.
- [ ] `parse_query_history`: split on `" | "` and `"\n"`, drop empties, `q:`/`a:` prefix tests
      (case-insensitive, after strip), other lines become question-only turns.
- [ ] `fold_conversation`: `"{query}\n" + "\n".join("Q: {q} | A: {a}")`; `[failed]` / `[canceled]`;
      truncate answers to 200 chars for every turn **except the last**.
- [ ] `preprocess`: auto-extract `schema.object` names (≤ 5, dedup case-insensitively) **only** when no pins
      exist; record them in `schema_metadata` (they are not pins); provisional mode
      `debugging`/`optimization`/`fresh_start`; `is_error_recovery` for debugging; `combined_query` folded;
      leave `dbms_type` at `"SQL Server"`.
- [ ] Session store: `OrderedDict` + lock, 256 entries, LRU eviction, `updated_at` recorded but no TTL,
      deep copies on `get`/`put`, `clear()` for all.
- [ ] `session_key`: `session:{source_id}:{session_id}` / `session:{session_id}` / `None`; skip all store I/O
      when there is no `session_id` but still run the lifecycle rules on the editor SQL's filters.
- [ ] Filter extraction: `_ALIAS_TABLE` + `_PREDICATE` verbatim; alias stop-list
      `ON WHERE INNER LEFT RIGHT FULL CROSS JOIN GROUP ORDER`; literal RHS only; drop `col/val == "1"`;
      map qualifier → table (alias name itself when unknown), else the single table; dedup on
      `(entity, column)`; cap `MaxActiveFilters = 12`; `source="sql"`, `origin_turn=turn_index`.
- [ ] Filter lifecycle: clear on `detect_filter_clear` (reset ∪ filter-clear lists, verbatim); replacement via
      the five `_REPLACEMENT_PATTERNS` + stop-word set; re-quote `= LIKE <> !=` values preserving the
      template's `%`; leave `NOT LIKE` alone; notes text verbatim.
- [ ] Coreference gate: skip SQL-shaped text, `schema.object` mentions, > 8 words; fire on the 14 vague
      patterns, or on ≤ 8 anaphoric words with context (abort when a filter value token is already in the text).
- [ ] LLM rewrite: system prompt verbatim; last ≤ 3 turns; answers truncated to 200 chars with newlines → spaces;
      `sanitize_conversation_history(lines, max_messages=6)`; `max_tokens=256`; JSON
      `{rewritten_query, carried_filters[{entity, attribute, operator, value}], changed}`; validate
      non-empty / different / ≤ 400 chars / ≥ 50 % of the original (min 8); parse carried filters
      (`source="llm"`, default operator `"="`); any failure ⇒ deterministic path.
- [ ] Deterministic fallback: fold only `phrase()`-producing filters (quoted value and operator `=` / `LIKE`),
      skip phrases already present and values already restated, join with `" and "`, prefix
      `"{query} for "`, abandon if the result exceeds 400 chars.
- [ ] Never rewrite directed optimization edits: `existing_code` **and** the deterministic preflight scenario
      `optimization` ⇒ `source="skipped_optimization"`, `rewritten_query == request.query`.
- [ ] Merge precedence: `merge_filters` keyed by `(entity.lower(), attribute.lower())`, later wins, order
      preserved; keep entity in the key.
- [ ] Prompt injection: `GENERATION MODE` + scenario rules + `ACTIVE SESSION FILTERS` + `SCOPE GUARD`
      (guard only when `filter_state_text` is neither empty nor `"(none)"`); the filter block is **absent**
      from the no-discovery optimization prompt.
- [ ] `record_generation_outcome`: merge the generated SQL's literal filters under turn `turn_index`, set
      `last_sql`, touch `source_id`, `put` the state; no-op without a session key.
- [ ] Scenario classifier: ordered table 1-9 with the exact confidences (1.0 / 1.0 / 0.95 / 0.9 / 0.85-0.9 /
      0.85 / 0.9 / 0.7 / 0.5) and sources; `_STRUCTURAL_ADDITION` beats refinement; `refine` signals
      concatenate the filter-clear matches; LLM fallback only when no signal, `allow_llm`, an LLM exists and
      ≤ 12 words, with `max_tokens=16` and substring label matching in `drill_down, refinement, optimization,
      fresh_start` order; otherwise `optimization` / `0.5` / `default`.
- [ ] Router: reproduce rows 1-16 exactly, including `_conversational` payload shape
      (`query_type="general"`, `error_category=branch`, `attempts=0`, `skip_discovery=True`), the two
      fast-path heuristics (180 chars / 40 words / complexity `simple` / keyword blocklist / strong DB
      signal; 50-word ceiling), inline-SQL handling, and `classify_intent` (labels, `max_tokens=16`,
      `/db_query/` default).
- [ ] Pin validation: `ObjectNameResolver.parse` (bracket strip, first two dotted parts, `dbo` default),
      exact → qualified, unqualified bare-name fallback, fuzzy at `≥ 0.85` with `Substituted … (confidence
      x.xx)` notes, `DatabaseCatalog.find_closest` = `max(SequenceMatcher(full), SequenceMatcher(bare))`;
      failure ⇒ `priority_validation_failed` result with the exact summary / resolution plan / guidance and
      the concatenated candidate list, emitted **before** discovery.
- [ ] Fast paths in order C1 → C2 → C3, all gated by `preserve_filters = is_refinement and active_filters`,
      all using `effective_query`, all with `attempts=0`, the three branch labels and the three payload
      messages; C2 compiles `smq_query` only in semantic mode and falls back to the stored SQL on any
      exception; C3 requires distance ≤ 0.05 after a 0.35 pre-filter.
- [ ] No-discovery path: trigger only when `skip_discovery and route ∈ {Optimize, Generate} and existing_code`;
      validate first; short-circuit a valid script unless the scenario is `optimization`; honour the 90 s
      deadline; rewrite once; keep the original code (as a **success**) when an optimization rewrite fails to
      validate; otherwise return the `validation` failure with `attempts=2` and branch `no_discovery`.
- [ ] Emit the six status strings verbatim (`Validating and routing request`,
      `Resolved follow-up context: …`, `Carried N active filter(s)`, `Validating pinned objects`,
      `No-discovery provided-code path`, `Running pre-analysis fast paths`) with the right `stage` and a
      monotonically increasing `step_id` starting at 1.

---

## 06 — Stage D: Query Analysis, Data Groups, Knowledge-Base-First Discovery, Ranking RRF and Context Hydration

Stage D is the retrieval heart of the built-in generator. It turns a natural-language turn into
(a) a short ranked list of schema objects, (b) the exact markdown blocks that will be pasted into the
generation prompt, and (c) a branch label used for analytics and tests. Everything in this section is
deterministic except the optional `analyze_query` LLM call.

### 06.0 Files, entry point, and execution order

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `app/core/orchestrator/builtin_sql_generator.py` | Stage D driver: pre-analysis exits, `analyze_query`, `resolve_active_data_groups`, `discover`, hydration wiring (`:182-292`) |
| `app/core/orchestrator/discovery_engine.py` | `DiscoveryEngine`: analysis, groups, KB-first decision tree, column evidence, caches |
| `app/utils/rrf.py` | `rrf_score`, `rrf_merge`, `merge_and_dedup` |
| `app/utils/hashing.py` | `discovery_cache_key`, `query_analysis_cache_key`, `as_text_token`, `question_lookup_key` |
| `app/utils/regexes.py` | `complexity_tier`, `COMPLEX_KEYWORDS`, `extract_qualified_object_names` |
| `app/services/vector_search_service.py` | `search_objects` (parent roll-up), `search_columns_scored`, `search_precomputed`, `try_get_precomputed_exact` |
| `app/services/fewshot_vector_service.py` | `try_get_exact`, `search` (KB few-shot vector search) |
| `app/services/value_index_service.py` | `plain_value` substring search (no vectors) |
| `app/services/bm25_service.py` | Optional lexical rank signal |
| `app/services/schema_index_service.py` | In-memory keyword index for objects and data-group keyword overlap |
| `app/services/stores/data_group_store.py` | Data-group metadata + semantic vector cache + `search` |
| `app/services/stores/precomputed_store.py` | Approved/modified precomputed Q&A rows |
| `app/services/sql_context_hydrator.py` | Four prompt slices, token budget, column pruning |
| `app/services/stores/skills_folder.py` | Skills-folder markdown lookup for hydration |
| `app/services/schema_context_utils.py` | Legacy schema-text builders (**not** on the built-in path — see 06.9.7) |
| `app/services/object_name_resolver.py`, `database_catalog.py`, `relationship_graph.py` | Pin resolution, catalog TTL, FK graph (legacy/adjacent helpers) |
| `app/core/orchestrator/attempts.py` | `_expand_missing` / `_merge_recovery` recovery API consumed by Stage E |

Stage D call order (`builtin_sql_generator.py:182-292`):

```
182  emit(PREANALYSIS, "Running pre-analysis fast paths")
183  preserve_filters = context.is_refinement and bool(context.active_filters)
185  kb_exact      = None if preserve_filters else engine.kb_exact(effective_query)          -> exit kb_exact
202  pre_exact     = None if preserve_filters else engine.precomputed_exact(effective_query) -> exit precomputed_exact
231  kb_top        = None if preserve_filters else engine.kb_vector_top1(effective_query)    -> exit kb_exact (score <= 0.05)
248  analysis      = engine.analyze_query(context.combined_query, existing_code, skip=decision.skip_preanalysis)
253  groups        = engine.resolve_active_data_groups(context.combined_query)
256  anchor        = existing_code if (is_error_recovery or existing_code) else combined_query
257  discovery     = engine.discover(anchor, analysis, pins, table_override, top_k, existing_sql=existing_code)
267  if is_refinement and existing_code: merge editor-SQL base objects; branch = scenario_branch(branch, mode)
277  discovery.active_groups = groups
278  discovery.query_analysis = analysis
279  hydrator = SqlContextHydrator(cap=12) if is_refinement else SqlContextHydrator(cap=8)
284  hydrator.set_value_mappings(discovery.value_mappings)
285  markdown_lookup = markdown_lookup_for_objects(source_id, discovery.objects)
286  selected, supp, schema, validation = hydrator.build_contexts(discovery.objects, markdown_lookup)
289-292 discovery.{selected_object_context, supplementary_objects, schema_context, schema_context_for_validation} = ...
294  run_attempt_loop(context, discovery, stores, llm, ...)      # Stage E
```

Two facts that shape the whole section:

1. `DiscoveryEngine` is constructed **per request** (`builtin_sql_generator.py:168`, `:543`). Its
   `_discovery_cache` / `_analysis_cache` are instance dictionaries, so `engine.clear_analysis_cache()`
   at `:169` clears an empty dict — it is defensive, not a cross-request invalidation. The advertised caps
   (256 / 100) therefore only bite for long-lived engine instances (tests, `discover_for_api` reuse).
2. `discover(..., existing_sql=...)` accepts `existing_sql` but **never reads it**
   (`discovery_engine.py:133-247`). Recovery-from-SQL is expressed by passing the editor SQL as the
   `query` argument (`anchor`, `:256`).

> ⚠️ Unverified: whether `existing_sql` was intended to feed a drift check. Faithful re-implementation
> should keep the parameter (call sites pass it) and keep it unused.

---

### 06.1 `analyze_query` end to end

`DiscoveryEngine.analyze_query(combined_query, existing_code, skip=False) -> QueryAnalysis`
(`discovery_engine.py:72-118`).

#### 06.1.1 Skip path (router)

```python
if skip:
    return QueryAnalysis(complexity="simple")
```

- The skip flag is `RouteDecision.skip_preanalysis`, set only by
  `should_use_simple_preanalysis_fast_path()` (`router.py:53-68`, `:122-124`).
- The skip path **does not write the cache** (`discovery_engine.py:73-74` returns before the cache store).
- The returned analysis is entirely empty: `keywords=[]`, `entities=[]`, `date_ranges=[]`,
  `filter_values=[]`, `extracted_columns=[]`, `complexity="simple"`.
- Consequence in `discover`: the discovery cache key falls back to `[query]` for its entity part
  (`:155`) and `discover_with_column_evidence` takes the **whole-query** column branch (`:271`), because
  `extracted_columns` is empty. `filter_values` is empty, so no value-index seeding happens at all.

`should_use_simple_preanalysis_fast_path` rules (all must hold), `router.py:53-68`:

1. `request.existing_code` falsy **and** `request.error_message` falsy.
2. `len(collapse_whitespace(query)) <= SimplePreAnalysisMaxCollapsedChars` (180).
3. `word_count(collapsed) <= SimplePreAnalysisMaxWords` (40).
4. `complexity_tier(collapsed) == "simple"` (see 06.1.3).
5. None of these lowercase keywords appear in `" " + collapsed.lower() + " "`:
   `join`, `group by`, `having`, `union`, `except`, `intersect`, `compare`, `versus`, `vs`
   (each matched with surrounding spaces).
6. `has_strong_language_agnostic_db_signal(collapsed)` — true when any of:
   - `SQL_STATEMENT_START` matches (start-of-text `SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|MERGE|SET NOCOUNT|SET TRANSACTION|SET ANSI|WITH <word>`),
   - `extract_inline_sql(text)` finds a ```` ```sql ```` block,
   - `CLAUSE_PAIR` matches (`select…from`, `insert into`, `update…set`, `delete from`, `merge into`).

#### 06.1.2 Cache

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Key function | `query_analysis_cache_key(combined_query, existing_code)` (`hashing.py:53-57`) |
| Key content | `f"{(combined_query or '').strip()}\|{(existing_code or '').strip()}"` |
| Key when raw length > 512 | `sha256_text(raw)` (hex digest) |
| Cache | `self._analysis_cache: Dict[str, QueryAnalysis]` |
| Cap | `MaxQueryAnalysisCacheEntries = 100` (`constants.py:45`) |
| Eviction policy | **full clear** when `len(cache) >= 100` *before* insert (`:115-116`); not LRU |
| Hit return | `self._analysis_cache[key].model_copy(deep=True)` (`:77`) |
| Store return | `analysis.model_copy(deep=True)` (`:118`) — the stored object is never handed out by reference |

Note the key includes `existing_code`, so the same question asked with a different editor SQL
re-analyses; and the raw (non-hashed) key embeds the entire query text for short turns.

#### 06.1.3 Deterministic complexity heuristic (always computed first)

```python
analysis = QueryAnalysis(complexity=complexity_tier(combined_query))
```

`complexity_tier` (`regexes.py:119-126`):

```python
lowered = f" {(text or '').lower()} "
hits = sum(1 for kw in COMPLEX_KEYWORDS if kw in lowered)
if hits >= 2:   return "complex"
if hits == 1:   return "moderate"
return "simple"
```

`COMPLEX_KEYWORDS` (`regexes.py:29-39`), matched case-insensitively as **plain substrings** inside a
space-padded lowercase copy:

| # | Keyword | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `join` | matches `join`, `joins`, `rejoin` |
| 2 | `group by` | requires the literal space |
| 3 | `having` | |
| 4 | `union` | matches `union all` |
| 5 | `except` | |
| 6 | `intersect` | |
| 7 | `compare` | matches `compared`, `comparison` does not |
| 8 | `versus` | |
| 9 | `" vs "` | the padding spaces are essential; a trailing `vs` at end of text matches because of the trailing pad |

Because the text is padded with one leading/trailing space, `" vs "` also matches a query ending in
`vs`. The LLM result overrides this **only** when it returns a non-empty string (06.1.4 step 3);
otherwise the heuristic value survives.

#### 06.1.4 LLM contract

Only executed when `self.llm is not None` (`:79`). Messages (`:81-92`), byte-for-byte:

```python
[
  {"role": "system",
   "content": ("Return JSON keys: keywords, complexity, entities, date_ranges, "
               "filter_values, extracted_columns. Every list item must be a string, not an object.")},
  {"role": "user", "content": combined_query[:2000]},
]
```

Call path and defaults: `LlmClient.complete_json(messages)` → `complete(messages)` →
`temperature=0.0`, `max_tokens=2048`, `presence_penalty=None`, `model=None`
(`llm_client.py:18-25`, `:64-78`). `complete_json` strips a leading markdown fence, then
`json.loads`; on failure it slices from the first `{` to the last `}` and retries; if that fails it
returns `{}` (`llm_client.py:64-78`). `complete` wraps the provider call and, on exception, raises
`RuntimeError` (`:57-59`) — that exception is caught by `analyze_query` (`:113-114`), so a provider
outage degrades to the heuristic-only analysis instead of failing the turn.

Field parsing rules (`:93-112`):

| JSON field | Type expected | Handling | Result field |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keywords` | list | `_stringify_terms` | `analysis.keywords` |
| `complexity` | str | used only if `isinstance(str)` and `.strip()` non-empty; stored **unstripped-normalized** (`.strip()` applied, no enum validation) | `analysis.complexity` |
| `entities` | list | `_stringify_terms` | `analysis.entities` |
| `date_ranges` | list | `_stringify_terms` | `analysis.date_ranges` |
| `filter_values` | list | `_stringify_terms` | `analysis.filter_values` |
| `extracted_columns` | list | custom loop (below) | `analysis.extracted_columns` |

`_stringify_terms(values)` (`discovery_engine.py:37-49`):

```python
out, seen = [], set()
for item in values or []:
    text = as_text_token(item)          # str -> strip(); dict -> first of name/entity/value/text/label/keyword/column
    if not text: continue
    key = text.lower()
    if key in seen: continue
    seen.add(key)
    out.append(text)
return out
```

`as_text_token` (`hashing.py:12-27`) coerces dicts by trying `name`, `entity`, `value`, `text`,
`label`, `keyword`, `column` in that order, then the first string value, then `str(value)`;
`None` → `""`. This is what keeps an LLM that returns `[{"name": "category"}]` working
(`tests/unit/test_discovery_cache_key.py:8-35`).

`extracted_columns` loop verbatim (`:100-112`):

```python
cols, seen = [], set()
for col in data.get("extracted_columns") or []:
    c = as_text_token(col).strip("[]\"'`")
    if "." in c:
        c = c.split(".")[-1]          # keep only the bare column name
    keyc = c.lower()
    if c and keyc not in seen:
        seen.add(keyc)
        cols.append(c)
    if len(cols) >= 20:
        break
analysis.extracted_columns = cols
```

Rules: max **20** columns; bracket/quote characters stripped from both ends; qualified names reduced
to their final segment; case-insensitive de-duplication keeping the first spelling; empty strings
dropped; the 20-cap breaks *after* appending, so exactly 20 max.

#### 06.1.5 Downstream use of each field

| Field | Consumers |
|---|---|
| `complexity` | discovery cache key (`:155`); prompt header `QUERY ANALYSIS` (`prompts.py:89-90`) |
| `keywords` | prompt header only (`prompts.py:90`) |
| `entities` | discovery cache key (`:155`) |
| `date_ranges` | **no consumer in Stage D/E prompt builders** (stored only) |
| `filter_values` | column evidence value-index seeding (`:190-200`, `:252-264`), `value_mappings` (`:241-245`) |
| `extracted_columns` | column-entity vector search (`:266-269`), discovery cache key, and Stage E recovery column expansion (`attempts.py:284`, `:546-548`) |

#### 06.1.6 Pseudocode

```
analyze_query(combined_query, existing_code, skip):
    if skip: return QueryAnalysis(complexity="simple")            # uncached
    key = sha256(raw) if len(raw) > 512 else raw                  # raw = f"{combined_query.strip()}|{existing_code.strip()}"
    if key in cache: return deep_copy(cache[key])
    a = QueryAnalysis(complexity=complexity_tier(combined_query))
    if llm is not None:
        try:
            data = llm.complete_json([SYSTEM_ANALYSIS_PROMPT, {user: combined_query[:2000]}])
            a.keywords          = stringify_terms(data["keywords"])
            if isinstance(data["complexity"], str) and data["complexity"].strip():
                a.complexity    = data["complexity"].strip()
            a.entities          = stringify_terms(data["entities"])
            a.date_ranges       = stringify_terms(data["date_ranges"])
            a.filter_values     = stringify_terms(data["filter_values"])
            a.extracted_columns = dedupe_strip_cap20(data["extracted_columns"])
        except Exception: pass
    if len(cache) >= 100: cache.clear()
    cache[key] = a
    return deep_copy(a)
```

---

### 06.2 `resolve_active_data_groups`

`resolve_active_data_groups(query) -> ActiveDataGroupContext` (`discovery_engine.py:120-131`).

```
groups = stores.data_groups.search(query, top_n=ActiveDataGroupTopN)          # 3
if not groups:
    scored = stores.schema_index.score_data_group_keywords(query, stores.data_groups.list())
    groups = [g for g in scored if g.get("overlap", 0) > 0][:ActiveDataGroupTopN]
members = {}
for g in groups:
    for member in g.get("members") or []:
        members.setdefault(str(member).lower(), []).append(g.get("group_name") or g.get("group_id"))
names = [g.get("group_name") or g.get("group_id") for g in groups]
summary = f"Active data groups: {', '.join(str(n) for n in names)}" if names else ""
return ActiveDataGroupContext(top_groups=groups, member_groups=members, summary=summary)
```

#### 06.2.1 Vector path (primary)

`DataGroupStore.search` (`data_group_store.py:70-85`):

1. `meta = {r["group_id"]: r for r in self.list()}` — `list()` fetches `data_group_metadata` for the
   source and JSON-decodes `keywords_json` → `keywords`, `members_json` → `members` (`:57-68`).
2. Read every row of `data_group_vectors_cache` for the source.
3. `vec = loads_vector(row["semantic_vector_json"])`; rows with an empty/unparseable vector are skipped.
4. `sim = cosine_similarity(query_vector, vec)` — **only the semantic vector** is scored here; the
   `functional_vector_json` and `object_vector_json` columns are written but never read by `search`.
5. `info = dict(meta.get(row["group_id"]) or {"group_id": row["group_id"]})`; `info["score"] = sim`.
6. Sort by `score` descending, return `[:top_n]` (3).

There is **no weighting formula and no threshold**: group scores are raw cosine similarities in
`[-1, 1]`, and the top 3 are always returned when the cache has rows. A group with similarity 0 or
negative is still returned if there are fewer than 3 cached groups.

The query vector is `embed_text(query, provider, source_id)` (L1/L2 cached; hash-embedding fallback
when no embedding provider is configured — `stores/embeddings.py:101-128`).

#### 06.2.2 Keyword fallback (only when the vector path returns zero groups)

`SchemaIndexService.score_data_group_keywords` (`schema_index_service.py:56-73`):

```python
q_tokens = set(t.lower() for t in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", query or ""))
for group in groups:
    keywords = group.get("keywords") or []          # already JSON-decoded by DataGroupStore.list()
    if isinstance(keywords, str): try json.loads else [keywords]
    g_tokens = set(str(k).lower() for k in keywords)
    overlap = 0.0 if not q_tokens else len(q_tokens & g_tokens) / max(len(q_tokens), 1)
    scored.append({**group, "overlap": overlap})
scored.sort(key=lambda g: g["overlap"], reverse=True)
```

Overlap = `|query_tokens ∩ group_keywords| / max(|query_tokens|, 1)` — a query-side-normalized
recall, **not** Jaccard. Only groups with `overlap > 0` survive the caller's filter, then `[:3]`.
Group keyword tokens are compared as whole lowercased strings (no tokenizer run over the keyword
strings themselves, so a keyword of `"credit risk"` never matches the token `credit`).

#### 06.2.3 Member expansion and summary

- `member_groups` maps `str(member).lower()` → list of `group_name` (falling back to `group_id`).
  Member strings are stored verbatim from `members_json` (e.g. `"dbo.Orders"`, `"Orders"`). The key is
  the **lowercase full member string** — the same shape later tested in `discover`.
- `summary` is `""` when no groups, else `"Active data groups: " + ", ".join(names)`. It is injected
  into the prompt as `ACTIVE BUSINESS CONTEXT` (`prompts.py:92-93`).

`ActiveDataGroupContext` (`models/pipeline.py:245-248`): `top_groups: List[Dict[str, Any]]`,
`member_groups: Dict[str, List[str]]`, `summary: str`.

#### 06.2.4 How groups feed discovery

- `discover` calls `resolve_active_data_groups(query)` again (its own copy, `:204`) to build the
  `data_group` RRF list; the driver's copy is overwritten back onto the result afterwards
  (`builtin_sql_generator.py:277`). Both use `context.combined_query` (the driver) and the
  **anchor** string (discover — which may be the editor SQL), so during error recovery / refinement the
  two group contexts can differ; the driver's version is what reaches the prompt.
- Group members become `ScoredObject`s with `score = float(g.get("score") or 0.5)`
  (`:206-209`) — note `or`, so a group score of exactly `0.0` becomes `0.5`. `schema`/`object` are
  split by `_split` (`:325-330`): brackets stripped, split on the first `.`, default schema `dbo`.
- If **any** merged object matches a member key, the branch becomes `group_anchored` (`:229-231`).

Group index build source: `skills/data-sources/<name>/data-groups/.data-group-index.json`
(`stores/skills_folder.py:146-191`). Each entry is upserted through `DataGroupStore.upsert`
(`data_group_store.py:19-55`), which writes one `data_group_metadata` row and one
`data_group_vectors_cache` row containing three embeddings:

| Vector column | Embedded text |
|---|---|
| `semantic_vector_json` | `description or group_name` |
| `functional_vector_json` | `" ".join(keywords)` |
| `object_vector_json` | `" ".join(members)` |

`group_id` defaults to `f"[{source_id}].[{group_name}]"`.

---

### 06.3 Stage-C exits that precede `discover` (branch completeness)

These three checks run before Stage D retrieval and produce branches that never reach `discover`
(`builtin_sql_generator.py:182-246`). Re-implement them or `kb_exact` / `precomputed_exact` will be
unreachable.

| Order | Call | Condition | Branch | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `engine.kb_exact(effective_query)` → `stores.fewshots.try_get_exact` | normalized-question equality on the `few_shots` table | `kb_exact` | Vector-free scan; skips rows with empty SQL; `score=1.0`, `is_exact_match=True` |
| 2 | `engine.precomputed_exact(...)` → `vector_search.try_get_precomputed_exact` | `question_lookup_key(row.question) == question_lookup_key(query)` **and** `status in {"Approved","Modified"}` | `precomputed_exact` | `score=1.0`, `is_exact_match=True`, carries `smq_query`; semantic mode compiles the SMQ instead of returning stored SQL |
| 3 | `engine.kb_vector_top1(...)` → `fewshots.search(query, top_k=1, max_distance=0.35)` | hit exists **and** `hit.score <= KbExactMatchThreshold` (0.05) | `kb_exact` | `score` is cosine distance |

All three are suppressed when `preserve_filters` is true:
`context.is_refinement and bool(context.active_filters)` (`:183`) — a stored answer authored without
the inherited filter must not satisfy the turn (`tests/parity/test_refinement_scope_expansion.py:125-143`).

`question_lookup_key` = `re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.strip().lower())` (`hashing.py:30-36`).

---

### 06.4 `discover` — complete control flow and branch decision tree

`DiscoveryEngine.discover(query, analysis, pins=None, table_override=None, top_k=8, existing_sql=None)`
(`discovery_engine.py:133-247`). `top_k` comes from `request.top_k` (default 8,
`preprocessing.py:61`).

#### 06.4.1 Step 0 — `table_override` short-circuit

```python
if table_override:
    objects = [ScoredObject(schema_name=self._split(n)[0],
                            object_name=self._split(n)[1],
                            score=1.0, priority=True, required=True)
               for n in table_override]
    return DiscoveryResult(objects=objects, branch=DiscoveryBranch.TABLE_OVERRIDE)
```

`table_override` is `request.table_override` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:261`), from the HTTP
`table_override` field (`preprocessing.py:54`, `:65`). Properties to preserve:

- No retrieval, no KB lookup, no cache read **or write**, no `query_analysis`, no
  `active_groups`, no `value_mappings`, no cap on the object count.
- Every object gets `score=1.0`, `priority=True`, `required=True`.
- `_split` strips `[`/`]` and splits on the first `.`; an unqualified name becomes `dbo.<name>`.
- Empty strings in `table_override` produce `dbo.` objects (no validation) — the driver passes the
  list through unvalidated (`preprocessing.py:54`).

#### 06.4.2 Step 1 — cache lookup

```python
cache_key = discovery_cache_key(analysis.entities or [query], analysis.complexity, top_k, analysis.extracted_columns)
if cache_key in self._discovery_cache:
    return self._discovery_cache[cache_key].model_copy(deep=True)
```

`discovery_cache_key` (`hashing.py:39-50`):

```
entity_part = ",".join(sorted(lowercase of each non-empty as_text_token(entity)))
key         = f"{entity_part}|{complexity}|{top_k}"
if extracted_columns:
    cols = ",".join(sorted(lowercase of each non-empty as_text_token(col)))
    key = f"{key}|cols:{sha256_text(cols)}"
```

Key facts: entities are sorted and lowercased; `top_k` participates; extracted columns are hashed
(SHA-256 hex) and prefixed `cols:`; when `entities` is empty the caller substitutes `[query]`; the
cache key **does not contain the raw query** when entities exist, so two different questions with the
same entities/complexity/top_k/columns share a cached DiscoveryResult. Cache writes happen only in
`_remember` (`:332-336`), i.e. never for `table_override`.

#### 06.4.3 Step 2 — collect the three pre-branch signals

```python
kb_hits        = self.stores.fewshots.search(query, top_k=3, max_distance=KbScoreThreshold)   # 0.35
best_kb        = kb_hits[0] if kb_hits else None
column_objects = self.discover_with_column_evidence(query, analysis)
precomputed    = self.stores.vector_search.search_precomputed(query)
```

`fewshots.search` (`fewshot_vector_service.py:114-133`) embeds the query and calls
`provider.search_vector("few_shots", source_id, vector, top_k=3, min_score=0.35)`. Both provider
implementations treat `min_score` as a **maximum cosine distance** filter
(`sqlite_vec_provider.py:171-173`, `milvus_provider.py:272-274`). Each hit becomes
`FewShotExample(question, sql, score=float(_distance or 1.0), is_exact_match = score <= KbExactMatchThreshold,
source="few_shot")`.

`VectorSearchService.search_precomputed` (`vector_search_service.py:110-147`): loads
`vec_data_group_query_vectors_cache`, joins against `vec_data_group_queries`, keeps only
`status == "Approved"`, computes `cosine_similarity` of the cached question vector, sorts descending,
takes `top_k=PrecomputedQueryTopK` (3), and sets
`is_exact_match = sim >= precomputed_direct_match_threshold()` (default 0.93,
`config.py:56`). `smq_query` is carried through. `score` here is a **similarity** (higher = better),
the opposite convention from the few-shot list.

#### 06.4.4 Step 3 — decision tree (faithful to the code)

```
best_kb and (1.0 - best_kb.score) >= 0.70:                 # i.e. distance <= 0.30
    confidence = 1.0 - best_kb.score if best_kb.score <= 1 else best_kb.score
    if best_kb.score <= 0.30 or confidence >= 0.70:
        tables = _objects_from_sql(best_kb.sql)
        return DiscoveryResult(objects = tables or column_objects,
                               branch  = "kb_direct",
                               few_shot_examples = [best_kb],
                               query_analysis = analysis)           # NO cap, NO pins, cached

if best_kb:                                                # distance in (0.30, 0.35]
    merged = merge_and_dedup(_objects_from_sql(best_kb.sql) + column_objects)
    return DiscoveryResult(objects = merged[:8],
                           branch  = "kb_gap_fill",
                           few_shot_examples = [best_kb],
                           query_analysis = analysis)              # NO pins, cached

# ---- no usable KB hit ----
schema_list   = vector_search.search_objects(query, top_k=top_k)
value_objects = for each fv in analysis.filter_values:
                    for hit in values.search(fv, top_k=5):
                        ScoredObject(schema_name = hit.schema_name or "dbo",
                                     object_name = hit.table_name or "",
                                     score       = 0.80,
                                     matched_columns = [hit.column_name] if present,
                                     required    = True)
fewshot_objects = concat(_objects_from_sql(ex.sql) for ex in kb_hits)      # up to 3 examples
group_ctx      = resolve_active_data_groups(query)
group_objects  = for g in group_ctx.top_groups:
                    for member in g.members:
                        ScoredObject(split(member).schema, split(member).object,
                                     score = float(g.score or 0.5))
bm25_list      = bm25.rank(query, schema_list + column_objects)            # [] when disabled

merged = rrf_merge({"schema_vector": schema_list,
                    "value_index":   value_objects,
                    "few_shot":      fewshot_objects,
                    "data_group":    group_objects,
                    "bm25":          bm25_list},
                   max_results = 8)
merged = merge_and_dedup(merged + column_objects)
if pins:
    merged = merge_and_dedup([ScoredObject(split(p).schema, split(p).object,
                                           score=1.0, priority=True, required=True) for p in pins] + merged)

branch = "dual_prong"
member_keys = set(group_ctx.member_groups.keys())
if any(f"{o.schema_name}.{o.object_name}".lower() in member_keys
       or o.object_name.lower() in member_keys for o in merged):
    branch = "group_anchored"

examples = list(precomputed[:3])
if examples and examples[0].score >= precomputed_few_shot_threshold() and not examples[0].is_exact_match:
    branch = f"precomputed_related/{branch}"

return DiscoveryResult(objects = merged[:8],
                       branch  = branch,
                       few_shot_examples = examples,
                       active_groups = group_ctx,
                       query_analysis = analysis,
                       value_mappings = [ {value, table, column}
                                          for fv in analysis.filter_values
                                          for v in values.search(fv, top_k=3) ])   # cached
```

#### 06.4.5 Branch reference (exact label strings)

| Branch constant | String | Produced by | Object set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DiscoveryBranch.KB_EXACT` | `kb_exact` | Stage C (06.3) | stored SQL returned, no discovery |
| `DiscoveryBranch.PRECOMPUTED_EXACT` | `precomputed_exact` | Stage C (06.3) | stored SQL / compiled SMQ |
| `DiscoveryBranch.TABLE_OVERRIDE` | `table_override` | `discover` step 0 | override names only, uncapped |
| `DiscoveryBranch.KB_DIRECT` | `kb_direct` | `discover` | tables from the matched SQL, else column evidence; uncapped |
| `DiscoveryBranch.KB_GAP_FILL` | `kb_gap_fill` | `discover` | SQL tables ∪ column evidence, capped 8 |
| `DiscoveryBranch.DUAL_PRONG` | `dual_prong` | `discover` | RRF top 8 + column evidence + pins |
| `DiscoveryBranch.GROUP_ANCHORED` | `group_anchored` | `discover` | same as dual_prong, analytics label |
| `DiscoveryBranch.PRECOMPUTED_RELATED_PREFIX` | `precomputed_related/` | `precomputed_related(base)` (`branch_taxonomy.py:78-79`) | prefix applied over `dual_prong` / `group_anchored` |
| `DiscoveryBranch.REFINEMENT_PREFIX` | `refinement/` | `scenario_branch` (`branch_taxonomy.py:82-88`) | prefix, applied only in the driver |
| `DiscoveryBranch.DRILL_DOWN_PREFIX` | `drill_down/` | `scenario_branch` | prefix |
| `DiscoveryBranch.NO_DISCOVERY` | `no_discovery` | provided-code path | none |
| `DiscoveryBranch.PRIORITY_VALIDATION_FAILED` | `priority_validation_failed` | pin validation failure | failure candidates |
| `DiscoveryBranch.APP_FEATURE` / `OFF_TOPIC` | `app_feature` / `off_topic` | conversational exits | none |

Prefix composition order: `discover` writes `precomputed_related/dual_prong`, then the driver applies
`scenario_branch` on refinement/drill-down turns, yielding
`refinement/precomputed_related/dual_prong`. Scenario prefixes are applied **only** inside
`if context.is_refinement and context.request.existing_code:` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:267-276`),
so a fresh-start dual_prong turn keeps the bare label.

#### 06.4.6 Extracting tables from a matched few-shot SQL (verified: regex, not a parser)

`_objects_from_sql` (`discovery_engine.py:316-323`):

```python
from app.utils.sql_normalization import extract_sql_object_refs
objs = []
for ref in extract_sql_object_refs(sql):
    schema, name = self._split(ref)
    objs.append(ScoredObject(schema_name=schema, object_name=name, score=0.9))
return objs
```

`extract_sql_object_refs` (`sql_normalization.py:54-68`) is **regex-based**, not a SQL parser:

```python
_SQL_IDENT        = r"(?:\[[^\]]+\]|[A-Za-z_][\w]*)"
_FROM_JOIN_OBJECT = re.compile(rf"(?is)\b(?:from|join)\s+({_SQL_IDENT}(?:\s*\.\s*{_SQL_IDENT})*)")
```

Rules: only `FROM` and `JOIN` introduce objects (not `INTO`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/CTE names); bracketed
identifiers support spaces (`[Order Details]`); 1–3 part names allowed and only the **last two** parts
are kept (`"db.dbo.Orders"` → `"dbo.Orders"`); a bare name stays bare and `_split` defaults it to
`dbo`; de-duplication is case-insensitive on the qualified string; ordering follows textual order.
Objects get `score=0.9`, `object_type="Table"` (default), no `matched_columns`, `priority=False`,
`required=False`.

Fallbacks when that yields nothing:

| Branch | Fallback |
|---|---|
| `kb_direct` | `objects = tables or column_objects` — an empty regex result silently falls back to column evidence |
| `kb_gap_fill` | union degenerates to just the column-evidence objects; a KB hit whose SQL has no `FROM`/`JOIN` therefore contributes only `few_shot_examples` |
| `dual_prong` | few-shot objects contribute zero objects; the remaining four signals still apply |

#### 06.4.7 Pins

- Pins are `request.database_objects`, already validated/normalized in Stage B by
  `ObjectNameResolver` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:118-131`).
- They are added **only** in the `dual_prong` branch, after `merge_and_dedup(merged + column_objects)`,
  by prepending `ScoredObject(score=1.0, priority=True, required=True)` and re-running
  `merge_and_dedup` (`:222-227`).
- `kb_direct` and `kb_gap_fill` **ignore pins entirely** (early return before `:222`).
- `merge_and_dedup` keeps the higher score, so a pin (1.0) beats a column-evidence copy (≤1.0, and
  strictly greater comparison means a 1.0 column object keeps the pin only if the pin is first — the
  pin is first, so on a tie the pin survives as the incumbent). See 06.6.3.
- Because the final slice is `merged[:8]` (`:236`), a low-ranked pin is never dropped by the cap only
  because the pin list is prepended; the tied tail of the merged list is what can be cut.

---

### 06.5 Column evidence (`discover_with_column_evidence`)

`discovery_engine.py:249-289`. This function is the reason a question that mentions a *value*
(`"chocolate"`) or a *column* (`Quantity`) can pull in a table the pure schema vector missed.

#### 06.5.1 Value-index seeds

For every `filter_value` (LLM-extracted), call `stores.values.search(fv, top_k=5)`.

`ValueIndexService.search` (`value_index_service.py:41-53`) — **no vectors, no scoring**:

```python
needle = (query or "").strip().lower()
if not needle: return []
rows = self.provider.fetch_all("value_index", self.source_id)[:fetch_cap]     # fetch_cap = 16384
hits = []
for row in rows:
    plain = (row.get("plain_value") or "").lower()
    if needle in plain: hits.append(row)
    if len(hits) >= top_k: break
return hits[:top_k]
```

Semantics that must be reproduced exactly:

- The needle is the **whole filter value**, lowercased and stripped — the analyzer does no
  tokenization at this stage; multi-word filter values only match as a contiguous substring.
- Match is `needle in plain_value` — a **substring** test, not equality, not prefix. `"1997"` matches
  `"northwind 1997"` and `"1997-01-01"`.
- `plain_value` is written at upsert time as `(value or "").lower()` (`:32`); the search lowercases
  again defensively.
- Ordering is **provider row order** (SQLite: `SELECT * … WHERE data_source_id = ?`; Milvus:
  `query(..., limit=16384, consistency_level="Strong")`), so hits are effectively arbitrary among
  matches — there is no relevance ordering and no dedup by table.
- `fetch_cap` defaults to `16384` and truncates the scanned row set; the early `break` at `top_k`
  means at most 5 hits are examined per filter value.

Seed assembly (`:252-264`):

```python
key = f"{hit.get('schema_name')}|{hit.get('table_name')}".lower()
obj = objects.get(key) or ScoredObject(schema_name=hit.get("schema_name") or "dbo",
                                       object_name=hit.get("table_name") or "",
                                       score=ColumnDetailValueSeedScore)      # 0.80
col = hit.get("column_name")
if col and col not in obj.matched_columns: obj.matched_columns.append(col)
obj.required = True
objects[key] = obj
```

Notes: the de-duplication key is `schema|table` lowercased with **no data-source component** (contrast
with `ScoredObject.merge_key`, 06.6.2); case is preserved in the stored `schema_name`/`object_name`
(the first hit wins); a hit without `table_name` creates an object with `object_name=""`; the seed
score is a flat 0.80 for every hit; `required=True` immediately; `object_type` stays the default
`"Table"`.

`value_index` rows are produced by the admin Excel loader: required columns
`value, schema_name, table_name, column_name`, `value` stringified/stripped, de-duplicated on
`(value, schema_name, table_name, column_name)`, empty values dropped, inserted in batches of 100
(`admin_service.py:550-608`). Each row also stores an embedding of `value`, but the search never uses it.

#### 06.5.2 Column-entity vector search

```python
threshold = effective_object_search_threshold()          # settings.OBJECT_SEARCH_VECTOR_SCORE_THRESHOLD, clamped [0,1]; default 0.50
if analysis.extracted_columns:
    for col in analysis.extracted_columns:
        hits = stores.vector_search.search_columns_scored(col, top_k=20, min_score=threshold)
        self._merge_column_hits(objects, hits)
else:
    hits = stores.vector_search.search_columns_scored(query, top_k=100, min_score=threshold)
    self._merge_column_hits(objects, hits)
```

`search_columns_scored` (`vector_search_service.py:79-90`): embeds the text, calls
`provider.search_vector("schemas", source_id, vector, top_k=top_k, min_score=threshold,
filter_fn=lambda r: (r.get("entity_type") or "") == "Column")`, and returns the **raw hit dicts**
(each carrying `_distance`).

| Mode | Calls | Provider `limit` | Filter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extracted_columns` non-empty | one per column | 20 each | `entity_type == "Column"`, distance ≤ 0.50 |
| `extracted_columns` empty (incl. skip path) | one for the whole query | 100 | same |

Budgets to keep identical: 20 hits per extracted column (max 20 columns → ≤ 400 column hits) versus
100 hits for the single whole-query search; the per-column loop does one embedding per column, so
`EMBEDDING` cost scales with `len(extracted_columns)` (mitigated by the L1/L2 embedding cache).

#### 06.5.3 `_merge_column_hits` — parent roll-up, score, and the 85% relative filter

`discovery_engine.py:291-314` verbatim behaviour:

```python
by_parent = {}
for hit in hits:
    if (hit.get("entity_type") or "") != "Column": continue        # redundant with filter_fn
    key = f"{hit.get('schema_name')}|{hit.get('object_name')}".lower()
    score = 1.0 - float(hit.get("_distance") or 1.0)               # similarity, higher = better
    by_parent.setdefault(key, []).append((score, hit))

for key, items in by_parent.items():
    best = max(s for s, _ in items) if items else 0
    obj = objects.get(key) or ScoredObject(schema_name=items[0][1].get("schema_name") or "dbo",
                                           object_name=items[0][1].get("object_name") or "",
                                           score=best,
                                           vector_score=1.0 - best)
    for score, hit in items:
        if best and score < best * RelativeColumnScoreThreshold:    # 0.85
            continue
        col = hit.get("column_name")
        if col and col not in obj.matched_columns:
            obj.matched_columns.append(col)
    obj.required = True
    objects[key] = obj
```

Fidelity points:

- `_distance` is cosine distance from the provider (SQLite: `1 - cosine_similarity`; Milvus:
  `milvus_score_to_cosine_distance`). `or 1.0` means a missing/`0` distance is treated as `1.0`
  (similarity 0).
- New (column-only) objects are **synthesized** with `score = best column similarity` and
  `vector_score = 1 - best` (i.e. `vector_score` stores the *distance* here, whereas the field name
  suggests a similarity — preserve as-is). `object_type` defaults to `"Table"`; the real parent type is
  not available on a column hit.
- If the object **already exists** (a value-index seed, or a schema-vector roll-up), neither `score`
  nor `vector_score` is updated — the 0.80 seed survives and only `matched_columns` grow. This is a
  real behavioural quirk: a value-seeded parent keeps 0.80 even if a column hit scored 0.99.
- The **relative-score filter (0.85)**: within one parent, a column whose similarity is below
  `best * 0.85` is dropped. `if best` guards a `best == 0` parent (then every column is kept).
  `RelativeColumnScoreThreshold = 0.85` (`constants.py:46`).
- `required = True` is set for every parent that got at least one column hit (after the filter) and
  also for parents whose columns were all filtered out.
- Column order: hit order from the provider (descending similarity for SQLite/Milvus), de-duplicated
  by exact column name (case-sensitive).

#### 06.5.4 The no-op keyword pass and the +0.15 boost

```python
tokens = [t for t in query.replace(",", " ").split() if t]
for obj in list(objects.values()):
    for tok in tokens:
        if tok.lower() in " ".join(obj.matched_columns).lower():
            obj.score = min(ApplyColumnBoostCap, obj.score + KeywordMatchScore * 0)

for obj in objects.values():
    if obj.matched_columns:
        obj.score = min(ApplyColumnBoostCap, obj.score + ApplyColumnBoost)
        obj.required = True
        # relative filter placeholder — keep all matched
        obj.matched_columns = obj.matched_columns
```

- **The keyword pass is a no-op**: `KeywordMatchScore * 0` multiplies the `1.0` constant by zero.
  Reproduce it (or drop it) but do not "fix" it into a real boost — behaviour must match.
- The boost: **+0.15** (`ApplyColumnBoost`) applied once per object that has ≥1 matched column,
  capped at **1.0** (`ApplyColumnBoostCap`), and `required` is set again. Applied to value-index seeds
  too, so a value seed with columns ends at `min(1.0, 0.80 + 0.15) = 0.95`, and a strong column-only
  parent can reach 1.0.
- The inner loop is a deliberate placeholder: the relative filter is implemented in `_merge_column_hits`,
  not here.
- Return order = Python dict insertion order: value-index seeds first (in the order the filter values
  and hits arrived), then column-only parents in first-seen order.

### 06.6 RRF fusion

#### 06.6.1 Formula and constants

```python
def rrf_score(rank: int, weight: float, k: float = RrfK) -> float:
    return weight * (1.0 / (k + rank + 1))          # rrf.py:33-34
```

| Constant | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `RrfK` (`k`) | `60.0` | `constants.py:23` |
| `RRF_WEIGHT_VALUE_INDEX` | `1.0` | `constants.py:24` |
| `RRF_WEIGHT_FEW_SHOT` | `1.0` | `constants.py:25` |
| `RRF_WEIGHT_SCHEMA_VECTOR` | `1.0` | `constants.py:26` |
| `RRF_WEIGHT_DATA_GROUP` | `2.0` | `constants.py:27` |
| `RRF_WEIGHT_BM25_DEFAULT` | `0.5` | `constants.py:28` |
| `MaxRerankTables` | `8` | `constants.py:29` |

`rank` is the **0-based** index in the list, so rank 0 contributes `weight / 61`, not `weight / 60`.
`default_weights()` (`rrf.py:25-30`) copies the dictionary and replaces `bm25` with
`float(settings.BM25_WEIGHT)` (default 0.5, `config.py:60`) — the other four are constants and are
**not** runtime-configurable.

Nominal range of a fused score: a single top-1 hit in one list is `2.0/61 ≈ 0.0328`; the maximum for
an object present at rank 0 in all five lists is
`(2.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 + 0.5)/61 ≈ 0.0902`.

#### 06.6.2 Lists, ranks, and the merge key

The five lists passed by `discover` (`:211-220`) and their ordering:

| List name | Weight | Source | Ordering |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_vector` | 1.0 | `vector_search.search_objects(query, top_k=top_k)` | `score` descending (similarity) |
| `value_index` | 1.0 | one per filter value, `values.search(fv, top_k=5)`, flat score 0.80 | filter-value order, then provider row order |
| `few_shot` | 1.0 | `_objects_from_sql` over up to 3 KB hits, flat 0.9 | KB-hit order, then SQL textual order |
| `data_group` | 2.0 | top-3 groups × their members | group rank, then member order |
| `bm25` | `BM25_WEIGHT` | `bm25.rank(query, schema_list + column_objects)` | BM25 score descending (or `[]`) |

`ScoredObject.merge_key()` (`models/pipeline.py:193-196`):

```python
stripped = self.object_name.split(" (Segment")[0].strip()
ds = self.data_source or ""
return f"{ds}|{self.schema_name}|{stripped}".lower()
```

- The `"(Segment N)"` suffix is stripped before keying: `Orders (Segment 2)` and `Orders` are the same
  entity. The split is on the literal `" (Segment"` (leading space, no closing paren), so
  `Orders (Segment 2)` → `Orders` and `Orders (Segment2)` → `Orders (Segment2)` (no space → no strip).
  This exists so drill-down segment objects never double-count in RRF.
- `data_source` participates: `None` and `""` both produce an empty prefix, so the current engine —
  which never sets `data_source` on discovered objects — effectively scopes by `schema|object` only.
  Two objects from different sources with the same schema/object name **would** collide today
  (all `data_source=None`). Reproduce the formula; do not add scoping.
- The schema itself is not segment-stripped and is lowercased along with everything else.

#### 06.6.3 `rrf_merge` semantics

`rrf.py:37-71`:

1. `weights = weights or default_weights()` — callers in Stage D pass no weights, so BM25's weight is
   read from settings at call time.
2. For each list (iterated in the caller's dictionary order) and each 0-based `rank`:
   `scores[key] += rrf_score(rank, weight, k)`.
3. First occurrence of a key stores a `model_copy(deep=True)`; later occurrences are merged **into the
   existing copy**:
   - if the later object has `matched_columns`, the union (existing first, then new, order-preserving)
     is written back and `required` is forced to `True`;
   - `priority` is OR-ed; `required` is OR-ed;
   - `markdown` is copied only when the existing object has none.
   Fields **not** merged: `object_type`, `description`, `vector_score`, `data_source`, `score`
   (later overwritten anyway) — the first occurrence wins for all of them.
4. Sort: `sorted(objects.values(), key=lambda o: scores[o.merge_key()], reverse=True)`.
   Python's sort is stable, so **ties keep dictionary insertion order**, which is the list order of the
   first `ranked_lists` iteration: `schema_vector` → `value_index` → `few_shot` → `data_group` → `bm25`.
   There is no secondary key (no score tiebreak, no alphabetical tiebreak).
5. `obj.score = scores[obj.merge_key()]` for every object in the ranked list — **the RRF score
   overwrites** the original similarity/0.80/0.9 values for every object that survives fusion.
6. `return ranked[:max_results]` (`max_results=MaxRerankTables` = 8 in Stage D).

Missing scores are simply absent contributions: a list that is `[]` (BM25 disabled) adds nothing; an
object present in only one list keeps its single contribution; there is no default/backfill score and
no minimum-score filter inside `rrf_merge`.

#### 06.6.4 `merge_and_dedup` semantics

`rrf.py:74-93`. Used three times in Stage D (`:179`, `:221`, `:227`) and once in recovery
(`attempts.py:555-558`).

```python
unique = {}
for obj in objects:
    key = obj.merge_key()
    existing = unique.get(key)
    if existing is None:
        unique[key] = obj.model_copy(deep=True); continue
    if obj.score > existing.score:
        cols = list(dict.fromkeys(obj.matched_columns + existing.matched_columns))
        obj = obj.model_copy(deep=True)
        obj.matched_columns = cols
        unique[key] = obj                      # replaces value, keeps dict position
    else:
        for col in obj.matched_columns:
            if col not in existing.matched_columns: existing.matched_columns.append(col)
        existing.priority = existing.priority or obj.priority
        existing.required = existing.required or obj.required
return list(unique.values())
```

- **Merge key**: identical to RRF (`data_source|schema|object-name-minus-"(Segment …)"`, lowercased).
- **Winner**: strictly higher `score` wins and absorbs the loser's matched columns (winner's columns
  first). Equal scores keep the **first** object (no replacement).
- When the winner replaces the value, the dictionary **position is preserved**, so the output order is
  first-seen order, not score order. `merge_and_dedup` never sorts and never caps.
- Loser fields are otherwise ignored on replacement (no OR-ing of `priority`/`required` in the
  replacement branch) — this is why the driver prepends pins rather than appending them.
- Consequence for `dual_prong`: `merge_and_dedup(merged + column_objects)` replaces RRF objects whose
  RRF score (~0.016–0.09) is below the column-evidence score (≥0.80) with the column-evidence copy —
  unioning columns, but **losing the RRF object's `object_type`/`description`** (the column evidence
  object defaults to `Table` and carries no description). Order still follows the RRF ranking.

#### 06.6.5 `max_rerank_tables`, pinning, and the 5% floor

Three different caps/order-keeping rules exist; keep them separate:

| Mechanism | Where | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| RRF result cap | `rrf_merge(..., max_results=8)` (`:219`) | top 8 by fused score |
| Final object cap | `objects=merged[:MaxRerankTables]` (`:236`) | first 8 in post-`merge_and_dedup` insertion order (RRF order first, then column-only extras) |
| Uncapped branches | `table_override` (`:142-153`), `kb_direct` (`:170-176`) | no slice at all |
| Pin pinning | `merge_and_dedup(pin_objs + merged)` (`:222-227`) | pins first ⇒ they keep position and win ties/score |
| Required/priority slot pinning | `SqlContextHydrator.cap_objects` (`sql_context_hydrator.py:25-41`) | required/priority/column-matched/SemanticModel objects are emitted **first**, before the cap is applied |
| 5% score floor | `cap_objects` (`:29-31`) | for non-required objects, `floor = best * 0.05`; objects with `score < floor` are dropped; `best == 0` ⇒ floor 0 |

The 5% floor is computed **only over the `rest` list** (non-required objects), and `cap_objects`
returns `required + rest` de-duplicated by `merge_key` and truncated to `self.cap` (8, or 12 for
refinement). Because the required block occupies the front of the list, the cap truncates only the
tail — required objects are dropped only if they alone outnumber `self.cap` — and the floor can only
remove supplementary (non-required) objects.

---

### 06.7 Optional BM25 signal

`Bm25Service` (`bm25_service.py`), wired in `build_source_stores` with settings values
(`stores/bundle.py:59-63`).

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Enable flag | `settings.ENABLE_BM25_RETRIEVAL`, default **`False`** | `config.py:59` |
| Per-instance override | `enabled=` constructor arg (used by tests) | `bm25_service.py:14-22` |
| `k1` | `settings.BM25_K1`, default `1.2` | `config.py:61` |
| `b` | `settings.BM25_B`, default `0.75` | `config.py:62` |
| RRF weight | `settings.BM25_WEIGHT`, default `0.5` | `config.py:60`, `rrf.py:29` |
| Default `top_k` in `rank` | `8` | `bm25_service.py:45` |

Index build/source: there is **no persistent BM25 index**. `rank()` builds everything in memory from
the objects handed to it, so the corpus for Stage D is exactly `schema_list + column_objects`
(`discovery_engine.py:210`) — i.e. the vector-search parents plus the column-evidence parents. Objects
that only appear in the value-index seed list, the few-shot list, or the data-group list are **not**
ranked by BM25 (they are the same parents as `column_objects` in practice, so the loss is small).

Algorithm (`bm25_service.py:45-77`):

```python
if not self.enabled: return []
docs = list(objects)
if not docs: return []
tokenized = [self._tokens(f"{o.object_name} {o.description or ''}") for o in docs]   # "description" = embedding payload
avgdl = sum(len(t) for t in tokenized) / len(tokenized)
df = Counter(); for toks in tokenized: df.update(set(toks))
q_tokens = self._tokens(query)
for obj, toks in zip(docs, tokenized):
    score = 0.0; tf = Counter(toks); dl = len(toks) or 1
    for term in q_tokens:
        if term not in df: continue
        idf = math.log((len(docs) - df[term] + 0.5) / (df[term] + 0.5) + 1)
        freq = tf[term]
        score += idf * (freq * (k1 + 1.0)) / (freq + k1 * ((1.0 - b) + b * dl / avgdl))
    copy = obj.model_copy(deep=True); copy.score = score; scored.append(copy)
scored.sort(key=lambda o: o.score, reverse=True)
return scored[:top_k]
```

Tokenizer (verbatim): `[t.lower() for t in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", text or "")]`.

Notes to preserve: documents are `object_name + " " + description`, where `description` for a
vector-store parent is the embedding payload `"Entity: Table | Name: X | Description: …"` — so the
literal tokens `entity`, `table`, `name` are part of every document's term statistics. `score` is
overwritten on a deep copy, so the fused list carries BM25 scores into `rrf_merge` (which uses only
ranks, not scores). `idf` uses the `+1` smoothed form with `len(docs)` as `N`.

### 06.8 Object types and allowed schemas

#### 06.8.1 Object-type vocabulary and normalization

| Level | Allowed values | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `ScoredObject.object_type` | free string; engine default `"Table"`; `"SemanticModel"` for injected models | `models/pipeline.py:179`, `attempts.py:551` |
| Vector row `object_type` | `Table`, `View`, `Function` | `schema_contracts.normalize_object_type` (`:318-329`) |
| Vector row `entity_type` | parent rows: `Table` / `View` / `Function`; column rows: `"Column"` | `schema_rows.py:48`, `:66`; `skills_folder.py:121` |
| `table_type` on `TableSchema` | lowercase `table` / `view` / `function` | `object_type_to_table_type` (`:332-334`) |

`normalize_object_type` maps `table→Table`, `view→View`, `function→Function`,
`stored_procedure`/`storedprocedure→Function`, anything unknown → `Table`. Column-entity rows are the
only rows with `entity_type == "Column"`; `search_columns_scored` and `_merge_column_hits` both rely
on that exact string.

Stored-procedure / function discovery (used when scanning a live database to build the schemas
collection) lives in `app/services/object_discovery_service.py`:

- `discover_stored_procedures(engine, schema="dbo")` — `sys.procedures ⋈ sys.sql_modules`, one
  `DataObject` per procedure with `parameters` parsed by `parse_sp_parameters` (regex
  `CREATE [OR ALTER] PROCEDURE <name> (.*?) AS`, then
  `(@\w+)\s+([A-Z_]+(\s*\(\s*\d+(\s*,\s*\d+)?\s*\))?)\s*(=\s*([^,]+))?`) and description from
  `-- Description:` / `-- Purpose:` / `/* Description: … */` / `/* Purpose: … */`, space-collapsed,
  truncated to 500 chars (`:12-59`, `:142-181`, `:243-270`).
- `discover_functions(engine, schema="dbo")` — `sys.objects ⋈ sys.sql_modules` for types
  `FN`/`IF`/`TF`, return type from `sys.parameters` (parameter_id = 0) or
  `RETURNS (@var )?<type>` regex (`:62-123`, `:184-240`).
- `discover_all_schemas(engine)` — `sys.schemas` minus the fixed system/db-role list (`:126-139`).
- Markdown renderers `build_sp_markdown_description` / `build_function_markdown_description`
  (`:273-371`) emit the `## **Stored Procedure:** …` / `## **Function:** …` blocks that the skills
  folder stores and the hydrator later pastes.

Admin-side type filtering (`api/endpoints/admin.py:447-475`) dispatches a schema-scan request per
requested `ObjectType` (`TABLE`, `VIEW`, `STORED_PROCEDURE`, `FUNCTION`);
`vector_store.search_objects_v2(object_types=[...])` compares
`{normalize_object_type(t)} | {t.lower()}` against the hit's `object_type`
(`vector_store.py:415-428`). Stage D itself does **not** filter by object type anywhere.

#### 06.8.2 Allowed schemas

- `DiscoveryResult.allowed_schemas` exists (`models/pipeline.py:265`) but is **never written** by the
  Python port — `grep` finds only its declaration.
  > ⚠️ Unverified: any intended population of `allowed_schemas`. Treat it as a dead field unless the
  > re-implementation chooses to fill it; nothing reads it today.
- The effective allow-list at validation time is derived from the discovered objects:
  `allowed = [f"{o.schema_name}.{o.object_name}" for o in discovery.objects]`
  (`attempts.py:325`) and passed to `SqlValidator.validate(sql, allowed)`
  (`attempts.py:332`, `:368`, `:508`, `:517`). Any `FROM`/`JOIN` reference outside that list produces
  `"TABLE_VALIDATION_ERROR: <refs>"` (`sql_validator.py:59-70`), which Stage E then turns into a
  recovery expansion (06.11). So **the object list produced by Stage D is the schema allow-list**.
- The legacy helpers `_get_allowed_table_set` (`generation_service.py:173-193`,
  `discovery_service.py:34-54`) build a `{"schema.table"}` set from a source's object list and keep
  only `object_type in {"table","view"}` — functions and procedures are excluded there. Those helpers
  are used by the legacy wrapper, not by Stage D.

#### 06.8.3 Legacy "heuristic → LLM → keyword fallback" order

This ladder exists only on the pre-orchestrator paths; keep it out of the built-in Stage D but preserve
it if the port must also serve `BUILTIN_SQL_GENERATOR=false`.

1. **Heuristic/keyword first** — `skills_service.search_objects_by_keyword(query, top_k=20)` (index
   JSON scoring: object name +3.0, keyword +2.0, description +1.0, ×1.5 schema-match bonus, ×1.2
   Function boost; scores converted to a distance-like value via
   `max(0.1, 3.0 - skill_score * 0.3)`), then Milvus `search_schemas(query, top_k=10)` contributing a
   flat `0.5` per hit with a `SCORE_THRESHOLD` of `1.2` when any skills score `< 1.0`, else `2.0`
   (`generation_service.py:674-750`).
2. **LLM next** — KB exact-match validation: top few-shot with L2 distance ≤ `0.1`, then
   `llm_service.chat(validation_prompt, temperature=0)` asking "Respond with only: YES or NO", and
   table extraction via `llm_service.extract_tables_from_sql([sql])`
   (`discovery_service.py:374-469`). `validate_groups_with_llm` is a stub that returns its input
   unchanged (`:810-829`) — there is no group validation today.
3. **Keyword fallback last** — when the vector pass produced nothing, tokenize the query with
   `\b\w{3,}\b`, drop the built-in stop-word list
   (`the, and, for, are, but, not, you, all, can, had, her, was, one, our, out, has, have, been, find,
   get, show, list, what, which, where, how, top, best, most`), scan all tables and score
   `5.0 - 0.5 * matches` for `matches > 0` (`generation_service.py:770-798`).

Legacy reranking (for reference only): `skills +10`, `value_index +8`, `knowledge_base +5`,
cumulative by normalized `(schema, table)` key (`discovery_service.py:572-640`); smart-threshold
decision triggers user selection when `(cross_schema or cross_database) and n >= 5`, or `n >= 10`, or
`n < 3` (`:643-700`).

### 06.9 Hydration (`SqlContextHydrator` + skills-folder markdown)

Entry: `builtin_sql_generator.py:279-292`. `SqlContextHydrator(token_budget=6400, cap=8)`, with
`cap=RefinementPromptContextCap` (12) for refinement/drill-down turns.

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| `SchemaContextTokenBudget` | `6_400` (`constants.py:33`) |
| `PromptContextDiscoveryCap` | `8` (`constants.py:34`) |
| `RefinementPromptContextCap` | `12` (`constants.py:37`) |

#### 06.9.1 Markdown payload lookup from the skills folder

`markdown_lookup_for_objects(source_id, objects)` (`stores/skills_folder.py:228-248`):

1. Resolve the folder by `source_id`: scan `skills/data-sources/**/_data-source.md` for a
   `(?im)^source_id:\s*['\"]?([^\s'\"#]+)['\"]?` match (case-insensitive compare); else try
   `skills/data-sources/<source_id>` when it contains `_data-source.md` or `schemas/`; else raise
   `FileNotFoundError` — which the loader swallows, returning an empty lookup
   (`:24-40`). Root default: `<repo>/skills/data-sources`
   (`default_data_sources_root`, `:20-21`).
2. For each object, `object_markdown_path(folder, schema, object, object_type)` (`:194-208`) tries,
   in order: `schemas/<schema>/<schema>.<object>.md`, `schemas/<schema>.<object>.md`,
   then a recursive `rglob`. For `object_type.lower() == "function"` the name
   `<schema>.fn.<object>.md` is tried **first**.
3. The file is read as UTF-8 with `errors="ignore"`.
4. On success, `lookup[f"{schema}.{object}".lower()] = text` **and** `obj.markdown = text` (mutating the
   discovered object). Failures are skipped (no empty-string entries).

Build side (for parity of file names): `rebuild_vectors_from_folder` (`:103-191`) parses object files
with `_parse_object_file` (`:251-260`; `schema.fn.name.md` → Function, `schema.name.md` → Table,
else parent-directory name) and columns with `_parse_columns` (`:263-269`; markdown table rows with
≥2 cells, header cells `column`/`name`/`column name` skipped).

#### 06.9.2 Token accounting

```python
def _estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    return max(1, len(text or "") // 4)          # sql_context_hydrator.py:12-13
```

A pure character-count estimate: 4 characters per token, floor of 1. No tokenizer is used, and no
per-object overhead is added. An empty body costs 1 token.

#### 06.9.3 `cap_objects` — slot selection

`sql_context_hydrator.py:25-41`:

```python
required = [o for o in objects if o.required or o.priority or o.matched_columns or o.object_type == "SemanticModel"]
rest     = [o for o in objects if o not in required]        # pydantic equality, not identity
if rest:
    best  = max((o.score for o in rest), default=0.0)
    floor = best * 0.05 if best else 0.0
    rest  = [o for o in rest if o.score >= floor]
merged = required + rest
# de-duplicate by merge_key(), first wins; then [: self.cap]
```

Rules to reproduce exactly:

1. An object is "required" if **any** of `required`, `priority`, `matched_columns` non-empty, or
   `object_type == "SemanticModel"`.
2. `rest` is computed with `o not in required`, which is **Pydantic value equality**, not identity — two
   distinct objects with identical fields collapse (both fall in `required`, neither in `rest`).
3. Floor = `best * 0.05` where `best` is the max score of `rest` (not of all objects); `best == 0`
   disables the floor; comparison is inclusive (`>=`).
4. Order = required block (input order preserved) then surviving `rest` (input order preserved). Input
   order is the discovery order (RRF rank order, then column-extras, with pins prepended).
5. De-duplication by `merge_key()` (so `(Segment N)` variants collapse *again* here), first occurrence
   wins; then `[:cap]` — 8, or 12 when the driver constructed the hydrator with the refinement cap.

#### 06.9.4 `build_contexts` — the four output slices

`sql_context_hydrator.py:43-88`. Returns
`(selected_object_context, supplementary_objects, schema_context, schema_context_for_validation)`,
each a `"\n\n"`-joined string.

For each capped object, in order:

```python
key  = f"{obj.schema_name}.{obj.object_name}".lower()
body = obj.markdown or markdown_lookup.get(key) or self._fallback_markdown(obj, dbms)
tokens = _estimate_tokens(body)
evidence = ""
if obj.matched_columns:
    cols = ", ".join(f"{quote_qualified(obj.schema_name, obj.object_name, dbms)}.{c}"
                     for c in obj.matched_columns)
    evidence = f"-- Matched column evidence: {cols}\n"
block = body if body.startswith("#") else f"## {obj.schema_name}.{obj.object_name}\n{body}"
```

| Condition | `selected_object_context` | `supplementary_objects` | `schema_context` | `schema_context_for_validation` | `used` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `obj.priority or obj.required` | `block` | — | `block` | `evidence + block` | `+= tokens` (no budget check) |
| `used + tokens <= 6400` | — | `block` | `block` | `evidence + block` | `+= tokens` |
| else (over budget) | — | `_prune_columns(block, obj.matched_columns)` | **omitted** | `evidence + pruned` | `+= tokens(pruned)` |

Critical asymmetry: an over-budget block is **never** added to `schema_context` (only to
`supplementary_objects` and `schema_context_for_validation`). The prompt uses
`discovery.schema_context or discovery.selected_object_context` for `AVAILABLE SCHEMAS`
(`prompts.py:102`, `:253`, `:364`, `:471`) and `discovery.supplementary_objects` for
`SUPPLEMENTARY SCHEMAS`, so an over-budget object can reach the model only through the supplementary
and validation slices. Required blocks ignore the budget entirely, so `used` can exceed 6400 and force
every subsequent non-required object down the pruning path.

Slice contracts:

| Slice | Contents | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `selected_object_context` | required/priority blocks only | fallback for `AVAILABLE SCHEMAS` |
| `supplementary_objects` | non-required blocks that fit, plus pruned over-budget blocks | `SUPPLEMENTARY SCHEMAS` |
| `schema_context` | selected + fitting supplementary | `AVAILABLE SCHEMAS` (primary) |
| `schema_context_for_validation` | every capped object as `evidence + block/pruned` | Stage E LLM critic (`attempts.py:344-350`) |

#### 06.9.5 Block shaping, evidence lines, and fallback markdown

- Heading rule: a body already starting with `#` is used verbatim; otherwise the hydrator prefixes
  `"## {schema}.{object}\n"` (unquoted, un-bracketed).
- `-- Matched column evidence` (`:60-66`) is synthesized only from `obj.matched_columns`, one line per
  object, columns comma-separated as `[schema].[object].[col]` under the default `dbms="SQL Server"`
  (`quote_identifier` → `[...]`; MySQL → backticks; everything else → `"..."`,
  `utils/dialect.py:6-19`). The *column* segment is appended raw, never quoted. The driver calls
  `build_contexts(...)` **without** a `dbms` argument (`builtin_sql_generator.py:286-288`), so the
  evidence lines always use SQL Server quoting even on other dialects.
- `_fallback_markdown` (`:90-98`) runs when neither `obj.markdown` nor the lookup has the object:
  - unwrap an embedding payload by splitting on `" | Description: "` and keeping the tail;
  - if the result starts with `#` or contains `"## Columns"`, return it as-is;
  - else return `"{quoted schema.object} ({object_type})\nColumns of interest: {cols}\n{desc}"`
    (the `Columns of interest` line only when matched columns exist).
  Tested by `tests/unit/test_sql_context_hydration.py:58-68`.

#### 06.9.6 Column pruning algorithm

`_prune_columns(markdown, keep)` (`:100-110`):

```python
if not keep:
    return "\n".join(markdown.splitlines()[:12])          # first 12 lines
keep_l = {c.lower() for c in keep}
kept = []
for line in markdown.splitlines():
    if line.strip().startswith("|") and not any(c in line.lower() for c in keep_l) and "name" not in line.lower():
        continue
    kept.append(line)
return "\n".join(kept)
```

- No matched columns → hard truncation to the first 12 lines (a header-only fragment in practice).
- With matched columns → drop markdown-table rows that mention none of them, but **always keep** rows
  containing the substring `name` (case-insensitive) anywhere — so header rows
  (`| Column | Type |`, `| Name | … |`) survive. Non-table lines are always kept; the heading and prose
  are never pruned. Matching is substring-on-lowercased-line, so `ID` also matches inside
  `void`, `paid`, etc.
- The pruned text is what gets token-counted into `used`.

Value mappings: `set_value_mappings(discovery.value_mappings)` is stored on the hydrator
(`:22-23`) but `build_contexts` **never reads `self.value_mappings`** — the `VERIFIED DATA MAPPINGS`
block is rendered by `prompts.py:79-82` directly from `discovery.value_mappings` as
`"- {value} → {table}.{column}"` lines (or `"(none)"`). Keep the setter for API compatibility; do not
expect it to affect the four slices.

#### 06.9.7 `schema_context_utils.py` — what it does, and why it is not on this path

`app/services/schema_context_utils.py` is a **legacy** shared helper module. Nothing in
`app/core/orchestrator/**` imports it (only `generation_service.py:2457-2458` and
`llm_service.py:517-538`, `:1172-1182` do). Documented here because the module is often mistaken for
part of hydration; if the port must also reproduce the legacy path, implement these exactly:

| Function | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `build_schema_text(schemas, use_table_override=False)` (`:17-60`) | `[VIEW]`/`[TABLE]` label via `_is_view`; per schema: `"{label} Table: {schema}.{name}\nDescription: {desc or 'No description'}\nColumns:"` then `"\n  - {col} ({type}){ [FK]}: {desc}"` per column or `"\n  (No columns defined)"`; `use_table_override` emits the raw description instead |
| `build_sufficiency_schema_text(schemas)` (`:63-94`) | `"{label} [{schema}].[{table}]: col (type), …"`; falls back to the description, then `"(no column information available)"` |
| `prioritize_base_tables(schemas)` (`:97-138`) | splits views/base tables; drops a view whose `_extract_base_name` name exists as a base table |
| `_is_view` (`:284-290`) | `table_type.upper() == 'VIEW'` or name ends `_vw` / `_view` / `view` |
| `_looks_like_fk` (`:293-296`) | ends with `id`, not exactly `id`, length > 2 |
| `_extract_base_name` (`:299-321`) | `^(.+?)_\d{4}$`, `^(.+?)_vw$`, `^(.+?)_view$`, `^(.+?)View$` |
| `generate_schema_id(schemas)` (`:141-160`) | SHA-256 of `"{schema}.{table}:{sorted col names}"` joined by a pipe character, sorted by table name, truncated to 16 hex chars |
| `has_datetime_columns` (`:163-184`) | any column type in `{datetime, datetime2, date, smalldatetime, timestamp, datetimeoffset, time}` |
| `get_derivation_guidance(code_type)` (`:187-253`) | fixed per-language (python/r/sas/sql) "DERIVABLE VALUES" text |
| `get_temporal_guidance(schemas)` (`:256-279`) | empty string unless datetime columns exist, else the fixed `### TEMPORAL DATA HANDLING` block |

### 06.10 Caches and invalidation

| Cache | Location | Key | Cap | Eviction | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Query analysis | `DiscoveryEngine._analysis_cache` | `f"{combined_query.strip()}\|{existing_code.strip()}"`, hashed when > 512 chars | `MaxQueryAnalysisCacheEntries = 100` | `clear()` on overflow; `clear_analysis_cache()` | one `DiscoveryEngine` (one request) |
| Discovery result | `DiscoveryEngine._discovery_cache` | `entities-sorted\|complexity\|top_k[\|cols:sha256]` | `MaxDiscoveryCacheEntries = 256` | full `clear()` when `len >= 256` before insert | one `DiscoveryEngine` |
| Object catalog | `database_catalog._cache` (module-level) | `source_id` | unbounded | TTL `CatalogCacheTtlSeconds = 300`; `list_objects(force=True)` bypasses | process |
| Embedding L1 | `stores/embeddings._l1` | `(data_source_id, sha256(f"{model}\|{text}"))` | `EmbeddingCacheL1Size = 512` | full `clear()` on overflow | process |
| Embedding L2 | `embedding_cache` collection | `sha256(f"{model}\|{text}")` per source | `EmbeddingCacheL2Size = 10_000` | delete `EmbeddingCacheL2EvictBatch = 1_000` oldest by `last_accessed_utc` | persistent |
| Source stores | `resolve_source_stores` (`stores/bundle.py:68-70`) | `source_id` | `lru_cache(maxsize=64)` | LRU | process |
| Relationship graph | `relationship_graph._graph_instance` | singleton | 1 | `invalidate_relationship_graph()` / `force_rebuild=True` | process |
| Vector provider | `provider_factory.get_vector_provider` | — | `lru_cache(maxsize=1)` | none (rebuild via `refresh_vector_store` in `vector_store.py:780-783`) | process |

Cache-key contents that must match the current behaviour:

- **Analysis key**: raw combined query + raw existing code for short turns; the whole query text is in
  the key, so no cross-question reuse. `combined_query` is
  `fold_conversation(request.query, history)` = `"{query}\nQ: … | A: …"` lines
  (`preprocessing.py:31-47`) — i.e. history is part of the key.
- **Discovery key**: entities (sorted, lowercased, comma-joined) + complexity + top_k; extracted
  columns are hashed into a `cols:` suffix. Query text itself is absent (unless entities are empty,
  in which case the caller substitutes `[query]`). `analysis.entities or [query]` is the only place the
  query enters.

Invalidation points in the current code:

| Point | Effect |
|---|---|
| `engine.clear_analysis_cache()` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:169`) | empties the analysis cache of the freshly built engine (effective no-op per request) |
| `_remember` overflow (`discovery_engine.py:332-336`) | full flush then insert |
| `analyze_query` overflow (`:115-116`) | full flush then insert |
| `DatabaseCatalog.list_objects(force=True)` | bypasses the 300 s TTL for one call; no global clear function exists |
| `invalidate_relationship_graph()` (`relationship_graph.py:180-184`) | drops the FK graph singleton (call after schema modifications) |
| `refresh_vector_store()` (`vector_store.py:780`) | drops the legacy `MilvusVectorStore` singleton |
| `import_skills_folder` / `rebuild_vectors_from_folder` (`skills_folder.py:95-106`) | wipes `schemas`, `data_group_*`, `vec_data_group_*` for the source and rebuilds |
| Schema sync / description edits | must call the two invalidation helpers above manually — Stage D has no automatic invalidation hook |
| New `DiscoveryEngine` per request | everything in the engine is discarded after the turn; there is **no** cross-request discovery cache today |
