### 11.4 Skills folder: layout, naming, and runtime lookup

#### 11.4.1 Layout and naming rules

```
skills/data-sources/
├── _index.md                                  # catalog: "### {Name}" sections
└── {slug}/
    ├── _data-source.md                        # YAML front matter (source_id) + metadata
    ├── .data-groups                           # "Group Name|_group-slug-group.md"
    ├── .schema-index.json
    ├── exclude_objects.txt                    # optional
    ├── vector-index.db                        # legacy; REJECTED on import
    ├── data-groups/
    │   ├── _{group-slug}-group.md
    │   ├── _{group-slug}-qas.md               # operator-visible Q&A sidecar
    │   └── .data-group-index.json             # consumed by rebuild_vectors_from_folder
    ├── schemas/{schema}/
    │   ├── {schema}.{object}.md               # tables AND views
    │   ├── {schema}.fn.{function}.md          # functions (fn. avoids collisions)
    │   └── .object-index.json
    └── tools/*.md                             # optional operator tools
```

* `{slug}` = `_slugify(name)` (lower-case, `[^\w\s-]` removed, spaces → hyphens).
* Group filename = `_{_slugify(group_name)}-group.md` (`skills_admin_service.py:374-375`, `schema_scan_service.py:612`).
* Group title line: `# {Group Name}` — `_parse_data_group_file` strips a trailing ` Group` from the title regex (`skills_service.py:287`).
* Table/view markdown filename = `{schema}.{object}.md`, function = `{schema}.fn.{function}.md` (`schema_scan_service.py:292,313`).
* Data-group object links are **relative** to the group file: `../schemas/{schema}/{file}` (`schema_scan_service.py:628`); `_parse_data_group_file` resolves them to absolute paths (`skills_service.py:304-309`).
* Slugs must never be `_`-prefixed: `load_object_indices` skips directories starting with `_` (`skills_service.py:809`).

#### 11.4.2 Per-object markdown (exact structure)

Table/view file, verbatim header + body (`schema_scan_service.py:575-584`):

```markdown
# {Table|View}: [{schema_name}].[{obj_name}]

**Data Source:** {data_source_name}
**Schema:** {schema_name}
**Type:** {Table|View}

## Description

{markdown_body}
```

where `{markdown_body}` is exactly the `build_table_markdown_description` block from §11.3.3 (blockquote description, `### **Columns:**` markdown table with `Ord | Name | Data Type | Description`).

Function file, verbatim from `build_function_markdown_description` (`object_discovery_service.py:341-371`) — **no** `# {Type}:` H1, the heading is an H2 with backticks:

````markdown
## **Function:** `[{schema}].[{name}]`
**Returns:** `{return_type}`          # omitted when no return type
> {description}                      # omitted when empty
---
### **Parameters:**
- `@param` (TYPE)

### **Usage:**
```sql
SELECT [{schema}].[{name}](@param = <value>)
```
---
````
With no parameters the usage line is `SELECT [s].[f]()` and the `### **Parameters:**` block is omitted.

**There is no YAML front matter in object files** — the only front matter in the tree is the `source_id` block in `_data-source.md`. Metadata lives in `**…:**` lines and in the `## Description` section.

`sync_schema_file_from_database(file_path)` (`schema_scan_service.py:436-508`) rebuilds one file: parse `…/data-sources/{slug}/schemas/{schema}/{schema}.{obj}[-fn.]{name}.md` (`:402-433`), introspect the live DB, build only the description+columns block, and splice it into the existing `## Description` section, preserving everything before and after (`_merge_description_section`, `:535-559`). If the file has no `## Description` section at all, the whole file is regenerated with `_build_object_markdown`. Afterwards `_data_sources_cache` and `_data_groups_cache` are cleared (`:500-506`). Endpoint: `POST /api/v1/admin/skills/sync-schema-markdown` with `{"file_path": "…"}` (`admin.py:1051-1070`).

Header validation regexes used to read files back (`skills_service.py:561-588`): the H1 `^#\s+Table:\s+\[?(\w+)\]?\.\[?(\w+)\]?`, `**Type:**\s*(\w+)`, an optional `## Columns` section (`### ColumnName (DataType) - tags` blocks), else the `| Ord | Name | Data Type | Description |` table.

#### 11.4.3 Index files and runtime lookup

| Runtime operation | Implementation |
|---|---|
| List sources | `load_data_sources_index()` parses `_index.md` (`skills_service.py:38-98`) |
| One source by name | `load_primary_data_source_by_name(name)` → `{slug}/_data-source.md`, else scan all (`:249-269`) |
| "primary" source | `load_primary_data_source()` = **first** `_data-source.md` from `rglob` (`:164-178`) |
| All groups (tree-wide) | `load_all_data_groups()` = `rglob("_*-group.md")` (`:100-119`) |
| Groups of one source | `load_data_groups_for_source(name)` reads `{slug}/.data-groups` then each group file (`:121-162`) |
| Schema index | `load_schema_indices()` = every `.schema-index.json` keyed by its `data_source` field (`:756-782`) |
| Object index | `load_object_indices(ds)` = every `.object-index.json` under the source dir keyed by `schema` (`:784-823`) |
| Keyword object search | `search_objects_by_keyword()` — two stages (`:909-962`) |
| Statistics / recommendations | `get_schema_statistics(query=…)` (`:1096-1166`) |
| Markdown for prompt | `markdown_lookup_for_objects(source_id, objects)` (`stores/skills_folder.py:228-248`) |

Two-stage keyword search: stage 1 `_get_relevant_schemas` scores each `(data_source, schema)` entry with `schema_name +2.0`, `description +1.0`, `keyword +1.5` per query term, keeps the top `self._top_schemas = 5` with score `>= self._min_schema_score = 1.0`, optional `domain` pre-filter (`skills_service.py:864-907`, thresholds at `:34-36`); stage 2 scores each object: object name `+3.0`, keywords `+2.0`, description `+1.0`, Function `×1.2`, then multiplies by `self._schema_match_multiplier = 1.5` when its schema was selected (`:964-1000`). Stop-word sets differ between `_extract_keywords`/`_normalize_query_terms` (`:397-424,825-842`); both need words `len > 2`.

`markdown_lookup_for_objects` resolves `{slug}` from the `source_id` by scanning every `_data-source.md` for the front-matter `source_id` (`skills_folder.py:24-40`), looks for `{schema}.fn.{object}.md` first for functions then `{schema}.{object}.md` in `schemas/{schema}/`, then `schemas/`, then `rglob` (`:194-208`), and returns `{"{schema}.{object}".lower(): markdown}` while also assigning `obj.markdown` (`:236-248`). The generator calls it immediately before hydration (`app/core/orchestrator/builtin_sql_generator.py:285-288`) and passes the result as `markdown_lookup=` into `SqlContextHydrator.build_contexts`. Markdown read failures return `""` and never raise (`skills_folder.py:211-217`).

### 11.5 Few-shots knowledge base (`few_shots`)

#### 11.5.1 Write path

`FewShotVectorService.upsert(question, sql, key=None)` (`fewshot_vector_service.py:40-54`):

```python
key = key or str(uuid4())
now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
vector = embed_text(question, self.provider, self.source_id)
rec = {
    "data_source_id": self.source_id,
    "key": key,
    "question": question,          # stored verbatim; NOT normalized
    "sql": sql,                    # field name is `sql`, not `sql_query`
    "created_at_utc": now,
    "vector": vector,              # embedding of the raw question
}
self.provider.upsert("few_shots", [rec])
```

There is **no mirror/companion table**. `few_shots_meta` was a duplicate scalar table; it is listed in `RETIRED_COLLECTIONS = ("few_shots_meta",)` (`schema_contracts.py:275`) and dropped on `ensure_schema` (`sqlite_vec_provider.py:36-42`) and again lazily on first few-shot use (`fewshot_vector_service.py:141-163`). Exact-question lookup is a plain scan of `few_shots`.

Question normalization (`app/utils/hashing.py:30-36`):

```python
def normalize_question(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (text or "").strip().lower())
def question_lookup_key(text: str) -> str:
    return normalize_question(text)
```
i.e. trim → lowercase → collapse internal whitespace. Nothing else (no punctuation stripping, no stemming).

`replace(key, question, sql)` (`:56-80`) regenerates the vector with `try_embed_text`; on `None` it calls `_update_scalars_without_vector` which fetches the existing row, overwrites `question`/`sql` and re-upserts, so the previous vector survives (`:192-201`). `created_at_utc` is preserved via `_try_get_created_at_utc` (`:182-190`). `delete(key)` → `provider.delete("few_shots", source_id, "key", key)` (`:82-84`). `list_all()` → `fetch_all` (`:135-139`).

#### 11.5.2 Read path used by the generator

```python
# exact (vector-free, first match wins, empty SQL skipped)
def try_get_exact(self, question):                                  # fewshot_vector_service.py:86-112
    if not self._collection_exists(DATA_TABLE_NAME): return None
    needle = question_lookup_key(question)
    for row in self.provider.fetch_all(DATA_TABLE_NAME, self.source_id):
        sql = (row.get("sql") or "").strip()
        if not sql: continue
        if question_lookup_key(row.get("question") or "") == needle:
            return FewShotExample(question=..., sql=sql, score=1.0,
                                  is_exact_match=True, source="few_shot")

# vector
def search(self, question, top_k=3, max_distance=KbScoreThreshold):  # :114-133
    vector = embed_text(question, ...)
    hits = self.provider.search_vector(DATA_TABLE_NAME, self.source_id, vector,
                                       top_k=top_k, min_score=max_distance)
    # score = hit["_distance"]; is_exact_match = _distance <= KbExactMatchThreshold (0.05)
```

Thresholds (`app/core/constants.py:12-14`): `KbExactMatchThreshold = 0.05`, `KbConfidenceThreshold = 0.70`, `KbScoreThreshold = 0.35` (max cosine distance). `FewShotVectorService.try_create_local(vector_db_path, source_id)` builds a `SqliteVecProvider`-backed service without any embedding provider (`:28-38`).

`DiscoveryEngine` consumes them (`app/core/orchestrator/discovery_engine.py`):

* `kb_exact(question)` → `stores.fewshots.try_get_exact` (`:62-63`) — the exact-match fast path is resolved *before* discovery.
* `kb_vector_top1` → `search(query, top_k=1, max_distance=KbScoreThreshold)` (`:68-70`).
* `discover()` → `search(query, top_k=3, max_distance=KbScoreThreshold)`; a best hit with confidence `1 - score >= KbConfidenceThreshold` produces branch `KB_DIRECT` with `_objects_from_sql(hit.sql)`; otherwise any best hit produces `KB_GAP_FILL` merging the KB SQL's objects with column evidence (`:159-186`).
* `vector_store.search_fewshots_with_threshold(query, top_k, knowledge_type, score_threshold=0.5)` filters `score < threshold` (`vector_store.py:266-286`), used by `generation_service.py:1913`.

Admin facade reads (`vector_store.py:452-490`) map `sql → sql_query` and hard-code `knowledge_type = "sql_query"` for list views; `delete_fewshot_item` searches all rows for a matching `key` and delegates to the per-source service.

#### 11.5.3 Ingest, CRUD and export endpoints

| Method | Path | Key fields / behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/ingest-fewshots` | multipart `file` (.xlsx/.xls only), `mode` ∈ `append|replace` (default `append`), `source_id` **required** (400 if missing); 200 ms sleep to let the SSE client attach (`admin.py:494-535`) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/admin/ingest-progress` | SSE `data: {current,total,percentage,status}` every 0.5 s; stops on `complete`/`error` (`admin.py:667-711`) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/admin/fewshots` | → `FewShotItem[]` with `id=key`, `question`, `sql_query`, `knowledge_type="sql_query"`, `verified=True` (`admin.py:539-556`) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/fewshots` | body `FewShotItem`; `source_guid = getattr(item, "source_id", None)`; `knowledge_type` defaults `sql_query` (`admin.py:558-570`) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/admin/fewshots/{item_id}` | deletes by contract key (`admin.py:572-579`) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/admin/fewshots/export` | xlsx `knowledge_base_{YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS}.xlsx` with `question, sql_query, knowledge_type` (`admin.py:581-614`) |

Excel ingest rules (`admin_service.ingest_fewshots_from_excel`, `:781-886`): columns lower-cased+stripped; required `question`, `sql_query`; optional `knowledge_type` defaulting to `sql_query` and clamped to `['general','sql_query','r_code','sas_code']`; drop rows with empty question/sql; `drop_duplicates(subset=['question'])`; `mode=="replace"` calls `vector_store.clear_fewshots_collection()` **without `source_id`** → ⚠️ clears every source's few-shots; per-row `insert_fewshot_item(..., source_guid=source_id)`; per-row failures print and continue; returns `{status, message, rows_processed, total_rows}` with `message = f"Successfully ingested {n} few-shot examples"`.

Contribution staging (`app/api/endpoints/contributions.py`) writes `contribution_library` rather than `few_shots`:

| Method | Path | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/contributions` | validates non-empty question/sql, `MAX_QUESTION_LENGTH = 2000`, `MAX_SQL_LENGTH = 4000`, `MAX_USER_ID_LENGTH = 128`; runs `check_similarity(question, threshold=0.9)`; inserts row with `status="pending"`, `user_id or "anonymous"`, `submitted_at = utcnow().isoformat()`, fresh `uuid4` key (`vector_store.py:594-612`) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/admin/contributions` | lists rows and re-computes similarity per row (admin only) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/contributions/approve` | `move_contribution_to_knowledge_base(contribution_id, edited_question, edited_sql, knowledge_type)` → inserts a `few_shots` row into the **contribution's** source, then deletes the contribution (`vector_store.py:660-676`) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/admin/contributions/{contribution_id}` | deletes the contribution row |

`check_similarity` (`vector_store.py:624-638`) searches top-1 and returns `(is_similar, similarity_score, similar_item_id)` with `similarity_score = max(0.0, 1.0 - hit.score)`.

### 11.6 Value index (`value_index`)

**Extraction: there is none in code.** No routine enumerates distinct database values. Values must arrive as an operator-supplied `.csv`/`.xlsx` (repo samples: `northwind_value_sets.csv`, `sample_values.csv`) via the admin endpoints or the loader scripts.

#### 11.6.1 Stored row

`ValueIndexService.upsert(value, schema_name, table_name, column_name, key=None)` (`value_index_service.py:16-39`):

```python
key = key or str(uuid4())
vector = embed_text(value, self.provider, self.source_id)
{
  "data_source_id": self.source_id,
  "key": key,
  "value": value,                      # original display value → embedded
  "plain_value": (value or "").lower(),
  "schema_name": schema_name,
  "table_name": table_name,
  "column_name": column_name,
  "vector": vector,                    # stored for parity; NOT used at query time
}
```
Contract fields: `schema_contracts.py:84-99`. SQLite index `idx_value_plain` on `(data_source_id, plain_value)` (`sqlite_vec_provider.py:43-46`).

#### 11.6.2 Substring search semantics at query time

```python
def search(self, query, top_k=10, fetch_cap=16384):        # value_index_service.py:41-53
    needle = (query or "").strip().lower()
    if not needle: return []
    rows = self.provider.fetch_all("value_index", self.source_id)[:fetch_cap]
    hits = []
    for row in rows:
        plain = (row.get("plain_value") or "").lower()
        if needle in plain: hits.append(row)
        if len(hits) >= top_k: break
    return hits[:top_k]
```
Substring (`in`), case-insensitive, first-`fetch_cap = 16384` rows in store order, returns full rows (including `vector`). `list_all()` = `fetch_all`, `delete(key)` = `provider.delete("value_index", source_id, "key", key)`, `clear()` = `provider.delete_source("value_index", source_id)` (`:55-62`).

**Schema/column association → seeding:** in `DiscoveryEngine.discover_with_column_evidence`, each `analysis.filter_values` term is searched with `top_k=5` and each hit becomes a `ScoredObject(schema_name=hit.schema_name, object_name=hit.table_name, score=ColumnDetailValueSeedScore=0.80, matched_columns=[hit.column_name], required=True)` (`discovery_engine.py:190-200,251-264`). `discover()` additionally emits `value_mappings` as `[{"value","table","column"}]` for every filter value with `top_k=3` (`:241-245`), which the generator forwards with `hydrator.set_value_mappings(discovery.value_mappings)` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:284`). The prompt presents them under the `### VERIFIED DATA MAPPINGS` heading (`docs/VALUE_INDEX_FEATURE.md:116-120`).

#### 11.6.3 Upload paths

| Path | Rules |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/admin/ingest-values` | multipart `file` (.xlsx/.xls/.csv), `mode` ∈ `append|replace`, `source_id` required; `.csv` → `file_type="csv"`, else `"xlsx"` (`admin.py:618-665`) |
| `scripts/load_value_index_file.py <path> [--mode append\|replace]` | CSV handled locally (encodings `utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1252, latin1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be`, exit 2 if all fail), xlsx delegated to `ingest_values_from_excel` (`load_value_index_file.py:10-90`) |
| `scripts/load_northwind_value_index.py --path <csv> --mode <append\|replace>` | default path `northwind_value_sets.csv` (`load_northwind_value_index.py`) |
| `scripts/rebuild_northwind_vectors.py [--values-only]` | wipes all contract collections for `SOURCE_ID = "1b2b4f87-5ef6-4389-976e-cee2ff56464f"`, rebuilds schemas/groups/QAs from `skills/data-sources/northwind`, replicates SQLite → Milvus, then loads values from `northwind_value_sets.csv` into both providers (`rebuild_northwind_vectors.py:13-24,62-105,108-178`) |

`ingest_values_from_excel` (`admin_service.py:487-629`) exact behaviour: CSV encodings tried in order `utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1252, latin1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be, iso-8859-1, windows-1252`, last resort `latin1` with `on_bad_lines='skip'`; columns `strip().str.lower()`; required `value, schema_name, table_name, column_name` (error payload lists both required and found); `metadata` column parsed with `json.loads` and silently discarded on failure; `drop_duplicates(subset=['value','schema_name','table_name','column_name'])`; empty values dropped; `mode=="replace"` → `clear_values_collection()` **without source** ⚠️; `batch_size = 100` slicing, each batch → `insert_value_items_batch(batch, source_guid=source_id)` which loops `values.upsert(...)` per item (`vector_store.py:526-538`) — so "batch" is only a loop boundary, each row is embedded and upserted individually; batch exceptions are logged and skipped. Response `{status, message: f"Successfully ingested {n} values", rows_processed, total_rows}`.

Read/manage endpoints: `GET /admin/values/search?query&top_k=50`, `GET /admin/values`, `DELETE /admin/values/{item_id}`, `POST /admin/values/clear?source_id=`, `GET /admin/values/template` (xlsx with the 5 template columns, `admin.py:772-798`), `GET /admin/values/export` (xlsx, drops `plain_value`/`vector`).

### 11.7 Data groups

#### 11.7.1 Definition and storage

A data group is a named business cluster of `schema.object` members. Two representations coexist:

1. **On disk** — `data-groups/_{slug}-group.md` plus the `.data-groups` manifest and (for the rebuild path) `data-groups/.data-group-index.json`.
2. **In the vector store** — `data_group_metadata` (scalars + `keywords_json` + `members_json`) and `data_group_vectors_cache` (three JSON vectors).

Group markdown written by the scan (`schema_scan_service.py:630-643`) and by `create_data_group` (`skills_admin_service.py:382-404`) — the latter writes `### {i}. …`-free plain list and a `No tables assigned yet.` placeholder when empty:

```markdown
# {name}

**Data Source:** {data_source}
**Category:** {category}            # default "User-defined"
**Keywords:** {keywords_str}

## Description

{description}

## Data Objects

- **[{table_stem}](../schemas/{schema}/{file}.md)** - Table
```

`.data-groups` line format (spec: `docs/DATA_GROUPS_REFACTORING.md:139-156`): `{Display Name}|{filename.md}`, UTF-8, one per line, trailing newline required. Parsed by `skills_admin_service._read_data_groups_file` (`:30-57`) and `skills_service.load_data_groups_for_source` (`:146-161`).

Group parse back (`skills_service._parse_data_group_file`, `:271-320`): `^#\s+(.+?)(?:\s+Group)?$` for the name, `**Data Source:**`, `**Category:**`, `**Keywords:**` (comma split), `## Description`, `## Schema (Migration )?Notes`, and table links `\*\*\[(.+?)\]\((.+?\.md)\)\*\*` resolved relative to the group file.

#### 11.7.2 Member lists and the `DataGroupStore` write

`DataGroupStore.upsert(group_name, description, keywords, members, group_id=None)` (`data_group_store.py:19-55`):

```python
group_id = group_id or f"[{source_id}].[{group_name}]"
now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
# data_group_metadata
{"data_source_id", "group_id", "group_name", "description",
 "keywords_json": json.dumps(keywords), "members_json": json.dumps(members), "updated_at_utc": now}
# data_group_vectors_cache
semantic   = embed_text(description or group_name, ...)
functional = embed_text(" ".join(keywords), ...)
object_vec = embed_text(" ".join(members), ...)
{"data_source_id", "group_id", "semantic_vector_json", "functional_vector_json",
 "object_vector_json", "updated_at_utc"}
```
`dumps_vector`/`loads_vector` come from `app/services/stores/score_utils.py`.

#### 11.7.3 Weighted similarity and discovery influence

`DataGroupStore.search(query, top_n=ActiveDataGroupTopN=3, query_vector=None)` (`:70-85`): reads `data_group_vectors_cache`, computes **cosine similarity against `semantic_vector_json` only** (functional/object vectors are stored but unused here), joins to `data_group_metadata` via `group_id`, sorts desc, truncates to `top_n`. Rows with unparsable vectors are skipped. `data_group_vectors_map` and `data_group_vectors_vec0` are contract/parity tables that `DataGroupStore` never reads (`docs/VECTOR_SCHEMA.md:180`).

`DiscoveryEngine.resolve_active_data_groups(query)` (`discovery_engine.py:120-131`): if the vector search returns nothing, it falls back to `stores.schema_index.score_data_group_keywords(query, stores.data_groups.list())` and keeps scored groups with `overlap > 0` (top 3). It then builds `members: {member.lower(): [group_name,…]}` and `summary = f"Active data groups: {', '.join(names)}"`.

In `discover()` the group members become their own RRF list with weight `RRF_WEIGHT_DATA_GROUP = 2.0` (`constants.py:27`):

```python
rrf_merge({"schema_vector": schema_list, "value_index": value_objects, "few_shot": fewshot_objects,
           "data_group": group_objects, "bm25": bm25_list}, max_results=MaxRerankTables)   # 8
```
and the branch is promoted to `GROUP_ANCHORED` when any merged object appears in `member_groups` (`discovery_engine.py:204-231`). Other RRF weights: value index 1.0, few-shot 1.0, schema vector 1.0, BM25 default 0.5, `RrfK = 60.0` (`constants.py:23-29`).

#### 11.7.4 Group population paths

* Scan: one auto group per schema, merged into `.data-groups` (`schema_scan_service.py:599-660`).
* Admin CRUD (§11.10) writing markdown + `.data-groups` only — **no vector-store write**.
* Skills-folder rebuild / import: reads `data-groups/.data-group-index.json` and upserts into `DataGroupStore` + `PrecomputedQueryStore` (`skills_folder.py:146-191`). Accepted JSON shapes: top-level list, or an object with `groups` or `data_groups`; per group `name` **or** `group_name`, `description`, `keywords`, `members`; per QA `question`, `sql_query`/`sql`, `smq_query`, `status` (default `"Approved"`), `id`/`query_id`.

### 11.8 Precomputed data-group questions

#### 11.8.1 Row fields

`PrecomputedQueryStore.upsert(...)` (`stores/precomputed_store.py:25-61`) writes **two** rows with the same `query_id`:

```python
# vec_data_group_queries
{"data_source_id", "query_id": query_id or str(uuid4()),
 "group_name", "group_file_name": group_file_name or group_name,
 "question", "sql_query",
 "smq_query": smq_query or "",            # optional SMQ JSON (see §09)
 "status": status (default PENDING),
 "updated_at_utc": utcnow().isoformat()}
# vec_data_group_query_vectors_cache
{"data_source_id", "query_id", "question_vector_json": dumps_vector(embed_text(question)), "updated_at_utc"}
```
Contract: `schema_contracts.py:149-175`. `list(status=None)` filters in Python on exact `status` equality (`:63-67`). `set_status(query_id, status)` fetches the row, rewrites `status` and `updated_at_utc`, re-upserts — it does **not** touch the vector cache (`:69-75`). `delete(query_id)` removes both rows (`:77-79`).

#### 11.8.2 Status workflow

Constants (`precomputed_store.py:13-17`): `APPROVED="Approved"`, `MODIFIED="Modified"`, `PENDING="Pending"`, `REJECTED="Rejected"`, `ERROR="Error"`.

`DataGroupQueryGenerationService` (`data_group_query_service.py`) creates rows as `Pending` and exposes transitions:

```
generate_pairs(group_name, questions_sql, status=PENDING)   # per item: question, sql_query|sql, group_file_name|group_name, smq_query
approve(query_id)        -> Approved
reject(query_id)         -> Rejected
mark_modified(query_id)  -> Modified
mark_error(query_id)     -> Error
```
Per-item field resolution: `sql_query = item.get("sql_query") or item.get("sql") or ""`, `group_file_name = item.get("group_file_name") or group_name`, `smq_query = item.get("smq_query") or ""` (`data_group_query_service.py:21-34`).

**Searchability matrix** (this is the important asymmetry):

| Status | Exact path | Vector path |
|---|---|---|
| `Approved` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `Modified` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `Pending`, `Rejected`, `Error` | ❌ | ❌ |

* `VectorSearchService.try_get_precomputed_exact` accepts `status in {"Approved", "Modified"}` and matches on `question_lookup_key` (`vector_search_service.py:92-108`).
* `VectorSearchService.search_precomputed` keeps only `status == "Approved"` rows, scores cosine similarity between the query embedding and `question_vector_json`, sorts desc, keeps `top_k = PrecomputedQueryTopK = 3`, and marks `is_exact_match = sim >= direct_threshold` (`:110-147`; `constants.py:18-20`). Thresholds: `PRECOMPUTED_QUERY_DIRECT_MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.93`, `PRECOMPUTED_QUERY_FEW_SHOT_THRESHOLD = 0.82` (`config.py:56-57`).
* In discovery the top precomputed examples are attached to the result, and when `examples[0].score >= precomputed_few_shot_threshold()` and it is not an exact match, the branch is renamed via `precomputed_related(branch)` — i.e. `precomputed_related/<branch>` (`discovery_engine.py:232-238`).

#### 11.8.3 Admin surface

| Method | Path | Params/body |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/admin/precomputed-queries` | query `source_id` (required), `status` (optional exact filter) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/precomputed-queries` | query `source_id`; body `{question, sql_query, group_name, group_file_name="", smq_query="", status="Pending", query_id=null}` → `{"query_id": …}` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/precomputed-queries/{query_id}/status` | query `source_id`, `status` → `{"status":"success"}` |

`source_id` goes through `resolve_known_source_id` on all three (404 when unknown) — `admin_precomputed.py:23-51`.

### 11.9 Semantic models (writes; compiler in §09)

`SemanticModelService` (`app/services/semantic_model_service.py`) writes six collections per saved model:

| Collection | Written fields |
|---|---|
| `semantic_models` | `data_source_id, model_id (uuid4 when absent), label, is_active (1/0 from `model.is_active`), updated_at_utc` (`:38-47`) |
| `semantic_measures` | `model_id, measure_name=m.name, expression=m.expression, description=m.description or ""` (`:79-89`) |
| `semantic_dimensions` | `model_id, dimension_name=d.name, column_name=d.column, table_name=d.table, description` (`:90-101`) |
| `semantic_joins` | `model_id, from_table, to_table, join_expression, join_type=j.join_type or "INNER"` (`:102-113`) |
| `semantic_governance_predicates` | `model_id, predicate=p, description=""` (`:114-123`) |
| `semantic_embeddings` | `model_id, embedding_json=dumps_vector(embed_text(semantic_embedding_source(label, measures, dimensions, governance_predicates))), updated_at_utc` (`:49-61`) |

Embedding source format (`schema_contracts.py:359-367`):

```
{label} | measure({name}:{desc}:{expr}) … | dimension({name}:{desc}:{table}.{column}) … | governance({pred}) …
```

`_replace_children` deletes prior child rows per table before rewriting (one `delete` per non-empty table, by `model_id`) — `:66-78`. Activation: `get_active_model()` filters `is_active == 1` and picks the most recent `updated_at_utc` (`:129-136`); `is_enabled(request_override)` returns `bool(override) and model is not None` when overridden, otherwise the per-source flag from `ENABLE_SEMANTIC_LAYER_PER_DATA_SOURCE` (`config.py:63,96-115`) with an active-model requirement (`:22-33`). Retrieval: `search_models(query, top_k=SemanticModelDiscoveryTopK=3)` ranks active models by cosine similarity of `embed_text(query)` against `embedding_json` (`:138-153`). Hydration maps rows back to `SemanticModel(model_id, data_source_key=source_id, label, is_active, measures, dimensions, joins, governance_predicates)` (`:155-196`).

Endpoints (`app/api/endpoints/admin_semantic.py`), all with a required `source_id` query param resolved via `resolve_known_source_id`:

| Method | Path | Body | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/admin/semantic-models` | — | `{"models": [...]}` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/semantic-models` | `SemanticModel` | saved model dump |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/semantic-models/extract` | `{schema_text, sql, label}` | `SemanticModelExtractionService().extract(...)` then save |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/admin/semantic-models/compile` | `{smq, dbms}` or a bare SMQ payload | `{"sql": …}` using the **active** model; 404 `"No active semantic model"`; 400 on `SemanticCompilationError` |

Raw storage shapes are frozen in `docs/VECTOR_SCHEMA.md:277-357`; the compiler itself is specified in §09.

### 11.11 Maintenance and rebuild matrix

| Change | What must be re-run | How |
|---|---|---|
| New table / column added | catalog scan + `schemas` ingest | `POST /admin/data-sources/{id}/scan` (both), or `POST /admin/schema/sync` / `batch-sync` (single objects), or `python scripts/ingest_metadata.py` |
| Table/column dropped | same, **plus** add the object to `exclude_objects.txt` (otherwise stale rows persist — see §11.2.5) or `DELETE /admin/schema` | `POST /admin/data-sources/{id}/exclude-objects`, then scan |
| Table/column description changed in the DB | markdown rebuild then re-embed | `POST /admin/skills/sync-schema-markdown {file_path}`, then `POST /admin/schema/sync?schema&table` (or a full scan) |
| Markdown edited by hand | re-embed that object | `POST /admin/schema/sync` / `batch-sync`; for the whole tree use `PUT /admin/skills/raw-markdown` then batch-sync |
| Index files missing/stale | `.schema-index.json` / `.object-index.json` | `POST /admin/skills/regenerate-indices` or `python scripts/generate_schema_indices.py` |
| **Embedding model or dimension changed** | **all** vector rows are invalid | full re-embed: `python scripts/ingest_metadata.py` (schemas) + re-import few-shots/values (no bulk re-embed endpoint exists; few-shots must be re-uploaded via `POST /admin/ingest-fewshots`, values via `POST /admin/ingest-values`). `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` must match `FLOAT_VECTOR(1536)` or the provider must recreate collections (`milvus_provider.py:120-122` drops a collection whose vector field is missing, but not one whose dimension changed). Clear `embedding_cache` as well — keys include the model name (`embeddings.py:64,103`), so stale entries are simply never hit; the table still grows and is LRU-evicted at 10 000 rows. |
| Data source moved (new server/database) | new `_data-source.md` values + re-registration | `PUT /admin/data-sources/{source_id}` or edit `_data-source.md` directly, then `POST /admin/data-sources/{source_id}/scan`; `GET /admin/data-sources/resolve` maps server+database back to a `source_id`. A new identity hash means a **new** `source_id` and a fresh partition — old rows remain under the old id. |
| Provider swap SQLite → Milvus | replicate every contract table | `python scripts/copy_sqlite_to_milvus.py` (drops + recreates each populated collection, upserts in `BATCH = 50`, verifies `milvus num_entities == sqlite rows` and uses `schemas` as the pass/fail table) |
| Milvus contents suspect | full rebuild from disk | `python scripts/rebuild_northwind_vectors.py` (Northwind only; wipes all contract collections, rebuilds from `skills/data-sources/northwind`, replicates, reloads values) — or `POST /admin/skills/rebuild/{source_id}` for any source |
| Few-shots suspect | recreate + re-ingest | `python scripts/rebuild_fewshots.py` (drops/clears `few_shots`, index recreate) then re-upload |
| Every source's `schemas` rebuilt | per-source ingest | `python scripts/rebuild_milvus_all_skills.py` — iterates `_index.md` sources, `create_milvus_collections()`, `ingest_metadata(source_id)` per source, `clear_engine_cache(source_id)` in `finally` |
| Value index only | reload | `python scripts/load_value_index_file.py <path> --mode replace` or `python scripts/rebuild_northwind_vectors.py --values-only` |
| Groups migrated from `_data-source.md` | manifest rewrite | `python scripts/migrate_data_groups_to_file.py [--dry-run] [--path skills/data-sources]` |
| Legacy Milvus → skills folder | one-off | `python scripts/migrate_milvus_to_skills.py [--output-dir skills/data-sources] [--dry-run]` |
| Auth method change | rewrite settings/env | `python scripts/update_to_windows_auth.py` (loads settings, rebuilds the connection string, `encrypt_string`) |
| Markdown cruft | prune unused sections | `python scripts/cleanup_markdown_files.py [--path skills/data-sources] [--dry-run]` |

CLI summary for the scripts named in the brief:

```
python scripts/ingest_metadata.py                 # no args; ensure_schema + ingest_metadata() (no source_id → first source)
python scripts/generate_schema_indices.py         # no args; walks <repo>/skills/data-sources
python scripts/rebuild_northwind_vectors.py [--values-only]
python scripts/load_value_index_file.py <csv|xlsx> [--mode append|replace]
python scripts/copy_sqlite_to_milvus.py           # no args; requires a connected Milvus
python scripts/load_northwind_value_index.py [--path northwind_value_sets.csv] [--mode append|replace]
```

---

### 11.12 Minimum viable dataset

**Tier 0 — absolute minimum that returns a correct answer with zero LLM involvement.** One data source must exist in `_index.md` + `_data-source.md` (so `resolve_known_source_id` succeeds), and exactly one `few_shots` row:

```
data_source_id = <source_id>
key            = <uuid4>
question       = "How many customers are in each country?"
sql            = "SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM dbo.Customers GROUP BY Country;"
created_at_utc = <iso8601 utc>
vector         = embed_text(question)
```
Then `POST /api/v1/generate-sql {"query": "how many CUSTOMERS are in each country??", "source_id": "<source_id>"}` hits `DiscoveryEngine.kb_exact` → `FewShotVectorService.try_get_exact` (whitespace+case normalized) → `DiscoveryBranch.KB_DIRECT`. Nothing else — no schema rows, no markdown, no values — is required for that specific question.

**Tier 1 — minimum for genuine generation from a schema.** Provide, in this order:

1. **Data source**: `POST /api/v1/admin/data-sources` with `friendly_name`, `server`, `database_name`, `auth_type`, `skip_auto_scan=true`, or `POST /api/v1/admin/skills/data-sources` with `{name, type:"SQL Server", server, database}`. Result: `{slug}/_data-source.md`, `.data-groups`, `_index.md` entry, and a PostgreSQL registry UUID.
2. **`schemas` rows for the tables the question needs** (2–3 tables is enough). The cheapest correct producer is `POST /api/v1/admin/schema/batch-sync` with `{"table_names": ["dbo.Customers","dbo.Orders"], "source_id": "<source_id>"}` or `POST /api/v1/admin/data-sources/{source_id}/scan` for the whole database. Each selected table yields `1 parent row + N column rows` with the exact shapes in §11.3.3. Without these rows `VectorSearchService.search_objects` returns empty and discovery degrades to keyword-only.
3. **Markdown hydration** (strongly recommended): run the scan so `schemas/{schema}/{schema}.{object}.md` exists; the prompt context is built from `markdown_lookup_for_objects`, and missing markdown means the hydrator has only the embedded `description` payload.
4. **One group + one precomputed Q&A** (recommended): `POST /api/v1/admin/skills/data-groups` for the business cluster, and `POST /api/v1/admin/precomputed-queries` with `status="Approved"` for the canonical phrasing. Only `Approved` rows participate in vector search; `Approved` **and** `Modified` participate in exact matching.
5. **Value index rows for literal filters** (only if the question filters on a coded value): one row per literal via `POST /api/v1/admin/ingest-values` with an `.xlsx`/`.csv` containing `value, schema_name, table_name, column_name`. This makes the seed table `required` at score `0.80` and injects `### VERIFIED DATA MAPPINGS` into the prompt.
6. Optional: `exclude_objects.txt` to keep noise out, one semantic model if `semantic_mode` will be used.

**Concrete smallest end-to-end example (Northwind-like):**

```
_index.md + skills/data-sources/northwind/_data-source.md   (Server=(local), Database=NORTHWIND)
schemas: 2 parents + their column rows   → dbo.Customers, dbo.Orders
few_shots: 1 row (question → SQL)        → optional if step 4's precomputed row exists
data_group_metadata + vectors_cache: 1   → "Customer Management" with members ["dbo.Customers"]
vec_data_group_queries: 1 row, status="Approved", smq_query=""
value_index: 1 row                       → ("Germany","dbo","Customers","Country")
```
That set exercises every branch the generator needs: exact match (`few_shots` or `vec_data_group_queries`), object + column vector evidence (`schemas`), group anchoring (`data_group_*`, RRF weight 2.0), value seeding (`value_index`), and markdown hydration (skills folder).

### Implementation checklist

- [ ] `schema_contracts.py` reproduces all 18 collections with `data_source_id` first, `VECTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.1.0"`, `EmbeddingDimensions = 1536`, cosine metric, and the SQLite PK rule `PRIMARY KEY (data_source_id, …unique_with_source…)` (except `data_group_vectors_vec0` → `rowid`, and `semantic_governance_predicates` → no PK).
- [ ] `ensure_schema()` creates every table/collection plus indexes `idx_value_plain` and `idx_embedding_lru`, and drops `few_shots_meta`.
- [ ] Provider factory prefers Milvus, falls back to SQLite when unreachable, and honours `VECTOR_PROVIDER ∈ {milvus, sqlite, sqlite_vec}`.
- [ ] `create_data_source` produces the exact slug, registry UUID via the identity hash, `_data-source.md` template, empty `.data-groups`, and the `_index.md` section.
- [ ] `POST /admin/data-sources` auto-starts the scan unless `skip_auto_scan`; the scan raises if the folder is missing; the background task then calls `ingest_metadata(source_id)`.
- [ ] `build_connection_string` reproduces all six auth modes and the `Encrypt=yes` / `TrustServerCertificate=yes` flags; runtime engine building uses Windows auth from `_data-source.md` with the `SQL_SERVER_CONNECTION_STRING` fallback.
- [ ] `scan_database_objects` queries `sys.extended_properties`/`sys.objects`/`sys.sql_modules`/`sys.parameters`/`sys.types` as specified, filters functions with `o.type IN ('FN','IF','TF')`, discovers functions before the empty-schema guard, and applies `exclude_objects.txt` including markdown file deletion.
- [ ] Object markdown matches the `# {Table|View}: [s].[o]` header + `## Description` + `build_table_markdown_description` body, and functions match the H2 `## **Function:**` form with `**Returns:**`, parameters and usage.
- [ ] `.object-index.json`, `.schema-index.json` and the auto data-group files are written with the exact JSON keys shown; `.data-groups` is merged and sorted by the scan, appended unsorted by the admin service.
- [ ] `build_schema_object_rows` emits parent rows with `entity_type = object_type`, `column_name = ""`, and column rows with `entity_type = "Column"`, using `schema_object_key`, `parent_embedding_text`, `column_embedding_text` verbatim.
- [ ] `ingest_metadata` builds `existing_items` from parent rows only, deletes then re-adds matched objects, prunes excluded objects, and performs one final `upsert("schemas", rows)`.
- [ ] `embed_text` / `try_embed_text` implement the L1 (512) + L2 (10 000 / evict 1 000) cache, `sha256("{model}|{text}")` keys, `text_content[:8000]`, `access_count` bumping, and the SHA-256 hash fallback **only** in `embed_text`.
- [ ] `EmbeddingFactory` supports openai/azure/openai_compatible/unknown via the OpenAI client (60 s timeout, newline replacement, index-sorted batch) and raises `NotImplementedError` for `huggingface`.
- [ ] `FewShotVectorService` stores `sql` (not `sql_query`), never normalizes on write, preserves `created_at_utc` across edits, keeps the old vector when `try_embed_text` returns `None`, and implements both the vector-free exact scan and the distance-thresholded search.
- [ ] `ValueIndexService` stores `plain_value = value.lower()` and searches by case-insensitive substring with `top_k`/`fetch_cap=16384` semantics.
- [ ] `DataGroupStore` writes `data_group_metadata` + three-vector `data_group_vectors_cache`, and `search` ranks by cosine similarity on `semantic_vector_json` only, top 3.
- [ ] `PrecomputedQueryStore` writes both rows, and status gating matches the matrix: exact accepts `Approved|Modified`, vector accepts `Approved` only.
- [ ] `SemanticModelService.save` writes all six tables and `semantic_embedding_source` exactly as shown; `get_active_model` picks the newest `is_active=1`.
- [ ] Skills folder layout, filenames (`{schema}.{object}.md`, `{schema}.fn.{function}.md`), relative group links, and `_index.md` / `.data-groups` parsing are byte-compatible with the existing tree.
- [ ] `markdown_lookup_for_objects` + `SqlContextHydrator` wiring is preserved so markdown reaches the prompt.
- [ ] All §11.10 endpoints exist with the same method, path, query/body fields, admin dependency, and status codes; literal paths (`resolve`, `registry`, `by-path`, `template`, `export`, `search`, `clear`) are registered before parameterised siblings.
- [ ] Import/rebuild paths reject `vector-index.db`, wipe the seven rebuild collections and every collection for `source_id` on import, and expose the `idle/running/completed/error` status map with 409 on concurrent rebuild.
- [ ] Ingest progress SSE emits `{current,total,percentage,status}` every 0.5 s and terminates on `complete`/`error`.
- [ ] Excel/CSV ingest rules (required columns, lower-cased headers, dedupe keys, empty-row dropping, `batch_size = 100`, `knowledge_type` clamping, CSV encoding ladder) are reproduced exactly.
- [ ] Rebuild scripts run with the documented CLI arguments and the `copy_sqlite_to_milvus.py` pass/fail rule (`schemas` row count must match).
- [ ] The Tier-1 minimum dataset in §11.12 produces a correct answer end to end on a fresh install.

## 12 — Script Targets (Python/R/SAS) and the Deterministic Utility Layer

This section covers two things that the rest of the blueprint depends on:

1. **The three script targets** (`python`, `r`, `sas`). They are *not* separate pipelines. Each is the built-in SQL
   pipeline (§05–§07) with `target_language` switched, plus a small set of deterministic extraction / qualification /
   materialization / interceptor utilities. Everything else — routing, pins, fast paths, discovery, RRF, the retry
   loop, the failure taxonomy — is shared verbatim.
2. **The deterministic utility layer** (`app/utils/*`) that the SQL pipeline itself uses: regex catalogue, SQL
   normalization, sanitization, dialect quoting, hashing, PII masking, RRF.

> **Parity rule.** Every function described here is pure and deterministic. If your re-implementation changes a regex,
> a template string, a normalization order, or a default weight, the pipeline will still *run* but will silently
> diverge on hashing (hallucination detection), caching (discovery/embedding), scope validation, and stored-answer
> materialization. §12.19 lists the functions that must be byte-identical.

### 12.1 Where these pieces sit

| Piece | File | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|
| Body extraction + structural hash + syntax check + qualification (Python) | `app/utils/python_normalization.py` | `attempts.py`, `builtin_sql_generator.py`, `execution_service.py`, `prompts.py` |
| Same for R | `app/utils/r_normalization.py` | `attempts.py`, `builtin_sql_generator.py`, `prompts.py` |
| Same for SAS | `app/utils/sas_normalization.py` | `attempts.py`, `builtin_sql_generator.py`, `prompts.py` |
| SQL fence/comment/object-ref normalization | `app/utils/sql_normalization.py` | `attempts.py:76`, `builtin_sql_generator.py:37,462`, `discovery_engine.py:317`, `sql_validator.py:9`, all three script modules |
| Named regexes | `app/utils/regexes.py` | `router.py`, `attempts.py`, `coreference.py`, `preprocessing.py`, `discovery_engine.py`, `sql_normalization.py` |
| Prompt-input sanitization | `app/utils/sanitization.py` | `coreference.py`, `refinement_service.py`, `insight_service.py` |
| Dialect quoting | `app/utils/dialect.py` | `semantic_compiler.py`, `sql_context_hydrator.py` |
| Cache keys + sha256 | `app/utils/hashing.py` | `discovery_engine.py`, `stores/embeddings.py`, `fewshot_vector_service.py`, `vector_search_service.py` |
| PII masking | `app/utils/pii.py` | `preprocessing.py:51` |
| RRF merge | `app/utils/rrf.py` | `discovery_engine.py:34,179,211,221,227`, `attempts.py:556`, `builtin_sql_generator.py:270` |
| Interceptors | `app/services/{python,r,sas,query}_interceptor.py` | `attempts.py:50-53` |
| Workflow templates | `app/services/template_service.py` | nothing in `app/` (dormant; see §12.18) |

---

### 12.2 How `target_language` threads through the pipeline

#### 12.2.1 Entry points

`app/core/orchestrator/builtin_sql_generator.py:331-352`

```python
def generate_python_builtin(request, stores, llm=None):
    yield from generate_sql_builtin(request, stores, llm, target_language="python")

def generate_r_builtin(request, stores, llm=None):
    yield from generate_sql_builtin(request, stores, llm, target_language="r")

def generate_sas_builtin(request, stores, llm=None):
    yield from generate_sql_builtin(request, stores, llm, target_language="sas")
```

`target_language` defaults to `"sql"` (`builtin_sql_generator.py:66`, `attempts.py:89`) and is never read from the
HTTP request body. The HTTP routes select it by *which endpoint* was called, in
`app/services/code_generation_service.py`:

| HTTP route | Service function | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /generate-r` | `generate_r_for_request` → `generate_r_builtin(request, stores)` | `api/endpoints/generation.py:109,128`; `code_generation_service.py:23-63` |
| `POST /generate-sas` | `generate_sas_for_request` → `generate_sas_builtin(request, stores)` | `api/endpoints/generation.py:165,184`; `code_generation_service.py:66-107` |
| `POST /generate-python` | `generate_python_for_request` → `generate_python_builtin(request, stores)` | `api/endpoints/generation.py:221,240`; `code_generation_service.py:155-195` |
| `POST /generate-sql` | `generate_sql_builtin(request, stores, target_language="sql")` | `api/endpoints/generation.py` (SQL endpoint) |

All three script services share the same prefix logic before delegating (`code_generation_service.py:28-56`):

* `request.queryMode == "search"` → `search_data_objects` and return (no pipeline).
* `forceGeneral` → `_handle_general_query` and return (no pipeline).
* otherwise → `resolve_or_primary(request.source_id)` → `build_source_stores(...)` → the built-in generator.
* after the generator returns a result event, `is_edit` (see §12.2.3) sets `payload["is_code_edit"] = True` and, if no
  explanation is present, `payload["explanation"] = "Code updated based on your request."`
  (`code_generation_service.py:57-62, 100-105, 189-194`).

#### 12.2.2 Every branch point inside the shared pipeline

| Location | SQL behaviour | Script behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `builtin_sql_generator.py:71-74` | `python_mode/r_mode/sas_mode` all `False`, `script_mode=False` | one flag true, `script_mode=True` |
| `builtin_sql_generator.py:83-85` `finalize()` | `apply_language_result(result, "sql")` → no-op | maps `query_type` and rewrites failure comments (see §12.8) |
| `builtin_sql_generator.py:87-94` `code_from_match()` | returns stored SQL unchanged | `materialize_python_code` / `materialize_r_code` / `materialize_sas_code` |
| `builtin_sql_generator.py:170` | `semantic_mode = stores.semantic.is_enabled(...)` | `semantic_mode` forced `False` (`... if script_mode else ...`) |
| `builtin_sql_generator.py:173-178` | no-discovery provided-code path | same path, calls `_generate_from_provided_sql(..., target_language=...)` |
| `builtin_sql_generator.py:294-304` | `run_attempt_loop(..., target_language="sql")` | passes the language through |
| `attempts.py:101-102` | — | `if script_mode: semantic_mode = False` (SMQ compilation unreachable) |
| `attempts.py:154-162` | `build_system_prompt` + `build_user_prompt` | `build_{python,r,sas}_system_prompt` + `build_{python,r,sas}_user_prompt` |
| `attempts.py:185-192` | `extract_sql_body(raw)` | `extract_python_body` / `extract_r_body` / `extract_sas_body` |
| `attempts.py:193-207` | no embedded-SQL handling | `qualify_sql_in_python` / `_r` / `_sas` with `known = [(o.schema_name, o.object_name) for o in discovery.objects]` |
| `attempts.py:255-277` | `QueryInterceptor.check(sql, ...)` | script interceptor first, then `QueryInterceptor.check` on **each** embedded SQL |
| `attempts.py:292-298` | `structural_sql_hash(sql)` | `structural_python_hash` / `structural_r_hash` / `structural_sas_hash` |
| `attempts.py:304-309` | `"Repeated SQL structure detected"` | `"Repeated Python/R/SAS structure detected"` |
| `attempts.py:330-338` | `skip_critic = db_ok` | `skip_critic = db_ok and at least one embedded SQL was extracted` |
| `attempts.py:343-350` | `_run_critic` | `_run_python_critic` / `_run_r_critic` / `_run_sas_critic` |
| `attempts.py:500-520` | `validator.validate(code, allowed)` | syntax check, then per-extracted-SQL `validator.validate(sql, allowed)` |

`_validate_candidate` (`attempts.py:500-520`) verbatim:

```python
def _validate_candidate(code, validator, allowed, target_language):
    extractors = {
        "python": (syntax_check_python, extract_sql_from_python),
        "r":      (syntax_check_r,      extract_sql_from_r),
        "sas":    (syntax_check_sas,    extract_sql_from_sas),
    }
    pair = extractors.get(target_language)
    if not pair:
        return validator.validate(code, allowed)
    syntax_check, extract_sql = pair
    ok, err = syntax_check(code)
    if not ok:
        return False, err, []
    sqls = extract_sql(code)
    if not sqls:
        return True, "", []          # script with no embedded SQL is "valid" by definition
    for sql in sqls:
        db_ok, db_err, db_missing = validator.validate(sql, allowed)
        if not db_ok:
            return False, db_err, db_missing or []
    return True, "", []
```

Note the asymmetry: a script with **no** extracted SQL passes `_validate_candidate` unconditionally, but the
attempt-1 `skip_critic` gate (`attempts.py:333-337`) still requires at least one extracted statement per active script
mode, so such a script always pays one extra LLM critic round.

#### 12.2.3 "User requested write" flag

`attempts.py:254` (identical for every language):

```python
user_write = bool(
    context.request.is_user_code
    and any(w in (context.request.query or "").lower() for w in ("insert", "update", "delete", "drop"))
)
```

This is the **only** way the interceptors' write guards are relaxed. It is computed from the raw request query
(`GenerateSQLRequest.is_user_code`, `models/schemas.py:110`), not from the combined/folded query, and it is not
language-specific. `_is_code_edit_request` (`code_generation_service.py:109-119`) is a *different*, purely cosmetic
predicate that only sets `is_code_edit` in the response payload; it never relaxes a safety check.

---

### 12.3 Body extraction from the LLM response

The response body is extracted **before** interception, hashing and validation, and re-qualified immediately after
extraction (`attempts.py:185-207`).

#### 12.3.1 Python — `extract_python_body(text)` (`python_normalization.py:104-115`)

Regexes (`python_normalization.py:12-25`):

```python
_SQL_START = re.compile(r"^\s*(SELECT|WITH|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|MERGE)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
_SQL_OBJECT = re.compile(r"(?is)\b(from|join|into|update)\s+(?:\[[^\]]+\]|[A-Za-z_][\w]*)")
_FENCE_PYTHON = re.compile(r"```(?:python|py)\s*([\s\S]*?)```", re.IGNORECASE)
_FENCE_ANY = re.compile(r"```[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\s*([\s\S]*?)```")
_TRIPLE_SQL = re.compile(
    r"""(?:pd\.read_sql(?:_query)?\s*\(\s*)?(?:[fFrR]?'''([\s\S]*?)'''|[fFrR]?\"\"\"([\s\S]*?)\"\"\")""",
)
_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")
_PYTHON_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#.*?$", re.MULTILINE)
```

Algorithm:

1. `_FENCE_PYTHON.search(text)` → `cleanup_python_code(group(1))`.
2. else `_FENCE_ANY.search(text)` → `inner = group(1).strip()`; accept only if
   `looks_like_python(inner) or not _SQL_START.match(inner)`; then `cleanup_python_code(inner)`.
   (So a bare ```sql fence falls through to step 3 rather than being treated as Python.)
3. else `cleanup_python_code(text)`.

`looks_like_python` (`python_normalization.py:28-42`) returns `True` when the stripped text starts with
`"import "`, `"from "`, `"def "`, `"class "`, or contains any of:
`"pd.read_sql"`, `"final_result_df"`, `"sqlalchemy.create_engine"`, `"import pandas"`, `"import sqlalchemy"`,
`"engine.raw_connection"`.

`cleanup_python_code` (`python_normalization.py:45-101`) applies, in this exact order:

```python
code = re.sub(r"^```python\s*\n?", "", code, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
code = re.sub(r"^```\s*\n?", "", code)
code = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", code)
code = re.sub(r"^'''python\s*\n?", "", code, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
code = re.sub(r"\n?'''$", "", code)
code = re.sub(r'^"""python\s*\n?', "", code, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
code = re.sub(r'\n?"""$', "", code)
# then per line: drop bare "python"/"python3" lines; on line 0 also drop
#   r'^python[3]?\s+(-[a-z]+\s+)?["\']?'   (i.e. "python script.py")
#   r"^[$%>]\s*python"
# then: if the count of '"""' is odd and the code starts with '"""', cut the leading docstring
#   up to the lookahead (?=\n(?:import|from|def|class|#|\w+\s*=)) , else strip the leading '"""'
# then: the same treatment for an odd count of "'''"
```

> ⚠️ Unverified (cosmetic only): the docstring unwrap lookahead
> `^""".*?(?=\n(?:import|from|def|class|#|\w+\s*=))` cannot match unless the docstring body itself begins a line with
> one of those tokens; when it does not match, the code falls back to stripping only the leading `"""`.

#### 12.3.2 R — `extract_r_body(text)` (`r_normalization.py:69-80`)

```python
_FENCE_R = re.compile(r"```(?:r|rscript)\s*([\s\S]*?)```", re.IGNORECASE)
_FENCE_ANY = re.compile(r"```[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\s*([\s\S]*?)```")
```

Same three-step algorithm as Python, with `looks_like_r` (`r_normalization.py:23-41`): `True` if the stripped text
starts with `"library("`, `"require("`, `"source("`, or contains any of `"library(DBI)"`, `"library(dplyr)"`,
`"library(odbc)"`, `"library(ggplot2)"`, `"dbConnect("`, `"dbGetQuery("`, `"dbReadTable("`, `"dbDisconnect("`, `"%>%"`,
`"<- "`.

`cleanup_r_code` (`r_normalization.py:44-66`):

```python
code = re.sub(r"^```(?:r|rscript)\s*\n?", "", code, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
code = re.sub(r"^```\s*\n?", "", code)
code = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", code)
# per line: drop bare "r"/"rscript"; on line 0 drop r"^r(script)?\s+" and r"^[$%>]\s*r(script)?"
```

#### 12.3.3 SAS — `extract_sas_body(text)` (`sas_normalization.py:68-79`)

```python
_FENCE_SAS = re.compile(r"```(?:sas|sasbase)\s*([\s\S]*?)```", re.IGNORECASE)
_FENCE_ANY = re.compile(r"```[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\s*([\s\S]*?)```")
```

`looks_like_sas` (`sas_normalization.py:25-43`) upper-cases the text and returns `True` if it starts with
`"PROC "`, `"DATA "`, `"LIBNAME "`, `"%MACRO"`, `"%LET "`, or contains any of `"PROC SQL"`, `"PROC PRINT"`,
`"PROC MEANS"`, `"PROC FREQ"`, `"PROC SGPLOT"`, `"LIBNAME "`, `"QUIT;"`, `"CONNECTION TO "`, `"DISCONNECT FROM"`.

`cleanup_sas_code` (`sas_normalization.py:46-65`):

```python
code = re.sub(r"^```(?:sas|sasbase)\s*\n?", "", code, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
code = re.sub(r"^```\s*\n?", "", code)
code = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", code)
# per line: drop bare "sas"/"sasbase"; on line 0 drop r"^[$%>]\s*sas"
```

#### 12.3.4 SQL — `extract_sql_body(text)` (`sql_normalization.py:34-36`)

```python
def extract_sql_body(text: str) -> str:
    fenced = strip_markdown_fences(text)
    return strip_reasoning_header(fenced)
```

with (`sql_normalization.py:23-31`, `regexes.py:18,77-83`):

```python
FENCE_SQL = re.compile(r"```(?:sql|tsql|smq)?\s*([\s\S]*?)```", re.IGNORECASE)

def strip_markdown_fences(text: str) -> str:
    if not text:
        return ""
    match = FENCE_SQL.search(text)
    if match:
        return match.group(1).strip()
    return text.strip()

def strip_reasoning_header(sql: str) -> str:
    if not sql:
        return ""
    text = sql.strip()
    if text.startswith("/*"):
        end = text.find("*/")
        if end != -1:
            text = text[end + 2 :].strip()
    return text
```

Accepted variants and exact results (verified by running the module):

| Input | `extract_sql_body` |
|---|---|
| ` ```smq\n{"metrics":[]}\n``` ` | `{"metrics":[]}` |
| ` ```SQL\nselect 1\n``` ` | `select 1` |
| ` ```tsql\nselect 2\n``` ` | `select 2` |
| `text before ```tsql\nselect 2\n``` after` | `select 2` (first fence anywhere wins) |
| ` ```\nselect 3\n``` ` (no label) | `select 3` |
| `/* reasoning */\nselect 4` | `select 4` |
| `/* reasoning\nmultiline */select 5` | `select 5` |
| `select 6 -- no fence` | `select 6 -- no fence` |
| ` ```sql\nselect 1\n```\n/* trailing note */` | `select 1` — fence branch wins, trailing text is discarded |

Fence-label coverage differs per regex: `FENCE_SQL` accepts `sql|tsql|smq` and also the *unlabelled* fence; the
router-only `INLINE_SQL_BLOCK` (`regexes.py:16`) accepts `sql|tsql` only and is **not** used by `extract_sql_body`.

---

### 12.4 Locating embedded SQL inside a script

All three extractors return a de-duplicated list of SQL strings (dedupe key = `text.lower()`, first occurrence wins)
and each candidate is filtered by `_looks_like_sql_fragment`:

```python
_SQL_START  = re.compile(r"^\s*(SELECT|WITH|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|MERGE)\b", re.IGNORECASE)   # match() → anchored
_SQL_OBJECT = re.compile(r"(?is)\b(from|join|into|update)\s+(?:\[[^\]]+\]|[A-Za-z_][\w]*)")  # search()

def _looks_like_sql_fragment(text: str) -> bool:
    if not text:
        return False
    return bool(_SQL_START.search(text) or _SQL_OBJECT.search(text))
```

(`_SQL_START.search` is used here even though the regex is `^`-anchored with no `MULTILINE`, so it only matches at the
start of the string.)

#### 12.4.1 Python — `extract_sql_from_python(code)` (`python_normalization.py:171-211`)

1. `ast.parse(code)`. On `SyntaxError`, fall back to `_TRIPLE_SQL.finditer` over the raw text (group 1 = `'''…'''`
   body, group 2 = `"""…"""` body).
2. Walk the AST for `ast.Call` nodes whose function is `.read_sql` / `.read_sql_query` (attribute) or `read_sql` /
   `read_sql_query` (bare name). Add `node.args[0]` and any keyword named `sql` / `sql_query`.
3. `_const_str` (`:157-168`) accepts `ast.Constant` strings and `ast.JoinedStr` **only when every part is constant**
   (no `{...}` placeholder).
4. If step 2 produced nothing, walk the AST again and add **every** string constant that passes
   `_looks_like_sql_fragment`.

Verified consequence of step 4: `f"SELECT a FROM t WHERE x = {v}"` yields `['SELECT a FROM t WHERE x =']` (the
constant fragment of the f-string), because `_const_str` refused the `JoinedStr` and the fallback walk collected the
inner `Constant`.

#### 12.4.2 R — `extract_sql_from_r(code)` (`r_normalization.py:252-254`)

R has no parser: `_scan_r_strings` (`:129-178`) is a hand-written character scanner that returns the *contents* of
every string literal in order:

* R raw strings `r"..."` / `R"..."` with optional raw delimiter `(`, `[`, `{` (`_RAW_OPENERS`,
  `{"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}`); the terminator is `closer` followed by `"`.
* single/double quoted literals with backslash escapes; `\"` and `\'` are unescaped before returning.

`_extract_call_string_args` (`:233-249`) then filters those contents with `_looks_like_sql_fragment`. There is no
`dbGetQuery`-specific check — any SQL-shaped literal anywhere in the script is treated as an embedded statement.
Verified: `'result <- dbGetQuery(con, r"(SELECT 1 FROM a)")'` → `['SELECT 1 FROM a']`.

#### 12.4.3 SAS — `extract_sql_from_sas(code)` (`sas_normalization.py:146-174`)

1. If either `_CONNECTION_OPEN = (?is)CONNECTION\s+TO\s+\w+\s*\(` or `_EXECUTE_OPEN = (?is)EXECUTE\s*\(` matches, pull
   the balanced parenthesised body with `_extract_balanced_paren` (`:121-143`) — a depth counter that ignores
   parens inside `'…'` / `"…"` strings — and return **only** those bodies. `None` (unbalanced) is dropped by `_add`.
2. Otherwise fall back to scanning every `"…"` literal, then every `'…'` literal, with
   `r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"'` and `r"'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'"`, keeping the SQL-shaped ones.

Verified: pass-through `(SELECT a FROM b WHERE c=1)` inside `CONNECTION TO dbcon (...)` → `['SELECT a FROM b WHERE c=1']`;
`EXECUTE (SELECT 1 FROM x) BY dbcon` → `['SELECT 1 FROM x']`; a `DATA _null_` step containing
`x="SELECT 1 FROM dbo.t"` → `['SELECT 1 FROM dbo.t']` (the fallback path is not restricted to `PROC SQL`).

#### 12.4.4 Schema qualification of embedded SQL

After extraction, `attempts.py:193-207` re-qualifies the script so bare table names inside *literals* become
`schema.object` before hashing/validation:

```python
if python_mode and sql:
    from app.utils.python_normalization import qualify_sql_in_python
    known = [(o.schema_name, o.object_name) for o in discovery.objects]
    sql = qualify_sql_in_python(sql, known)
elif r_mode and sql:
    from app.utils.r_normalization import qualify_sql_in_r
    known = [(o.schema_name, o.object_name) for o in discovery.objects]
    sql = qualify_sql_in_r(sql, known)
elif sas_mode and sql:
    from app.utils.sas_normalization import qualify_sql_in_sas
    known = [(o.schema_name, o.object_name) for o in discovery.objects]
    sql = qualify_sql_in_sas(sql, known)
```

The underlying rewriter is `qualify_unqualified_objects` (`sql_normalization.py:71-110`, see §12.10.5).

**Python** (`python_normalization.py:282-324`) is token-based and the most delicate:

1. `known_objects` (the `[(schema, name), …]` list) is turned into `name_to_schema` by
   `qualify_unqualified_objects` itself.
2. `tokenize.generate_tokens`; on `TokenError` / `IndentationError` / `SyntaxError` the token list is empty.
3. For each `tokenize.STRING` token: `ast.literal_eval`; skip non-strings; qualify the value if it looks SQL-shaped;
   if changed, apply `result.replace(tok.string, _rebuild_string_token(tok.string, qualified), 1)` — **count=1**, i.e.
   the first textual occurrence of that literal in the file, which may not be the token's own location. This quirk is
   parity-relevant.
4. For each `FSTRING_MIDDLE` token (Python ≥ 3.12; the runtime here is CPython 3.14.7) the middle text is qualified and
   replaced directly.
5. If nothing changed, fall back to `extract_sql_from_python(code)` and `result.replace(sql, qualified)` for each.

`_rebuild_string_token` (`:257-279`) preserves the string prefix (`rRuUfFbB`) and the quote style, switching to triple
quotes or the other quote character when the new value would collide.

**R** (`r_normalization.py:280-291`) and **SAS** (`sas_normalization.py:222-233`) are simple:

```python
for sql in extract_sql_from_r(code):          # or extract_sql_from_sas
    qualified = qualify_unqualified_objects(sql, known_objects, default_schema)
    if qualified != sql:
        result = result.replace(sql, qualified)   # all occurrences, no count
```

Verified: `qualify_sql_in_python('df = pd.read_sql("SELECT * FROM Categories", conn)')` → `... FROM dbo.Categories ...`
and `from sqlalchemy import create_engine` is untouched (`tests/unit/test_python_normalization.py:121-147`).

---

### 12.5 Materialization templates (verbatim)

Used when a stored/few-shot/precomputed SQL answer (or the caller's `existing_code`) has to become script code:
`builtin_sql_generator.py:87-94` (`code_from_match`) and `builtin_sql_generator.py:408-415`
(`_generate_from_provided_sql`). Entry points: `materialize_python_code` / `materialize_r_code` /
`materialize_sas_code`, which are one-line aliases of `wrap_sql_as_python` / `wrap_sql_as_r` / `wrap_sql_as_sas`.

**Dispatch rule (all three).** If the input `looks_like_<lang>(body)`, it is treated as *code*:
`return qualify_sql_in_<lang>(cleanup_<lang>_code(body))` — i.e. the script path never double-wraps
(`tests/unit/test_python_normalization.py:36-40`, `test_r_normalization.py:36-40`). Otherwise the SQL body is
qualified with `qualify_unqualified_objects(body)` (no known objects, default schema `dbo`) and embedded.

#### 12.5.1 Python (`python_normalization.py:118-150`)

Indentation: each non-empty body line is prefixed with **8 spaces**; empty lines stay empty. The fence is
`'''` when the body contains `"""`, otherwise `"""` (`fence = "'''" if '"""' in body else '"""'`).

```python
# Retrieves data using the matched SQL query, then returns a pandas DataFrame.
import pandas as pd
import sqlalchemy

# DB_CONNECTION_STRING is injected at runtime.
# DB_CONNECTION_STRING = ("mssql+pyodbc://@your_server_name/your_database_name?driver=ODBC+Driver+17+for+SQL+Server&trusted_connection=yes")
engine = sqlalchemy.create_engine(DB_CONNECTION_STRING)
conn = engine.raw_connection()
try:
    final_result_df = pd.read_sql(
        """
        <SQL body, each non-empty line indented by 8 spaces>
        """,
        conn,
    )
finally:
    conn.close()
```

Byte-for-byte assembly (the concatenated comment line above is a single source line in the code):

```python
"# Retrieves data using the matched SQL query, then returns a pandas DataFrame.\n"
"import pandas as pd\n"
"import sqlalchemy\n"
"\n"
"# DB_CONNECTION_STRING is injected at runtime.\n"
"# DB_CONNECTION_STRING = ("
'"mssql+pyodbc://@your_server_name/your_database_name'
'?driver=ODBC+Driver+17+for+SQL+Server&trusted_connection=yes")\n'
"engine = sqlalchemy.create_engine(DB_CONNECTION_STRING)\n"
"conn = engine.raw_connection()\n"
"try:\n"
"    final_result_df = pd.read_sql(\n"
f"        {fence}\n"
f"{indented}\n"
f"        {fence},\n"
"        conn,\n"
"    )\n"
"finally:\n"
"    conn.close()\n"
```

#### 12.5.2 R (`r_normalization.py:83-116`)

Indentation: **4 spaces** per non-empty body line. The SQL is wrapped in an R *raw string* `r"( … )"`, so no escaping
of `"` is needed.

```r
# Retrieves data using the matched SQL query, then prints a data frame.
library(DBI)
library(odbc)
library(dplyr)

# Replace server and database names as needed. Use Windows authentication.
con <- dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  Driver = "SQL Server",
  Server = "your_server_name",
  Database = "your_database_name",
  Trusted_Connection = "Yes"
)
tryCatch({
  result <- dbGetQuery(con, r"(
    <SQL body, each non-empty line indented by 4 spaces>
  )")
  print(result)
}, finally = {
  dbDisconnect(con)
})
```

#### 12.5.3 SAS (`sas_normalization.py:82-108`)

Indentation: **8 spaces** per non-empty body line.

```sas
/* Retrieves data using the matched SQL query, then prints the result. */
PROC SQL;
    CONNECT TO ODBC AS dbcon
        (NOPROMPT="Driver={SQL Server};Server=your_server_name;Database=your_database_name;Trusted_Connection=Yes;");
    CREATE TABLE work.result AS
    SELECT * FROM CONNECTION TO dbcon (
        <SQL body, each non-empty line indented by 8 spaces>
    );
    DISCONNECT FROM dbcon;
QUIT;

PROC PRINT DATA=work.result;
RUN;
```

All three templates are **dialect-independent**: the driver/connection placeholders are always SQL Server ODBC, and
the SQL body is qualified with `dbo.` by default. `context.dbms_type` is never consulted here (see §12.9).

Empty input returns `""` for all three (`if not body: return ""`).

---

### 12.6 Syntax checking

| Language | Function | Implementation | Failure string |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python | `syntax_check_python(code)` `python_normalization.py:214-221` | real `compile(code, "<generated>", "exec")` | `f"Python syntax error: {exc.msg} (line {exc.lineno})"`; other exceptions → `f"Python compile error: {exc}"` |
| R | `syntax_check_r(code)` `r_normalization.py:274-277` | empty check + `_delimiter_balance` only | `"Empty R code"`; `f"R syntax error: unmatched '{ch}'"`; `f"R syntax error: unclosed '{stack[-1]}'"` |
| SAS | `syntax_check_sas(code)` `sas_normalization.py:202-219` | empty check + `/*`/`*/` count + `()`/`[]` balance | `"Empty SAS code"`; `"SAS syntax error: unmatched comment"`; `f"SAS syntax error: unmatched '{ch}'"`; `f"SAS syntax error: unclosed '{stack[-1]}'"` |

`_delimiter_balance` (`r_normalization.py:257-271`) strips `_R_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#.*?$", re.MULTILINE)`, then
blanks R string literals with `_blank_r_strings` (`:181-230`, handles raw strings), then walks pairs
`{"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}` with a stack.

`syntax_check_sas` uses `_blank_sas_comments_and_strings` (`sas_normalization.py:177-199`), which replaces
`_BLOCK_COMMENT = /\*[\s\S]*?\*/` and `_STAR_COMMENT = (?m)^\s*\*.*?;` with a space, then blanks `'…'` and `"…"`.

**There is no real R or SAS parser anywhere in the repository.** Neither checker knows anything about language
keywords, so structurally invalid scripts that happen to balance brackets pass the syntax stage and are only caught by
the LLM critic or the database validator. Do not "improve" this: the exact error strings and the exact acceptance set
are part of the contract enforced by `tests/unit/test_r_normalization.py:18-23,51-54` and
`tests/unit/test_sas_normalization.py:19-21,57`.

> ⚠️ Unverified: whether the reference C#/other-impl engine had a real R/SAS parser. The Python port
> (`docs/BUILT_IN_SQL_GENERATOR_PYTHON_PORT_PLAN.md`) only has the bracket-balance check.

### 12.7 Interception (safety) rules

Order inside the attempt loop (`attempts.py:253-279`): **script interceptor first**, then the *shared* SQL
interceptor on every extracted embedded statement. If the script interceptor fails, the embedded statements are not
checked. The failure returns `_fail(ErrorCategory.SAFETY, reason, …)`, i.e. `error_category == "safety"` and the
attempt loop terminates immediately (no retry).

#### 12.7.1 Python (`services/python_interceptor.py`)

```python
_TRIPLE_DOUBLE = re.compile(r'""".*?"""', re.DOTALL)
_TRIPLE_SINGLE = re.compile(r"'''.*?'''", re.DOTALL)
_SINGLE_STRING = re.compile(r"'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'")
_DOUBLE_STRING = re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"')
_COMMENTS = re.compile(r"#.*?$", re.MULTILINE)

DANGEROUS = re.compile(
    r"\b("
    r"os\.system|os\.popen|os\.remove|os\.unlink|os\.rmdir|os\.removedirs|"
    r"subprocess\.|shutil\.|socket\.|ctypes\.|multiprocessing\.|"
    r"pickle\.|requests\.|urllib\.request|"
    r"eval\s*\(|exec\s*\(|compile\s*\(|__import__\s*\("
    r")",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
WRITE_OPEN = re.compile(r"""\bopen\s*\([^)]*(?:mode\s*=\s*)?['"][wax]""", re.IGNORECASE)
```

Checks, in order (`check(code, user_requested_write=False)`):

1. `stripped = self._strip(code)` — string literals (triple first, then single/double) and `#` comments are removed.
   If nothing is left → `(False, "Empty Python code")`.
2. `DANGEROUS.search(stripped) and not user_requested_write` → `(False, "Dangerous Python operation blocked by safety policy")`.
3. `WRITE_OPEN.search(code) and not user_requested_write` → `(False, "Filesystem write blocked unless explicitly requested")`.
   Note this one runs against the **original** code, not the stripped text.
4. `"sqlalchemy.create_engine(" in stripped and "DB_CONNECTION_STRING" not in code` →
   `(False, "create_engine must use the injected DB_CONNECTION_STRING")`.
5. else `(True, None)`.

#### 12.7.2 R (`services/r_interceptor.py`)

```python
_STRING_DOUBLE = re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"')
_STRING_SINGLE = re.compile(r"'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'")
_RAW_STRING = re.compile(r'(?i)[rR]"(?:\[|\(|\{)?[\s\S]*?(?:\]|\)|\})?"')
_COMMENTS = re.compile(r"#.*?$", re.MULTILINE)

DANGEROUS = re.compile(
    r"\b("
    r"system\s*\(|system2\s*\(|shell\s*\(|"
    r"unlink\s*\(|file\.remove\s*\(|file\.rename\s*\(|"
    r"Sys\.chmod|Sys\.setFileTime|"
    r"download\.file\s*\(|install\.packages\s*\(|"
    r"eval\s*\(\s*parse\s*\(|parse\s*\(\s*text\s*="
    r")",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
WRITE_FILE = re.compile(r"\b(write\.(csv|table|dta|xlsx)|saveRDS|save\s*\(|ggsave)\s*\(", re.IGNORECASE)
```

`_strip` order: raw strings → double → single → comments. `WRITE_FILE` is tested against the **stripped** text
(unlike Python's `WRITE_OPEN`). Reasons: `"Empty R code"`, `"Dangerous R operation blocked by safety policy"`,
`"Filesystem write blocked unless explicitly requested"`.

#### 12.7.3 SAS (`services/sas_interceptor.py`)

```python
_BLOCK_COMMENT = re.compile(r"/\*[\s\S]*?\*/")
_STAR_COMMENT = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*\*.*?;")
_STRING_DOUBLE = re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"')
_STRING_SINGLE = re.compile(r"'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'")

DANGEROUS = re.compile(
    r"(?is)\b("
    r"X\s*['\"]|"
    r"CALL\s+SYSTEM|"
    r"SYSTASK|"
    r"%SYSEXEC|"
    r"FILENAME\s+\w+\s+PIPE|"
    r"\bDDE\b"
    r")"
)
WRITE_FILE = re.compile(r"(?is)\bPROC\s+EXPORT\b")
```

Reasons: `"Empty SAS code"`, `"Dangerous SAS operation blocked by safety policy"`,
`"Filesystem write blocked unless explicitly requested"`.

#### 12.7.4 SQL — `QueryInterceptor` (`services/query_interceptor.py`), applied to every embedded statement

```python
_STRINGS = re.compile(r"(N?'(?:''|[^'])*')", re.IGNORECASE)
_BLOCK_COMMENTS = re.compile(r"/\*.*?\*/", re.DOTALL)
_LINE_COMMENTS = re.compile(r"--.*?$", re.MULTILINE)

DANGEROUS = re.compile(
    r"\b(DROP|ALTER|TRUNCATE|GRANT|REVOKE|CREATE\s+LOGIN|CREATE\s+USER|EXEC(?:UTE)?\s+xp_|SHUTDOWN)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
WRITE_OPS = re.compile(r"\b(INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|MERGE|CREATE|DROP|ALTER|TRUNCATE)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
TEMP_OBJECT = re.compile(r"(#\w+|tempdb\.)", re.IGNORECASE)
```

Logic: strip block comments → line comments → string literals (in that order, replaced with `''`). Empty → `"Empty SQL"`.
`DANGEROUS` → `"Dangerous operation blocked by safety policy"`. Otherwise `WRITE_OPS` without
`user_requested_write` is allowed **only** if `TEMP_OBJECT` matches (`#temp` table or `tempdb.`); otherwise
`"Write operation blocked unless explicitly requested"`.

**Consequence for scripts:** a Python/R/SAS script that legitimately uses `CREATE TABLE #stage` in embedded SQL is
allowed, while `INSERT INTO dbo.Real` is blocked unless `is_user_code` + a write keyword in the raw query.

### 12.8 Results: `query_type`, `explanation`, failure bodies

`app/core/errors.py:54-72`:

```python
_LANGUAGE_QUERY_TYPES = {"python": "python_code", "r": "r_code", "sas": "sas_code"}

def apply_language_result(result, target_language):
    query_type = _LANGUAGE_QUERY_TYPES.get(target_language)
    if not query_type:
        return result
    if result.query_type == "database":
        result.query_type = query_type
    if not result.success and (result.sql or "").lstrip().startswith("/*"):
        if target_language == "python":
            result.sql = wrap_failure_python_comment(result.message or result.explanation or "")
        elif target_language == "r":
            result.sql = wrap_failure_r_comment(result.message or result.explanation or "")
    return result
```

* `BuiltInGenerateResult.query_type` defaults to `"database"` (`models/pipeline.py:224`) and
  `GenerateSQLResponse.query_type` likewise (`models/schemas.py:166`).
* `apply_language_result` is called only in `builtin_sql_generator.finalize()` (`:83-85`), i.e. on every result that
  leaves the script generator — including failures, whose `query_type` therefore also becomes `python_code`/`r_code`/
  `sas_code` (asserted in `tests/parity/test_builtin_python_fast_paths.py:58`).
* Conversational immediates keep `query_type == "general"` (set by `router._conversational`, `router.py:71-83`) and are
  therefore *not* rewritten (asserted at `test_builtin_python_fast_paths.py:36-43`).
* Other services use other values (`"search"`, `"plan"`, `"code_advisor"`, `"ask"`) — those never flow through the
  script generators.
* Failure comment conversion: `wrap_failure_sql_comment` produces `/*\n<msg>\n*/` with `*/` neutralised to `* /`
  (`errors.py:40-42`). For Python and R the whole block becomes `#`-comment lines
  (`wrap_failure_python_comment`, `errors.py:45-51`: empty line → `#`). For **SAS the `/* … */` block is kept
  unchanged** (valid SAS), and `query_type` still becomes `sas_code`.

Explanation defaults (`builtin_sql_generator.py:515-522`), applied in `_to_http`:

```python
explanation = result.explanation or result.message
if result.query_type == "python_code" and result.success:
    explanation = explanation or "The following Python code uses pandas to analyze your data."
elif result.query_type == "r_code" and result.success:
    explanation = explanation or "The following R code uses tidyverse to analyze your data."
elif result.query_type == "sas_code" and result.success:
    explanation = explanation or "The following SAS code may resolve your request."
```

So: `explanation` is `result.explanation` if set, else `result.message` (e.g. `"KB exact match"`, `"Precomputed exact
match"`, `"OK"`), and the generic per-language sentence is used **only** when both are falsy and the result succeeded.
On an edit turn, `code_generation_service` additionally fills `"Code updated based on your request."` when the payload
has no explanation (§12.2.1).

Typical `(success, query_type, message, explanation)` combinations for script targets:

| Flow | `success` | `query_type` | `message` | `sql` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KB exact / precomputed / KB vector exact | `True` | `python_code`… | `"KB exact match"`, `"Precomputed exact match"`, `"KB vector exact match"` | materialized script |
| Attempt loop success | `True` | `python_code`… | `"OK"` | script from the LLM |
| Timed out | `False` | `python_code`… | `"Generation timed out"` | `# Generation timed out` (Py/R) or `/* … */` (SAS) |
| Safety block | `False` | `python_code`… | e.g. `"Dangerous Python operation blocked by safety policy"` | `# …` (Py/R) / `/* … */` (SAS) |
| Hallucination loop | `False` | `python_code`… | `"Repeated Python structure detected"` | `# …` |
| No-discovery optimization, rewrite failed | `True` | `python_code`… | `"Optimization rewrite did not validate; the original editor SQL was kept."` | the materialized original |
| Conversational / off-topic / app-feature | `True` | `general` | `"General response requested."` / `"This request was classified as {intent}."` | `""` |
